issues.title: Transitional equity (PS1/26 Rules 4.1-4.10) cannot satisfy the OF 07.00 risk-weight-row checks on rows 0250 / 0261
issues.requirement: boe_b1016 / boe_b1031 (ERROR, no precondition, no EBA equivalent): on the Total sheet 0001 (and sheets 0009 / 0010, where the Bank's WARNING rules boe_b0442 / boe_b0445 expect the two rows to be empty) the RWEA in row 0250 must be at least 2.5 x the exposure value in that row, and in row 0261 at least 4 x. boe_b0491 / boe_b0506 (WARNING): on every other class sheet, including 0016 'Subordinated debt, equity and other own funds instruments', RWEA must EQUAL 2.5 x / 4 x exposure value. Their labels add: 'RWEA shall only exceed 250% [400%] of exposure value if an Equities Transitional Approach is being applied' - which suggests (an inference from the word 'exceed' and the WARNING severity) that the Bank anticipated the transitional approach only in the upward (IRB higher-of) direction. No rule reads the memorandum rows 0371-0374 except non-negativity checks and boe_b0710_2.

authority.locator: OF 07.00 rows 0140-0280 'Breakdown of exposures by risk weights'
authority.quote: Equity exposures (including higher risk equity exposures) in the exposure class ‘subordinated debt, equity and other own funds instruments’ subject to the transitional provisions in Rules 4.1 to 4.10 of the Credit Risk General Provisions (CRR) Part shall be reported against the risk weights set out in Article 133 of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part disregarding the transitional provisions. However, the RWEA shall still reflect the transitional provisions.

Exposures subject to rules 4.1 to 4.10 of the Credit Risk: General Provisions Part should be reported in this row during the transitional period if they qualify as an equity exposure as set out in Article 133(1) and (2) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.

Exposures subject to rules 4.1 to 4.10 of the Credit Risk: General Provisions Part should be reported in this row during the transitional period if they qualify as a higher risk equity exposure as set out in the Glossary Part.

authority.locator: para 47 (scope of OF CR SA: the Total sheet)
authority.quote: The information in OF CR SA is required for the total exposure across all exposure classes and individually for each of the exposure classes under the Standardised Approach. The total figures as well as the information of each exposure class shall be reported in a separate dimension.

Firms shall only report the memorandum items in rows 0371 and 0372 for exposures that are subject to the Rules 4.1 to 4.3 of the Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part. The reporting of these memorandum items in rows 0371 and 0372 shall not affect the calculation of the risk-weighted exposure amount of the exposure class referred to in Article 112(1)(p) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part reported in template OF CR SA.

authority.locator: para 55C (IRB Transitional Approach is reported inside class (p) of OF CR SA)
authority.quote: (which shall include exposures subject to the IRB Transitional Approach described in Rules 4.4 to 4.8 of the Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part).

The memorandum items in rows 0371-0374 provide additional information on the transitional provisions for the treatment of equity exposures as stated in Rules 4.1 to 4.10 of the Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part.
Institutions shall report all equity exposures to which the Standardised Transitional Approach for equities applies in these rows.
The reporting of the memorandum items in rows 0371 to 0374 shall not affect their reporting in rows 0250 and 0261.

authority.locator: OF 07.00 rows 0140-0280 (the parallel instruction the '>=' rules were written for)
authority.quote: Exposures subject to the currency mismatch multiplier (Article 123B of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part) shall be reported against the risk weight which would have applied if the currency mismatch multiplier was not applied. However, the RWEA shall still reflect the currency mismatch multiplier.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part, Rule 4.1
authority.quote: 4.2 and 4.3 only apply to an institution that did not have permission to use the Internal Ratings Based Approach under Article 143 of CRR on 31 December 2026.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part, Rule 4.2
authority.quote: This rule modifies paragraph 3 of Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 133 for a transitional period beginning with 1 January 2027 and ending with 31 December 2029, in which equity exposures that are not higher risk equity exposures or within the scope of paragraph 6 of Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 133 shall be assigned the following risk weights: (1) 160% during the period beginning with 1 January 2027 and ending with 31 December 2027; (2) 190% during the period beginning with 1 January 2028 and ending with 31 December 2028; and (3) 220% during the period beginning with 1 January 2029 and ending with 31 December 2029.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part, Rule 4.3
authority.quote: This rule modifies paragraph 4 of Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 133 for a transitional period between 1 January 2027 and 31 December 2029, in which equity exposures that are higher risk equity exposures and are not within scope of paragraph 6 of Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 133 shall be assigned the following risk weights: (1) 220% during the period beginning with 1 January 2027 and ending with 31 December 2027; (2) 280% during the period beginning with 1 January 2028 and ending with 31 December 2028; and (3) 340% during the period beginning with 1 January 2029 and ending with 31 December 2029.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part, Rule 4.6 (IRB Transitional Approach)
authority.quote: Subject to 4.9, an institution shall calculate the risk weight for each equity exposure as the higher of: (1) the risk weight calculated using the relevant methodology used by the institution as specified in its permission to use the Internal Ratings Based Approach under Article 155 of CRR as that provision was in force on 31 December 2026; and (2) the risk weight calculated under 4.2 or 4.3.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 133(3)
authority.quote: An equity exposure shall be assigned a risk weight of 250%, unless the exposure is a higher risk equity exposure, in which case the treatment in paragraph 4 applies, or is within scope of paragraph 6, in which case the treatment referred to in paragraph 6 applies.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 133(4)
authority.quote: A higher risk equity exposure shall be assigned a risk weight of 400%, unless the exposure is within the scope of paragraph 6, in which case the treatment referred to in paragraph 6 applies.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Annex II p.95 fixes both halves: the ROW is the Article 133 weight 'disregarding the transitional provisions' (row 0250 or 0261), and the RWEA 'shall still reflect the transitional provisions'. So for equity under Rule 4.2 the firm reports exposure value T in row 0250 with RWEA = w x T where w = 1.6 (2027), 1.9 (2028), 2.2 (2029); under Rule 4.3, row 0261 with w = 2.2 / 2.8 / 3.4. Every w is below the row weight. Row 0250 c0220 on the Total sheet is therefore 2.5 x E - (2.5 - w) x T, which is < 2.5 x E whenever T > 0 (E = everything in the row). It fails whenever the transitional shortfall exceeds any excess over 250% carried by other items in row 0250, which is always the case where row 0250 holds only class (p) equity and items at exactly 250% (Art. 133(6)(c) / Art. 48(4)); no rule closes rows 0250 / 0261 on sheets 0015 (CIU) or 0017 (other items), and Annex II does not say how the 1.2 factor Article 132(4) applies to CIU RWEA is rowed. And the multipliers the '>=' form was written for (currency mismatch, p.94) apply to retail and residential real estate, where the WARNING rules boe_b0442 / boe_b0445 expect rows 0250 / 0261 to be empty. Para 47 (p.77) puts the equity on the Total sheet, boe_b0713 (ERROR) forces Total r0010 = sum of class sheets and the WARNING rule boe_b0719 expects the RWEA on a risk-weight row of the Total sheet. Numbers (2027): 1,000,000 listed equity -> RWEA 1,600,000 < 2,500,000 (boe_b1016 fails; boe_b0491 fails on sheet 0016); 500,000 higher-risk equity -> RWEA 1,100,000 < 2,000,000 (boe_b1031 fails; boe_b0506 fails). The rounding allowance is immaterial (about 1.75 currency units at decimals=0 against a shortfall of 0.9 x T). The '>=' design handles 'report against the unadjusted weight, RWEA reflects the adjustment' only when the adjustment raises RWEA; the Standardised Transitional Approach is the one such instruction that lowers it. Sub-questions tested: (a) row 0250 c0220 IS the transitional RWEA (p.95, verbatim); (b) the Total sheet carries the equity (para 47; boe_b0713); (c) no other compliant row exists - there is no 160/190/220/280/340% row, p.95 names the Article 133 row, and boe_b0458 forbids row 0280 on sheet 0016; (d) rows 0371-0374 (table OF07.00.01.04, sheet 0016 only, with c0200 and c0220) are information-only memorandum rows that no rule nets off today, but a rule could (see proposed fix); (e) IRB-transitional equity (Rule 4.6, weight = max(legacy IRB weight, 4.2/4.3 weight)) can fail too - a limb less well founded than the standardised one, resting on Rule 4.6(2)'s cross-reference to Rule 4.3 and on memorandum row 0373, not on Rule 4.4, which derogates from Article 133(3) only: boe_b1031 whenever the legacy weight is below 400%, boe_b1016 whenever the blended weight in row 0250 is below 250%, and boe_b0491 / boe_b0506 whenever it is not exactly 250% / 400%.

example.description: A firm with no IRB permission on 31 December 2026, reference date 31 March 2027, all positions on-balance-sheet, unrated, no CRM or provisions (c0010 = c0040 = c0110 = c0150 = c0200). (1) Listed equity 1,000,000: Rule 4.2(1) 160% -> RWEA 1,600,000, reported in row 0250 of sheet 0016 and of the Total sheet 0001 (Annex II p.95-96), and in memorandum row 0372 of OF07.00.01.04. (2) Higher-risk equity 500,000: Rule 4.3(1) 220% -> RWEA 1,100,000, row 0261 on both sheets and memorandum row 0371. (3) Control legs: subordinated debt 200,000 at 150% (Art. 133(5)) -> RWEA 300,000 in row 0240 of sheets 0016 and 0001; an unrated corporate loan 2,000,000 at 100% -> row 0230 of sheets 0008 and 0001. Rows 0010 and 0070 carry the totals on each sheet (Total: exposure value 3,700,000, RWEA 5,000,000); c0235 (RWEA without an ECAI assessment) = c0220, although Annex II p.87 gives columns 0230/0235 the legal reference Article 112(1)(a-d, f, g, l, o, q), which omits class (p): without it the four rules give the same verdicts, and boe_b0703 (WARNING) fails. 97 facts, no structure findings, Arelle completed with no errors.

issues.alternatives_considered: None is Annex-II-compliant and passes. (1) Row 0280 'Other risk weights' on both sheets: the four rules do not evaluate, but boe_b0458 fails [0,5] on sheet 0016 and it contradicts p.95 ('reported against the risk weights set out in Article 133 ... disregarding the transitional provisions'). (2) Rows 0250 / 0261 on sheet 0016 but row 0280 on the Total sheet only: avoids boe_b1016 / boe_b1031 (not evaluated; boe_b0713 [3,0]; boe_b0719 [12,0] with c0235 populated on row 0280) because no rule ties Total r0250 / r0261 to the class sheets - though across all 213 OF 07.00 rules the same return still fails boe_b0710 and boe_b0710_2 (ERROR), for the unrelated PI-15a; boe_b0491 / boe_b0506 still fail [0,1] as WARNINGs. It is a gateway workaround, not compliant reporting: the Total sheet's risk-weight breakdown stops being the total across classes (para 47) and p.95 applies to the Total sheet too. (3) The row of the actual weight: no 160 / 190 / 220 / 280 / 340% row exists. (4) Reporting RWEA at 2.5x / 4x in rows 0250 / 0261 (numerically the control return B): passes, but p.95 says 'the RWEA shall still reflect the transitional provisions' and it overstates RWEA against Rules 4.2 / 4.3. (5) Leaving out the memorandum rows changes nothing: none of the four rules reads them. (6) No precondition, filing indicator, grey cell or default helps: the rules have no precondition, every cell involved is reportable, and Arelle evaluates them at a 2027 reference date. No opt-out was found for a firm without IRB permission in Rules 4.1-4.10 (Rule 4.9 replaces only 4.5, 4.6 and 4.8).
issues.proposed_fix: Preferred (keeps the check, uses the memorandum rows the template already collects). boe_b1016, scope reduced to sheet 0001: {t: OF07.00.01.01, r: 0250, c: 0220, z: 0001, dv: 0} i- {t: OF07.00.01.04, r: 0372, c: 0220, z: 0016, dv: 0} i- {t: OF07.00.01.04, r: 0374, c: 0220, z: 0016, dv: 0} i>= ({t: OF07.00.01.01, r: 0250, c: 0200, z: 0001, dv: 0} i- {t: OF07.00.01.04, r: 0372, c: 0200, z: 0016, dv: 0} i- {t: OF07.00.01.04, r: 0374, c: 0200, z: 0016, dv: 0}) i* 2.5. boe_b1031: the same with row 0261, memorandum rows 0371 and 0373, factor 4. boe_b0491 / boe_b0506: remove sheet 0016 from the scope and add a sheet-0016 twin with 'i=' netted off the same way (rows 0372 + 0374, and 0371 + 0373). This fix needs boe_b0710_2 corrected at the same time, because on-balance-sheet equity in rows 0371-0374 fails it today. It also assumes rows 0371-0374 are a subset of sheet 0016 rows 0250 / 0261, which Annex II does not settle: para 55C (p.79) speaks of exposures subject to Rules 4.4 to 4.8 (4.7 and 4.8 are CIU underlyings, which para 63 puts on the CIU sheet), the row instructions (p.98) of Rules 4.4 to 4.6. Simpler alternatives, of which (a) has neither dependency and is the safer first recommendation: (a) for reference dates up to 31 December 2029 lower the bounds to the smallest transitional weight - row 0250 c0220 >= c0200 x 1.6 and row 0261 c0220 >= c0200 x 2.2 - which holds for both transitional approaches in all three years; or (b) deactivate boe_b1016 and boe_b1031, or downgrade them to WARNING as was done for boe_b0491 / boe_b0506, until 1 January 2030. In every case correct the boe_b0491 / boe_b0506 labels: under the Standardised Transitional Approach RWEA is BELOW 250% / 400% of exposure value, not above.
issues.eba_precedent: No EBA rule or Q&A settles this (the EBA Q&A site was not searched). boe_b0491 restates EBA v0327_m (C 07.00 r0250: c0215 = c0200 x 250%, ERROR, live); the Bank downgraded it to WARNING and added the transitional caveat to its label, which shows the transitional case was recognised for the class-sheet equalities but in the upward direction only. boe_b1016 and boe_b1031 have no EBA equivalent (new Bank rules for the sheets where risk-weight multipliers apply). The v4.0.0 extract maps boe_b0506 to v0328_m, which in the EBA list is the 1250% row rule - a cosmetic mislabel.
issues.reach: Reference dates 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2029. ERROR (boe_b1016 / boe_b1031, Total sheet): a firm with equity subject to Rule 4.2 or 4.3 whose rows 0250 / 0261 hold nothing weighted above 250% / 400% to offset the shortfall - firms without IRB permission on 31 December 2026, and IRB firms for equity that was under the Standardised Approach on that date (Rule 4.5(1)) - unless the firm elected Rule 4.9. IRB-transitional equity (Rule 4.6): boe_b1031 fails whenever the legacy weight is below 400%, boe_b1016 whenever the blended weight in row 0250 is below 250%. WARNING (boe_b0491 / boe_b0506, sheet 0016): the same firms, plus IRB-transitional equity above 250%. Not affected: subordinated debt (150%, row 0240) and Article 133(6) items. The same four rule ids are enforced in PRA116 on SC07.00.01.01 (not tested here).
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b1053, boe_b1054, boe_b1055: OF 09.02 row 0055 is compared with OF 08.01 sheets 0011 and 0012 one at a time, not with their sum
issues.requirement: OF 09.02 row 0055 (other general corporates non-SME) on the all-countries sheet (CEG = eba_GA:x1), column 0010 / 0105 / 0110, must equal OF 08.01 row 0010 column 0020 / 0110 / 0260 on sheet 0011 (AIRB) and, as a separate evaluation, on sheet 0012 (FIRB). The Bank's formula file confirms it: in vr-boe_b1055.xml the OF 08.01 variable $v1 has bindAsSequence=false, fallbackValue=0 and its own covering filter APR in {eba_AP:x66, eba_AP:x67}; the test is iaf:numeric-equal($v0,$v1). vr-boe_b0288.xml (the SME twin, sheets 0023;0024) has the same filters but bindAsSequence=true, fallbackValue=() and the test iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:sum($v1)). The labels of all three rules say the right-hand side is the total 'across approaches (FIRB and AIRB)'. The expression and label text were read from the Bank's own workbook (sheet banking_reporting) and match the packaged rule book.

authority.quote: Other corporate exposures as referred to in Article 147(4E) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part not reported in 0042-0050.
All institutions shall submit information aggregated at a total level.
Same definition as for column 0020 of OF CR IRB 1 template.
In OF CR IRB 1, "FIRB/slotting" in cases where the FIRB approach or the slotting approach is applied, and "AIRB" in cases where the AIRB approach is applied.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 147A(1)(f)
authority.quote: (ii)  the Advanced IRB Approach for exposures where permission has been granted under Article 143(2A) or (2B) to use the Advanced IRB Approach; (iii) the Foundation IRB Approach for all other exposures within that exposure subclass;

An institution which has been granted permission by the PRA to use the Advanced IRB Approach in the calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts and expected loss amounts for one or more type of exposures within the non-Retail AIRB Modelling roll-out category may, with the prior permission of the PRA, apply the Foundation IRB Approach for a given type of exposures in that category if it can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the PRA that the requirement in point (b) is met;
1.1.2.1.06 06 Corporates – Other general corporates non-SME See CR IRB templates
1.1.2.2.03 Corporates – Other general corporates non-SME See CR IRB templates

In cases where an institution uses the AIRB approach for a part of its IRB exposures and the FIRB or slotting approach to calculate risk-weighted exposure amounts for the other part of its IRB exposures, one OF CR IRB Total for exposures subject to the FIRB approach or the slotting approach and one OF CR IRB Total for exposures subject to the AIRB approach shall be reported.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Let A be the sheet 0011 (AIRB) figure and F the sheet 0012 (FIRB) figure. For a firm without corporate purchased receivables, Annex II makes row 0055 the whole non-SME other-general-corporate population, so row 0055 = A + F. The rule asks row 0055 = A and, separately, row 0055 = F. Both hold only if A = F = row 0055, which with row 0055 = A + F means A = F = 0. Measured in Arelle 2.47.5 on the Bank's v4.1.1 package (counts are [satisfied, unsatisfied], the same for b1053, b1054 and b1055 unless stated): both sheets with figures and row 0055 = A + F: [0,2]. Only sheet 0011 reported: [1,0]. Only sheet 0012 reported: [1,0]. Sheet 0011 with figures and sheet 0012 reported as explicit zeros: [1,1], because a reported zero is a fact and binds. Both sheets, row 0055 left empty: [0,2]. A second route reaches b1055 only: OF 02.00 r0356 c0010 is the same data point as OF 08.01 sheet 0011 r0010 c0260 (data point 7883 in the taxonomy pack) and OF 02.00 r0297 c0010 is the same data point as sheet 0012 r0010 c0260 (7875). A FIRB-only firm that reports 0 in OF 02.00 row 0356 has therefore reported the AIRB sheet's total as 0: Arelle gives b1055 [1,1] with b1053 and b1054 [1,0]; the mirror case (AIRB only, OF 02.00 r0297 = 0) is also b1055 [1,1]. So the result of b1055 depends on whether a firm writes 0 or leaves the cell empty for an approach it does not use.

example.description: A firm that applies AIRB to part of its other general non-SME corporate book and FIRB to the rest (PS1/26 Art. 147A(1)(f); allowed during roll-out under Art. 148(1A) or permanently under Art. 150(4)). OF 08.01 sheet 0011 row 0010: original exposure 1,000, exposure value 800, RWEA 500. Sheet 0012 row 0010: 600 / 450 / 400. OF 09.02 all-countries row 0055: c0010 = 1,600, c0105 = 1,250, c0110 = 900. Controls in the same return: SME sheets 0023 (300 / 250 / 150) and 0024 (200 / 180 / 120) with OF 09.02 row 0050 = 500 / 430 / 270, and row 0030 = 2,100 / 1,680 / 1,170.

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) Set row 0055 to one sheet's figure (row 0030 lowered with it so boe_b0785 still holds): b1053-b1055 [1,1] and boe_b0282, b0283, b0284 [0,1] each. (2) Leave row 0055 empty: [0,2], and boe_b0785 then fails as well [0,3], because row 0030 no longer equals its breakdown. (3) Equal figures on both sheets with row 0055 equal to one of them: b1053-b1055 pass [2,0], but row 0055 is then half the true figure and boe_b0282-b0284 fail [0,1]. (4) Put both approaches on one sheet: not allowed, Annex II para 75 has each class reported under the approach applied. (5) Leave one sheet out: correct only when that approach has no exposures, and then the rule passes anyway. (6) No precondition or greyed cell helps: every cell is reportable and paragraph 85 has every institution file the all-countries sheet. None of these lets a correct return with both approaches pass. The only escape is for a single-approach firm: leave the unused sheet, and OF 02.00 row 0356 or 0297, empty instead of 0.
issues.proposed_fix: Make the OF 08.01 reference a sum over the two sheets, exactly as in boe_b0288-b0290. One limitation: row 0055 is 'not reported in 0042-0050' (Annex II p.144) and row 0049 holds purchased receivables (p.143), while OF 08.01 row 0175 (purchased receivables of the classes in Article 147(2)(c) or (d), p.117) is reportable on sheets 0011 and 0012, so their totals include them: the summed rule would still fail a firm with non-SME corporate purchased receivables unless they are taken off. boe_b1053: {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0055, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], seq: False, id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0020, z: 0011; 0012, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}). boe_b1054: the same with c: 0105 on the left and c: 0110 on the right. boe_b1055: the same with c: 0110 on the left and c: 0260 on the right. In the formula files this is bindAsSequence="true" and fallbackValue="()" on $v1 and test="iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:sum($v1))", as in vr-boe_b0288.xml. Also correct the label of boe_b1055, whose left-hand side reads 'Corporates (Other General SME)' for the non-SME row.
issues.eba_precedent: None recorded for boe_b1053-b1055: the v4.0.0 rule list gives them no EBA equivalent. The SME twin boe_b0288 restates EBA v0435_m, whose formula sums the two approach sheets: "{C 09.02, r0050, c0010, [CEG=eba_GA:x1]} = sum({C 08.01.a, r0010, c0020, (s0007-0008)})".
issues.reach: From the first PRA001 v4.1.1 return (valid from 1 January 2027), ERROR severity. (a) Any IRB firm with other general non-SME corporates under both AIRB and FIRB: all three rules fail. (b) Any firm on one approach that reports the other sheet's row 0010 as zeros: all three fail. (c) Any firm on one approach that reports 0 in OF 02.00 r0356 c0010 (AIRB) or r0297 c0010 (FIRB): boe_b1055 fails.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0823, boe_b0829: OF 08.06 total row is compared per type of specialised lending with the all-types OF 08.01 figure
issues.requirement: boe_b0823: OF 08.06 row 0095 (Total) column 0090 (expected loss amount) must equal the sum of OF 08.01 r0080 c0280 over sheets 0002 and 0010, divided by 2. boe_b0829: the same for OF 08.06 c0100 against OF 08.01 c0290. In vr-boe_b0823.xml the OF 08.06 variable $v0 has bindAsSequence=false, fallbackValue=0 and its own covering filter TSL in {eba_TA:x0, boe_eba_TA:x10001, boe_eba_TA:x10002, eba_TA:x129, eba_TA:x131, eba_TA:x132}; the test is iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:numeric-divide(sum($v1),2)). So the rule is evaluated once for each OF 08.06 sheet that carries the fact, each time against the all-types OF 08.01 figure. vr-boe_b0822.xml has the same filters with $v0 bindAsSequence=true and iaf:sum($v0). Both labels say 'across all the types of specialised lending'.

authority.quote: Institutions shall report information on the following types of specialised lending exposures referred to in Table A of Article 153(5) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part: (a) Object finance exposures; (b) Project finance exposures; (c) Commodities finance exposures (d) IPRE exposures; and (e) HVCRE exposures.
(-) VALUE ADJUSTMENTS AND PROVISIONS See OFCR IRB 1 instructions for column 0290.
EXPECTED LOSS AMOUNT See OFCR IRB 1 instructions for column 0282.
1.1.2.3.01 Project finance exposures See CR IRB 6 template ... 1.1.2.3.04 Income Producing Real Estate (IPRE) exposures See CR IRB 6 template

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 147A(1)(c)
authority.quote: for point (c)(i) of Article 147(2) (specialised lending) for IPRE exposures and HVCRE exposures: (i) the Standardised Approach for exposures where permission has been granted under Article 148 or Article 150; or (ii) the Slotting Approach for all other IPRE exposures and HVCRE exposures;

issues.why_correct_return_fails: With two types reporting expected loss e1 and e2, OF 08.01 r0080 c0280 is e1 + e2 on both sheets, so the rule asks e1 = e1 + e2 on the first type's sheet and e2 = e1 + e2 on the second. Both fail unless one type has no fact in the cell. The same holds for provisions in boe_b0829. Arelle on a project finance + IPRE return: boe_b0823 [0,2], boe_b0829 [0,2]. How this differs from the claim as first written. (1) The claim says the type axis 'has no total member'. That is wrong and must not go to the Bank in those words. The axis hierarchy includes eba_TA:x0 'Not applicable/All activities', which is the dimension default; Arelle accepts an OF 08.06 sheet with no TSL member without error and boe_b0823 / b0829 pass on it. It does not rescue a two-type firm: Annex II paragraph 82 asks for the five types; with the all-types sheet filed beside the type sheets the type sheets still fail (b0823 and b0829 [1,2]) and boe_b0816, b0817, b0819, b0822, which sum x0 together with the five types, double count ([0,1] each); with the all-types sheet alone, boe_b0632 and b0635 (OF 02.00 rows 0412 / 0415 against each type's OF 08.06 total) fail [0,1] each. (2) The failing condition is narrower than 'two types of exposure': two or more type sheets must carry a fact in r0095 c0090 (or c0100), and at least one of them must be non-zero: two type sheets reporting 0 and 0 pass. A second type with explicit zero expected loss and provisions gives [1,1]; a second type that leaves those cells empty gives [1,0]. (3) The label point is confirmed: boe_b0829's label, in the Bank's own workbook, reads 'Total Specialised Lending Original exposure pre-conversion factors (Slotting approach) across all the types of specialised lending shall be consistent', but the rule compares OF 08.06 c0100 with OF 08.01 c0290, both '(-) Value adjustments and provisions'. Original exposure is boe_b0816.

example.description: A firm with two types of slotting exposure. Project finance (TSL x129), all in 'Good / other' (row 0055; 90% risk weight, 0.8% expected loss per Art. 153(5) Table A and Art. 158(6) Table B): original exposure 1,000, exposure after CRM substitution 1,000, exposure value 1,000, RWEA 900, expected loss 8, provisions -5. IPRE (TSL x10001), all in 'Satisfactory' (row 0065; 115%, 2.8%): 2,000 / 2,000 / 2,000 / 2,300 / 56 / -20. Each type's row 0095 repeats its category row. OF 08.01 r0080 on sheets 0002 and 0010: c0020 3,000, c0090 3,000, c0110 3,000, c0260 3,200, c0280 64, c0282 64, c0290 -25. OF 02.00 r0412 = 900, r0415 = 2,300.

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) File an all-types OF 08.06 sheet (no TSL member) beside the two type sheets, with its own category rows: boe_b0823 and b0829 [1,2] (the all-types sheet passes, each type sheet fails); boe_b0816, b0817, b0819, b0822 [0,1] each (double count); boe_b0815 [18,0]. (2) File the all-types sheet only: boe_b0823, b0829 and b0816-b0822 pass, but boe_b0632 and b0635 fail [0,1] each, and Annex II paragraph 82 asks for the types. (3) Report zero expected loss and provisions for the second type: [1,1]. (4) Leave the second type's expected loss and provisions cells empty: [1,0] for both rules, but the type then reports no expected loss, which is not what Annex II asks unless the amount really is nil. (5) No greyed cell, precondition or default helps: r0095 c0090 and c0100 are reportable on every sheet and $v0 falls back to 0. No compliant way of reporting two types with expected loss or provisions satisfies both rules.
issues.proposed_fix: Sum the OF 08.06 side over the type sheets, as boe_b0822 does. boe_b0823: isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, r: 0095, c: 0090, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v0}) i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0280, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}) i/ 2 - the minimal fix, keeping column 0280; if the Bank agrees with PI-03b, c0282 in place of c0280. boe_b0829: isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, r: 0095, c: 0100, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v0}) i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0290, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}) i/ 2. In the formula files: bindAsSequence="true" and fallbackValue="()" on $v0, and iaf:sum($v0) in the test, as in vr-boe_b0822.xml. Correct boe_b0829's label to name '(-) Value adjustments and provisions'. Also say whether an all-types OF 08.06 sheet (TSL = eba_TA:x0, the dimension default) may be filed. If not, take x0 out of the summed variable's member list in boe_b0816-b0823, b0829 and b1043 (or make it unusable on the table). If it may, those rules should read the x0 sheet alone and not add it to the five types.
issues.eba_precedent: The v4.0.0 rule list maps boe_b0823 to EBA v09794_m and boe_b0829 to v09795_m. v09794_m: "sum({C 08.06, r0110, c0090, (sNNN)}) + sum({C 08.06, r0120, c0090, (sNNN)}) = sum({C 08.01.a, r0080, c0280, (sNNN)})"; v09795_m is the same for c0100 against c0290. Both sum the C 08.06 side over all sheets, both are WARNING, and both were deactivated by the EBA on 2021-06-10 and not reactivated. The Bank's versions are ERROR and do not sum.
issues.reach: ERROR severity, from the first PRA001 v4.1.1 return. Every IRB firm with slotting exposures that reports expected loss or provisions on two or more of the five type sheets, at least one of them non-zero. That is the normal case for a firm with commercial property lending: Art. 147A(1)(c) puts both IPRE and HVCRE on the slotting approach.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0823 ties OF 08.06 expected loss to OF 08.01 column 0280 (before post-model adjustments); Annex II defines it by column 0282 (after)
issues.requirement: OF 08.06 row 0095 column 0090 (expected loss amount) must equal OF 08.01 row 0080 column 0280 (sum over sheets 0002 and 0010, divided by 2). Column 0280 is 'Expected loss amount pre post-model adjustments'. boe_b0743 separately requires, on row 0080 among others, c0282 = c0280 + c0281, so the taxonomy provides for a post-model adjustment to expected loss on the slotting row.

authority.quote: EXPECTED LOSS AMOUNT See OFCR IRB 1 instructions for column 0282.

EXPECTED LOSS AMOUNT AFTER POST-MODEL ADJUSTMENTS The expected loss amount calculated in accordance with Article 158 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. Post-model adjustments as determined in in Article 158(6A) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part shall be taken into account.
Adjustments referred to in Article 158(6A) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part shall not be taken into account.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 158(6)
authority.quote: Subject to paragraph 6A, where an institution has assigned a risk weight to a specialised lending exposure under the Slotting Approach, the institution shall calculate an expected loss amount in accordance with the formula in paragraph 5.

An institution shall increase the total expected loss amounts calculated under paragraphs 5 and 6 to reflect any post model adjustments in respect of expected loss amounts calculated under point (c) of Article 146(3).

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Annex II defines OF 08.06 c0090 by the instruction for OF 08.01 column 0282, the amount after post-model adjustments. The rule compares it with column 0280, the amount before them. For a firm with a post-model adjustment P > 0 on its slotting expected loss (Art. 158(6A) applies to the slotting amounts of paragraph 6), OF 08.06 c0090 = EL + P while OF 08.01 r0080 c0280 = EL, so the rule fails even with a single type of specialised lending. Arelle: boe_b0823 [0,1] on a one-type return with EL 8 and adjustment 2 (OF 08.06 c0090 = 10; OF 08.01 r0080 c0280 = 8, c0281 = 2, c0282 = 10), while boe_b0743 holds [2,0] and boe_b0829 passes [1,0]. This is independent of the per-type defect in PI-03a. The likely origin is the EBA rule v09794_m, written when C 08.01 had one expected loss column (0280); the Bank split the column into 0280 / 0281 / 0282 and Annex II points OF 08.06 at 0282, but the rule kept 0280.

example.description: A firm with project finance slotting exposures only (TSL x129), all 'Good / other' (row 0055): original exposure 1,000, exposure after CRM substitution 1,000, exposure value 1,000, RWEA 900, provisions -5. Expected loss from Table B is 8 and the firm carries a post-model adjustment of 2. OF 08.06 r0055 and r0095 c0090 = 10 (after the adjustment, as Annex II directs). OF 08.01 r0080 on sheets 0002 and 0010: c0280 = 8, c0281 = 2, c0282 = 10, c0290 = -5, c0260 = 900. OF 02.00 r0412 = 900.

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) Report OF 08.06 c0090 before the adjustment so that it equals c0280: satisfies the rule but contradicts the Annex II cross-reference to column 0282. (2) Leave OF 08.01 r0080 c0281 empty and put the adjusted amount in c0280: contradicts the column 0280 instruction ('shall not be taken into account'). (3) No other rule ties OF 08.06 c0090 to OF 08.01 c0282; boe_b0823 is the only cross-template rule on that column. Rule and instruction cannot both be met when the adjustment is non-zero. If the Bank's intention is the pre-adjustment amount, the fix is to the Annex II cross-reference and not to the rule; either way the two disagree.
issues.proposed_fix: In boe_b0823 read OF 08.01 column 0282 instead of 0280. Combined with the PI-03a change: isum({t: OF08.06.01.01, r: 0095, c: 0090, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v0}) i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0282, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}) i/ 2. Alternatively, if the pre-adjustment amount is what OF 08.06 should show, change the Annex II instruction for OF 08.06 column 0090 to refer to column 0280.
issues.eba_precedent: EBA v09794_m: "sum({C 08.06, r0110, c0090, (sNNN)}) + sum({C 08.06, r0120, c0090, (sNNN)}) = sum({C 08.01.a, r0080, c0280, (sNNN)})", WARNING, deactivated 2021-06-10. C 08.01 has a single expected loss column (0280); the split into 0280 / 0281 / 0282 is the Bank's.
issues.reach: ERROR severity. Any IRB firm that carries a post-model adjustment to expected loss on slotting exposures (Art. 146(3)(c), Art. 158(6A)), whatever its number of types. Firms without such an adjustment are unaffected by this point.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0380 / boe_b0395: expected loss is capped at an original exposure that stays with the obligor when a guarantee moves the covered part to the guarantor's class and grade

publisher_log.statement: The validation rule boe_b0746 verifies that c:0090 is equal to the sum of c0020 + c0035 + c0070 + c0080. The formula doesn't behave as expected for {r:0017, c:0035} and {r:0020, c:0035} in sheet 0019 because these cells are incorrectly greyed-out. Solution: The validation boe_b0746 has been deactivated

issues.requirement: On every in-scope row of every OF 08.01 sheet, and on every obligor-grade row of every OF 08.02 sheet, expected loss before post-model adjustments (col 0280) must not exceed original exposure pre-conversion factors (col 0020). Both operands default to 0, so a row with expected loss and no original exposure fails. No precondition beyond the table's filing indicator.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 cols 0070-0080
authority.quote: Outflows shall correspond to the covered part of the original exposure pre-conversion factors that is deducted from the obligor's exposure class and, where relevant, obligor grade or pool, and subsequently assigned to the guarantor's exposure class and, where relevant, obligor grade or pool. That amount shall be considered as an inflow into the guarantor's exposure class and, where relevant, obligor grades or pools.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 col 0090
authority.quote: Exposures assigned in the corresponding obligor grade or pool and exposure class after taking into account outflows and inflows due to CRM techniques with substitution effects on the exposure.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 col 0280
authority.quote: For the definition of Expected Loss, see Article 5(3) CRR and, for the calculation of expected loss amounts, see Article 158 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part.

authority.locator: PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 158(1)
authority.quote: An institution using the Foundation IRB Approach or Advanced IRB Approach shall, unless otherwise stated in this Article, calculate expected loss amounts based on the same input figures of PD, LGD and the exposure value for each exposure as are used for the calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts in accordance with Article 151.

authority.locator: PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk Mitigation (CRR) Part, Article 236(1A)(b) (Parameter Substitution Method; 'eg' and 'rg' are subscripted symbols in the PDF)
authority.quote: The expected loss for the covered part, eg, shall be PD ∙LGD, where PD and LGD are as defined for the purposes of calculating rg in point (a) of paragraph 1.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 col 0300 (the column the instructions single out as NOT following the redistribution)
authority.quote: As this column deals with an element of the structure of the rating scales, it relates to the original exposures pre-conversion factor assigned to each obligor grade or pool without taking into account the effect of CRM techniques (in particular redistribution effects).

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 col 0310 (the other carve-out)
authority.quote: The amounts shall be presented in the exposure classes relevant for the exposures to the original obligor.

41. The exposure type shall not change because of unfunded credit protection. 42. If an exposure is secured by an unfunded credit protection, the secured part shall be assigned as an outflow e.g. in the exposure class of the obligor and as an inflow in the exposure class of the guarantor. However, the type of the exposure shall not change due to the change of the exposure class.

authority.locator: final answer published 08/12/2017 (precedent on the identical EBA columns; fetched from eba.europa.eu on 16 Nov 2026, saved at <scratch>/dl/qa3509.html)
authority.quote: In that regard, the interdependency between columns 020 (original exposure) and 280 (Expected Loss Amount) of templates C 08.01 / C 08.02 as established by validation rules v4772_m for C 08.02 and v4757_m for C 08.01 does not exist, considering that CRM techniques with substitution effect can lead to a reassignment of parts of an exposure to a different exposure class. Both validation rules will therefore be amended.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 158(5)
authority.quote: Expected loss amount = EL ∙exposure value

shall take into account all forms of credit risk mitigation techniques that are eligible according to Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 (CRR) and actually applied by the institution, such as credit risk mitigation techniques with substitution effects

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Col 0020 is pre-CRM and stays in the obligor's class and grade. Under the Parameter Substitution Method the covered part leaves as an outflow (col 0070) and arrives as an inflow (col 0080) in the guarantor's class and grade, where it carries its exposure value (0110), RWEA (0260) and - because Art. 158(1) computes EL from the same PD, LGD and exposure value as the RWEA, and Art. 236(1A)(b) gives the covered part an EL of guarantor-PD x LGD - its expected loss (0280). On any row that receives an inflow but holds no original exposure of its own, col 0280 > 0 = col 0020, so abs(0280) <= abs(0020) is false. Such rows are ordinary: a guarantor's obligor grade in OF 08.02 with no direct obligor in it; the off-balance-sheet rows (0030 and the conversion-factor bucket rows 0031-0035/0001) of a guarantor class that has only on-balance-sheet direct exposures, since paragraph 41 keeps a guaranteed commitment off-balance-sheet; or a whole class sheet reached only through guarantees (a parent-company guarantee from a large corporate). The Bank's own boe_b0746 / boe_b0760 (col 0090 = 0020 + 0035 + 0070 + 0080) are satisfied on the same rows, i.e. the rule set itself expects exposure to arrive on rows with no col 0020 (boe_b0746 has since been deactivated at the gateway, for an unrelated reason: known issues log #26). A counter-reading is open to the Bank: Article 236(1)(c) and (1A)(c) (PS1/26 Appendix 1 pp.216-217) define the risk weight and expected loss 'that shall apply to such exposure in its entirety' as a blend, which could be read as keeping the exposure whole with the obligor; but Annex II columns 0070-0080 (p.104) require the split for both the Risk-Weight and the Parameter Substitution Methods.

example.description: A FIRB firm lends 10,000,000 (drawn) to corporate S (other general corporates, non-SME: sheet 0012; PD 2.00%, FIRB LGD 40% under Art. 161(1)(aa)). The loan is guaranteed in full by S's parent P, a large corporate the firm rates at PD 0.20% (financial corporates and large corporates: sheet 0022) and to which it has no direct exposure. Parameter Substitution Method, Art. 236: covered part risk-weighted with P's PD and correlation and the loan's LGD and 2.5y maturity -> RW 39.0173%, RWEA 3,901,732, EL = 0.20% x 40% x 10,000,000 = 8,000. Reported: sheet 0012 r0010 c0020 10,000,000, c0070 -10,000,000, c0090 0, c0280 0 (c0290 -6,000: the specific provision left with the original exposure); sheet 0022 r0010 c0080 10,000,000, c0090 10,000,000, c0110 10,000,000, c0260 3,901,732, c0280 8,000 and no c0020; the FIRB total sheet 0002 the sum; and one OF 08.02 grade row on each class sheet with the same figures. Arelle: boe_b0380 unsatisfied on sheet 0022 r0010 (8,000 against no original exposure), boe_b0395 unsatisfied on sheet 0022's grade row. A fuller book gives boe_b0380 [15, 5] - the five are sheet 0006 rows 0030 and 0001 (off-balance-sheet inflow, EL 4,000, no c0020, although the sheet's r0010 holds 50,000,000 of original exposure) and sheet 0022 rows 0010/0020/0070 - and boe_b0395 [4, 4]. Reporting c0020 = 0 explicitly on the inflow-only rows changes nothing ([15, 5] and [4, 4]). The example leaves out column 0040 on the obligor's rows and OF 08.01 rows 0020 / 0070; with them the same guarantor rows fail.

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Leave the covered part's EL on the obligor's row (so every row with EL also has col 0020): tested in Arelle - boe_b0380 becomes [20, 0] and boe_b0395 [8, 0], and the other 157 single-template rules return exactly the counts they return on the correct 250-fact return (which itself leaves boe_b0356 and boe_b1040 unsatisfied, as it reports no PD and no c0104), so the Bank's rule set - the OF 08.01-08.03 ties boe_b0736-b0740 included - cannot tell the two reportings apart. That (a) is not compliant is therefore an argument from the instructions, not something the rules show. It is not what Annex II asks: the covered part is 'assigned to the guarantor's exposure class and, where relevant, obligor grade or pool' (p.104), its exposure value and RWEA are reported there, Art. 158(1) ties EL to the same PD/LGD/exposure value as the RWEA, and Annex II names cols 0300 and 0310 as the ones kept on the original-obligor basis (p.114-115); an obligor grade row would otherwise show EL computed with another grade's PD against a zero exposure value. The EBA answered the same question for the same columns the same way. (b) Report the covered part as original exposure on the guarantor's row: double-counts col 0020 (the 10,000,000 would sit on both class sheets), contrary to the col 0020 and cols 0070-0080 instructions (p.102, p.104), which keep original exposure in the obligor's class and bring the covered part in through col 0080; not run in Arelle. (c) Report c0020 = 0 explicitly: still fails (Arelle). (d) Use the LGD Adjustment Method instead of substitution: a change of capital method, not of reporting, and not open to FIRB firms. None satisfies the rule compliantly.
issues.proposed_fix: Deactivate boe_b0380 and boe_b0395, as the EBA did with their originals v4757_m and v4772_m on 8 December 2017 (still deactivated in the EBA list up to release 3.5). If a ceiling on expected loss is wanted, put it on the post-substitution base that col 0280 is computed from - exposure value, col 0110, which is an open cell on every in-scope row - at WARNING severity: boe_b0380 -> iabs({t: OF08.01.01.01, c: 0280, dv: 0}) i<= iabs({t: OF08.01.01.01, c: 0110, dv: 0}); boe_b0395 -> {t: OF08.02.01.01, c: 0280, dv: 0} i<= {t: OF08.02.01.01, c: 0110, dv: 0}; scopes unchanged. Also ask the Bank to state in Annex II (OF 08.01 cols 0280-0282) that expected loss is reported after CRM substitution effects, in the guarantor's class and grade.
issues.eba_precedent: boe_b0380 restates v4757_m and boe_b0395 restates v4772_m (the v4.0.0 workbook's DESCRIPTION labels say so). EBA Q&A 2017_3509 (submitted 01/09/2017, final 08/12/2017) answers that the col 020 / col 280 interdependency 'does not exist'; docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx shows both rules 'Deactivated on 2017-12-08' in every sheet from v2.6 to 3.5, never reactivated or deleted. Note for the write-up: the earlier report's quotation of the Q&A dropped the words 'of templates C 08.01 / C 08.02'; the verbatim sentence is in the authority list. The Q&A is pre-exit EBA material on the repealed ITS 680/2014 - precedent, not UK authority.
issues.reach: An IRB firm that recognises guarantees or credit derivatives by the Parameter Substitution Method (FIRB firms that recognise unfunded protection from IRB-treated guarantors; AIRB firms where they substitute rather than adjust LGD) is affected wherever an inflow lands on a row with no, or negligible, direct original exposure - a guarantor's grade or class reached only through guarantees, an off-balance-sheet row or a conversion-factor bucket row; where the guarantor's grade or class already holds direct exposure, the row passes. From the first OF 08.01 / OF 08.02 return under PS1/26 (effective 1 January 2027). ERROR severity. On OF 08.02 it breaks on a guarantor grade with no direct obligor (boe_b0395); OF 08.01 breaks on off-balance-sheet / conversion-factor rows and on classes reached only through guarantees. The Bank widened the EBA's row scope (v4757_m: rows 0010;0015;0016;0020;0030;0070;0080;0180) to the conversion-factor rows 0031-0035/0001 and memo rows 0017/0175/0190/0200.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0684 / boe_b0686: provisions capped at original exposure - breaks only where provisions are reported on inflow-only rows (required for general credit risk adjustments if PI-04a holds, unstated for specific ones)
issues.requirement: On every in-scope OF 08.01 row and every OF 08.02 grade row, the absolute value of '(-) value adjustments and provisions' (col 0290) must not exceed original exposure pre-conversion factors (col 0020); both default to 0.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 col 0290 (second sentence)
authority.quote: General credit risk adjustments shall be reported by assigning the amount pro rata on the basis of the expected loss of the different obligor grades.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 col 0290 (end of first sentence; nothing in the entry says where a provision on a covered part is reported)
authority.quote: shall be reported, and other own funds reductions related to the asset item.

authority.locator: the SA counterpart, which is tied to the original exposure in terms
authority.quote: (-) Value adjustments and provisions associated with the original exposure

authority.locator: PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 159(2)(c)
authority.quote: an institution taking credit risk mitigation into account using the Risk-Weight Substitution Method shall not include any credit risk adjustments in respect of the covered part of an exposure, calculated in accordance with Credit Risk Mitigation (CRR) Part Article 235.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: It fails only where col 0290 is reported on a row that has an inflow and no original exposure. Annex II requires that for GENERAL credit risk adjustments: they are assigned pro rata on expected loss by obligor grade, expected loss follows the covered part to the guarantor's grade (PI-04a), so a guarantor grade or class row that holds only inflows gets a share of the general adjustment against col 0020 = 0. For SPECIFIC credit risk adjustments Annex II is silent: the entry says only that they 'shall be reported', with own funds reductions 'related to the asset item'. A firm that leaves specific provisions with the original exposure - the natural reading, and what OF 07.00 col 0030 does in terms - reports abs(0290) <= 0020 on every row and passes. The earlier claim that provisions in general 'follow EL onto the guarantor's sheet' is not supported by the text.

example.description: The PI-04a position (10,000,000 FIRB corporate loan, guaranteed by the large-corporate parent, EL 8,000 on sheet 0022) with a 6,000 specific provision on the loan and, in addition, a general credit risk adjustment of 1,600. All of the book's expected loss sits on the guarantor's rows, so the pro-rata instruction puts the whole 1,600 there: sheet 0022 r0010 c0290 = -1,600 with no c0020; sheet 0012 r0010 c0290 = -6,000 against c0020 10,000,000; total sheet 0002 c0290 = -7,600. Arelle: boe_b0684 unsatisfied on sheet 0022 r0010, boe_b0686 unsatisfied on sheet 0022's grade row. Without the general adjustment (the PI-04a spec, specific provision left with the obligor) both rules are satisfied. Fuller book with a general adjustment of 20% of EL: boe_b0684 [15, 5], boe_b0686 [4, 4]; same book with specific provisions only: boe_b0684 [15, 0], boe_b0686 [4, 0].

issues.alternatives_considered: Yes, and one satisfies the rule: keep specific credit risk adjustments with the original exposure (obligor's class and grade). Annex II does not forbid it, and Arelle shows boe_b0684 / boe_b0686 satisfied. That is why the finding is rescoped rather than confirmed. For a general credit risk adjustment there is no compliant alternative once any grade or class row holds only inflows, because the pro-rata-on-expected-loss instruction fixes where it goes.
issues.proposed_fix: Two asks. (1) Clarify Annex II OF 08.01 col 0290: are specific credit risk adjustments on a covered part reported with the original exposure (obligor's class and grade) or with the covered part (guarantor's)? authority.locator: Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 113(6)
authority.quote: With the exception of exposures giving rise to Common Equity Tier 1, Additional Tier 1 or Tier 2 items, an institution may with the prior permission of the PRA, assign a risk weight of 0% to the exposures of that institution to a counterparty which is its parent undertaking, its subsidiary, a subsidiary of its parent undertaking or an undertaking linked by a common management relationship, to the extent and subject to any modifications set out in the permission.
Intra-group exposures referred to in Article 113(6) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part shall be reported in line with paragraph 68.

That means that intra-group counterparties are not necessarily institutions but also undertakings which are assigned to other exposure classes, and therefore shall be reported in the corresponding exposure class.

Exposures to central governments or central banks (point (a) of paragraph 1). Exposures for which a risk-weight treatment is set out in Article 114, Article 115(2), Article 137(2), Article 114(7) of CRR, Article 115(4) of CRR or, for exposures that are deferred tax assets, paragraph 4 of Own Funds (CRR) Part Article 48.

Firms shall categorise Original exposures pre-conversion factors into the different exposure classes referred to in Article 112(1) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part and assign these Original exposures pre-conversion factors in the order set out in Article 112(2) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.
250 % Article 133(3) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part and Article 48(4) CRR

Retail exposures arising due to loans granted by a credit institution to pensioners or employees with a permanent contract against the unconditional transfer of part of the borrower's pension or salary to that credit institution shall be assigned a risk weight of 35%, provided that all the following conditions are met:

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Three weights the PS1/26 rules assign inside a class have a template row that the class's rule closes. (1) Intragroup exposures at 0% under an Art. 113(6) permission are reported in the counterparty's own class (Annex II paras 66 and 68), which is Institutions or Corporates; the 0% row is 0140 and boe_b0440 / boe_b0441 close it on those two sheets. (2) Deferred tax assets risk-weighted at 250% under Own Funds Art. 48(4) are assigned to the central governments class by Art. 112(2) Table A2 row (11), which Annex II para 56 tells firms to follow; the 250% row is 0250, Annex II cites Art. 48(4) for it, and boe_b0430 closes it on sheet 0002. (3) Retail loans repaid by assignment of salary or pension are weighted 35% by Art. 123(4); the 35% row is 0190 and boe_b0442 closes it on the retail sheet. In each case every fact in the row is one unsatisfied evaluation.

example.description: One return with the three positions, each on its class sheet and on the Total sheet 0001. Sheet 0002: a deferred tax asset of 500,000 at 250%, RWEA 1,250,000, row 0250. Sheet 0008: a 1,000,000 loan to a UK financial-institution subsidiary under the same permission, 0%, row 0140. Sheet 0009: 400,000 of pension-assigned loans meeting Art. 123(4), 35%, RWEA 140,000, row 0190. Rows 0010 and 0070 on each sheet carry the same figures; sheet 0001 carries the sums (exposure 3,900,000, RWEA 1,390,000).

Deferred tax assets: Table A2 row (11) fixes the class; 'Other items' (row 16) covers only Art. 113(5) and Art. 134 treatments. Retail 35%: Art. 123(4) calls these retail exposures, and the 35% row is listed. No Bank statement placing any of the three elsewhere was looked for beyond these passages.
issues.proposed_fix: Remove row 0140 from the row lists of boe_b0440, boe_b0440_1, boe_b0441 and boe_b0441_1; remove row 0250 from boe_b0430 and boe_b0430_1 (at least for sheet 0002 - the rule covers sheets 0002 and 0003 in one expression, so it must be split if row 0250 is to stay closed for regional governments); remove row 0190 from boe_b0442 and boe_b0442_1. authority.locator: Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 124I(2)
authority.quote: Subject to paragraph 3, an institution shall assign a risk weight of 110% to the entirety of a regulatory commercial real estate exposure that is materially dependent on the cash-flows generated by the property where the LTV is greater than 80%.

An institution shall, to the entirety of a regulatory commercial real estate exposure that is not to a natural person or an SME and that is not materially dependent on the cash-flows generated by the property, assign a risk weight that is the higher of: (a) 60%; and (b) the lower of: (i) the risk weight of the counterparty in accordance with point (e) of Article 124L(1); and (ii) the risk weight that would be assigned to the exposure under Article 124I if the exposure was materially dependent on the cash-flows generated by the property.
Real estate exposures (point (i) of paragraph 1). Exposures for which a risk-weight treatment is set out in Articles 124 to 124L.

Institutions shall report the information on the allocation of risk weights within the respective exposure class according to the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part and Chapter 2 of Title II of Part Three CRR.

Real estate exposures where there are 'charges not held by the institution ranking in priority ahead of the charge that the exposure is secured by' (Articles 124G(2), 124H(3) and 124I(3) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part), shall be reported against the risk weight which would have applied if Article 124G(2) and Article 124I(3) were disapplied (including for risk weights applied in accordance with Article 124H(3)). However, the RWEA shall still reflect the charge priority structure.

0340 of which: Real estate exposures - regulatory commercial real estate exposures Articles 124H and 124I of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part. Only reported in exposure class 'real estate exposures' (Article 112(1)(i) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part).

issues.why_correct_return_fails: PS1/26 assigns a 110% weight in exactly one place: Art. 124I(2), regulatory commercial real estate that depends on the property's cash flows with LTV above 80% ('110%' occurs once as a risk weight in Appendix 1). Art. 112(2) Table A2 row (7) puts that exposure in the real estate class, which is sheet 0010, and the template's only 110% row is 0232. boe_b0445 lists row 0232 among the rows that must be empty on sheet 0010, so every fact in that row raises the warning (6 facts, 6 unsatisfied evaluations in the example). The same row is reached by Art. 124H(3) (own-use commercial property lent to a borrower that is neither a natural person nor an SME: max(60%, min(counterparty weight, Art. 124I weight)) = 110% when the counterparty weight is 150%, or 135% where the investment-grade election of Art. 122 is used, and LTV is above 80%) and, through Annex II p.95, by Art. 124I(3)(c) (137.5% with a prior charge, reported against the 110% row with RWEA at 137.5%). The other eleven class rules of the family (boe_b0430, b0434, b0435, b0439, b0440, b0441, b0442, b0448, b0449, b0450, b0458) also list row 0232, so the 110% row is open only on the Total sheet (0001), CIUs (0015) and Other items (0017): it is closed on the one class that can have a 110% exposure. Every other real-estate weight of Art. 124F-124L has an open row once Annex II's conventions are applied (enumeration in PI-05b), and the open-row list matches those weights exactly, so the omission of 110% reads as an oversight.

example.description: An SA firm with one on-balance-sheet loan of 1,000,000 secured on a let office building: regulatory commercial real estate, materially dependent on the property's cash flows, unrated borrower, LTV 85%, no provisions, no credit protection. Art. 124I(2): 110%, RWEA 1,100,000. Reported on OF 07.00 sheet 0010 and on the Total sheet 0001: rows 0010 (total), 0070 (on-balance sheet), 0340 (regulatory commercial real estate) and 0342 (of which materially dependent) carry c0010 = c0040 = c0110 = c0150 = c0200 = 1,000,000 and c0220 = 1,100,000; row 0010 also c0235 = 1,100,000; risk-weight row 0232 (110%) carries c0010 = c0040 = c0150 = c0200 = 1,000,000 and c0220 = c0235 = 1,100,000.

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) Row 0280 'Other risk weights' instead of row 0232: Arelle boe_b0445 [0,6] again (the rule closes 0280 as well), and Annex II p.96 keeps that row for 'exposures not subject to the risk weights listed in the template'; 110% is listed. Annex II lets a firm report against a lower weight only for the currency-mismatch multiplier (p.94), prior charges (p.95) and transitional equity (p.95); none applies to a plain Art. 124I(2) loan. (3) Another sheet: not available, Art. 112(2) Table A2 row (7) makes it a real estate exposure. No Annex-II-compliant reporting satisfies the rule.

issues.title: boe_b1041 (ERROR, always executed) fails every OF 08.01 filer that reports nothing in the slotting row on sheet 0002 or 0010; one explicit zero there is enough to pass

publisher_log.statement: OF08.01 columns 0125, 0140, 0170, 0180 are greyed out for row 0080 on sheet 0002 and 0010 and therefore unnecessariy referenced in the expression context. issues.requirement: Whenever OF 08.01 is filed (filing indicator OF08.01.01 positive), at least one fact must be reported in row 0080 'Specialised lending slotting approach: Total' of OF 08.01.01.01 on sheet 0002 (Total, FIRB approach and slotting approach) or sheet 0010 (Corporates - Specialised Lending, FIRB approach or slotting approach), in any of the listed columns. Of the 24 listed columns, 20 are cells of that row on those sheets (0020, 0035, 0040, 0050, 0060, 0070, 0090, 0101, 0102, 0103, 0104, 0110, 0251, 0252, 0260, 0280, 0281, 0282, 0290, 0300); 0125, 0140, 0170 and 0180 are not cells of row 0080 at all. Each matching fact is one satisfied evaluation; with no matching fact there is exactly one evaluation and it is unsatisfied. It does not require every cell, both sheets, or a non-zero value.

authority.quote: SPECIALISED LENDING SLOTTING APPROACH: TOTAL Exposures subject to the slotting approach. This shall only apply to the exposure sub-class 'corporate - specialised lending'.

In cases where an institution uses the AIRB approach for a part of its IRB exposures and the FIRB or slotting approach to calculate risk-weighted exposure amounts for the other part of its IRB exposures, one OF CR IRB Total for exposures subject to the FIRB approach or the slotting approach and one OF CR IRB Total for exposures subject to the AIRB approach shall be reported.
Total (The Total template must be reported for the FIRB and the slotting approaches and, separately for the AIRB approach.)

Missing fact The fact doesn't appear in the XBRL report. Template including this fact is reported The value is treated as equivalent to zero (if numeric fact) or empty (if non-numeric) by the recipient.
Inapplicable information should not be included in an XBRL report, i.e. inapplicable facts MAY be omitted.
Zero values SHOULD, preferably, be explicitly reported where they are interesting supervisory reporting information.
In case of error severity, failing validation should block the submission of the report.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: A firm with no slotting exposure has nothing to put in the slotting row. Annex II p.117 defines row 0080 as exposures subject to the slotting approach and restricts it to specialised lending; nothing asks for a zero. Everywhere else in the rule set an unreported row 0080 and a zero are the same statement: boe_b0631 compares OF 02.00 row 0411 ('Exposures subject to the slotting approach') with OF 08.01 row 0080 on sheet 0002 using dv: 0 on both sides, and Arelle satisfies it with r0411 = 0 and no row 0080. boe_b1041 alone turns the absence into an ERROR. For an A-IRB-only firm it is worse: only the FIRB/slotting sheets satisfy the rule, and Annex II para 75 asks for the FIRB/slotting Total where the firm uses those approaches; a zero on the firm's own Total sheet (0001) does not satisfy boe_b1041 and breaks boe_b0206 instead. The label describes a restriction (it is boe_b0206's label, and boe_b0206 states the restriction correctly), not a presence requirement. The rule is also not needed where slotting exists: boe_b0816, b0819 and b0822 are each unsatisfied [0,1] in Arelle when OF 08.06 reports slotting exposure and row 0080 is missing. Without 'Always execute' the rule could never fail, because it would evaluate only when a fact is bound; so as published it is either harmful or empty.

example.description: An F-IRB firm with a corporate loan book and no specialised lending: a collateralised loan: original exposure, exposure after CRM and exposure value 1,000,000, PD 1.25%, RWEA 600,000 (pre-adjustment RWEA 600,000), 10 obligors. OF 08.01 is reported on sheet 0012 (Corporates - Other general corporates - non-SME, FIRB) and on the Total sheet 0002, rows 0010, 0020 (on-balance sheet) and 0070 (obligor grades total). Row 0080 is not reported because there is no slotting exposure. OF 02.00 row 0411 (slotting RWEA) is reported as 0 so that the Bank's own cross-check boe_b0631 evaluates.

issues.alternatives_considered: To pass, a firm must file at least one fact, which may be 0, in OF 08.01.01.01 row 0080 on sheet 0002 or sheet 0010, in any of the 20 reportable columns. For an F-IRB firm that is an extra zero on a sheet it already files. For an A-IRB-only firm it means filing a fact on the FIRB/slotting Total sheet, a sheet for approaches it does not use. Zero-filling its own Total sheet 0001 does not work (boe_b1041 still [0,1], boe_b0206 [0,1]). Not filing OF 08.01 is not open to an IRB firm. The zero is a true statement and breaks no other rule (wide sweep), so it is a workable workaround, but nothing in Annex II asks for it.
issues.proposed_fix: Withdraw (deactivate) boe_b1041. The restriction its label states is already enforced by boe_b0206 and boe_b0206_1, and the presence of row 0080 whenever slotting exposure exists is already enforced by boe_b0816, b0817, b0819, b0822, b0823 and b0829 against OF 08.06 row 0095. If a presence check is still wanted, make it conditional on slotting being reported and stop executing it unconditionally, for example: if not(isNull({t: OF08.06.01.01, r: 0095, c: 0010, dv: emptySequence()})) then not(isNull({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: 0020, z: 0002; 0010, dv: emptySequence()})) else true(), with Always execute = no. The Bank already intends to drop columns 0125, 0140, 0170 and 0180, which are not cells of row 0080 (known issues log #28).

authority.quote: EXPOSURE-WEIGHTED AVERAGE MATURITY VALUE (DAYS) The value reported shall be determined in accordance with Article 162 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted averages. The average maturity shall be reported in days.

This data shall not be reported for the exposure values for which the maturity is not an element in the calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts. This column shall therefore not be filled in for the exposure class ‘retail’ or for exposures subject to the slotting approach.

For all exposure classes, with the exception of the exposure class ‘retail’ and, for other exposures classes, the cases mentioned in the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.

Within the exposure class ‘retail’, or if separate exposures to the same obligor are assigned to different obligor grades in accordance with the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part in other exposure classes, the institution shall report the number of exposures which were separately assigned to a certain rating grade or pool.

Off-balance sheet items shall be reported in accordance with Article 166A to Article 166D and shall comprise items that are listed in Table A1 Article 111 of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.

authority.locator: OF 08.01 rows 0031, 0032, 0001, 0033, 0035 (BREAKDOWN OF OFF-BALANCE SHEET ITEMS BY CONVERSION FACTORS)
authority.quote: For exposures subject to the slotting approach, the FIRB approach, or the AIRB approach where neither conversion factors nor EADs are estimated, institutions shall report values in rows that correspond to the applicable conversion factors in Article 111 of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, in accordance with Articles 166A to 166D of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 166C(1)
authority.quote: An institution shall determine the exposure value for off-balance sheet items in respect of which it uses the Foundation IRB Approach or the Slotting Approach in accordance with Article 147A by multiplying the conversion factor that would be applicable to the off-balance sheet item under the Standardised Approach, as set out in Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 111, by the item’s nominal value.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 111 Table A1 (Column B: 40% against row (5); 50% against rows (3)-(4), checked by word coordinates)
authority.quote: (5) Any other commitment that is not subject to a conversion factor of 10%, 50% or 100%.
(3) Other issued off-balance sheet items that do not have the character of credit substitutes.

Where Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part applies, an obligor may be considered in more than one grade. As this column deals with an element of the structure of the rating scales, it relates to the original exposures pre-conversion factor assigned to each obligor grade or pool without taking into account the effect of CRM techniques (in particular redistribution effects).

issues.why_correct_return_fails: The rule holds when |row0030 - sum(bucket rows)| <= sum of allowances (0.5 for each reported integer fact). c0300: an obligor with a facility in two buckets is one obligor in row 0030 (counted 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted') and one in each bucket row, so the bucket rows add to more than the total. 12 corporates each with a 40% and a 50% facility: 12 against 12 + 12 = 24, allowance 1.5, unsatisfied. c0250: row 0030 is the exposure-value-weighted average of the bucket maturities, (48m x 1,095 + 24m x 365) / 72m = 852 days, against 1,095 + 365 = 1,460; an average of positive numbers never equals their sum. Thresholds measured in Arelle: c0250 fails as soon as two bucket rows carry a maturity (even with one obligor, or with no obligor in two buckets); c0300 fails when the number of double-counted obligors exceeds 0.5 x (reported bucket rows + 1), i.e. from two overlapping obligors with two buckets (one overlapping obligor is absorbed by the allowance: 1 against 2, allowance 1.5, satisfied). The other 27 evaluable columns are monetary amounts attributable to single exposures, each of which sits in exactly one conversion-factor row, and are additive: all 8 that the example reports are satisfied.

example.description: OF 08.01 sheet 0012 (Corporates - Other general corporates - non-SME, FIRB). Twelve corporates, each with (a) an undrawn committed facility of 10m, Table A1 row (5), 40%, row 0001, maturity 3 years, and (b) a 4m issued off-balance-sheet item not having the character of a credit substitute, Table A1 row (3), 50%, row 0033, maturity 1 year. Row 0001: original exposure 120,000,000; exposure value 48,000,000; RWEA 28,800,000; EL 96,000; provisions -48,000; average maturity 1,095 days; 12 obligors. Row 0033: 48,000,000; 24,000,000; 10,800,000; 48,000; -18,000; 365 days; 12 obligors. Row 0030: 168,000,000; 72,000,000; 39,600,000; 144,000; -66,000; exposure-weighted average maturity 852 days; 12 obligors. OF 08.01.01.02 r0010 c0120 = 72,000,000 (for the control rules). Monetary facts stated exact to units (decimals 0), integers at decimals 0.

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) Leave c0250 and c0300 empty on rows 0030, 0001 and 0031-0035 (spec a3): boe_b0742 [8,0], passes, because no evaluation exists where nothing is reported. Annex II has no instruction that exempts these rows, the DPM leaves the cells open and the Bank's own boe_b0314_6 / boe_b0314_1_x scope them, so this is an omission the gateway tolerates, not a compliant reading. (2) Report c0250 / c0300 on row 0030 only and leave the bucket rows empty for those two columns (a4): [8,2], fails (852 against 0, 12 against 0). (3) Report row 0030 as the sum of the bucket rows, 24 'obligors' and 1,460 days (a8): [10,0], passes, but it counts each obligor once per facility and reports a sum of averages, contrary to pp.111 and 114. (4) Nothing in the filing-indicator precondition or defaults helps: the rule has dv: 0 on row 0030 and an empty-sequence default on the bucket rows.
