issues.title: boe_b0737 treats distinct obligor counts as additive (OF 08.01 c0300 total minus CCR rows = OF 08.03 c0060)
issues.requirement: On each of the 17 IRB sheets: the number of obligors on the OF 08.01 Total row (r0010 c0300), minus the sum of the numbers of obligors on the three counterparty-credit-risk rows (r0040 SFT netting sets, r0050 derivative netting sets, r0060 cross-product netting sets), must equal the sum of the numbers of obligors over the eight top-level PD ranges of OF 08.03 (c0060). Blocking (ERROR).

authority.quote: For all exposure classes, with the exception of the exposure class ‘retail’ and, for other exposures classes, the cases mentioned in the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.

The number of legal entities or obligors allocated to each bucket of the fixed PD range. The number of obligors shall be counted in accordance with the instructions in column 0300 of template OF08.01. Joint obligors shall be treated the same as for the purpose of PD calibration.
This template excludes counterparty credit risk (CCR) exposures (Counterparty Credit Risk (CRR) Part and Chapter 6 of Title II of Part Three CRR).
Exposures that are subject to counterparty credit risk shall be reported in rows 0040-0060 and, therefore, shall not be reported in this row.

authority.locator: OF 07.00 rows 0090 and 0110 (to which OF 08.01 rows 0040 and 0050 refer)
authority.quote: Netting sets containing only SFTs, as defined in Article 4(1)(139) CRR. [...] Netting sets containing only derivatives listed in Annex II CRR and long settlement transactions as defined in Article 272(2) CRR.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Write N for the distinct obligors on a sheet, A for the obligors with a non-CCR exposure (what OF 08.03 counts, because OF 08.03 excludes CCR), and S, D, X for the obligors with an SFT, a derivative and a cross-product netting set. Annex II defines every one of these cells as a count of legal entities 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted'. The rule asserts N - (S + D + X) = A. That is an identity only when no obligor sits in two of the groups. If B obligors have both a loan and a swap, N - D = A - B, so the rule is short by B. If an obligor has both an SFT and a derivative netting set, S + D counts it twice and the left side is short again. Separately, the boe_b0836 family requires S + D + X = the number of CCR counterparties in OF 34.07, while boe_b0737 requires S + D + X = N - A (the CCR-only obligors): the two cannot both hold once an obligor has a loan and a CCR netting set, where N (row 0010) is the distinct count that p.114 asks for. The rounding allowance is at most 0.5 per integer fact stated with decimals 0 (0.5 x 4 = 2 in the example, at most 0.5 x 12 = 6 if every CCR row and every PD range is reported; none for a count stated with decimals INF, which the Filing Manual's rule 2.18 also allows), so about seven overlapping obligors always break the rule.

example.description: Corporates - other general corporates - non-SME (FIRB), sheet 0012. 30 obligors: 10 with a loan only, 10 with a loan and an interest-rate swap hedging it, 10 with a swap only. OF 08.01: r0010 c0300 = 30 (legal entities), r0020 = 20 (borrowers), r0050 = 20 (obligors with a derivatives netting set), r0070 = 30; exposure value 2,400 / 2,000 / 400 and RWEA 1,400 / 1,200 / 200 on rows 0010 / 0020 / 0050. OF 08.03 (no CCR): the 20 borrowers in PD ranges r0050 (12 obligors, EV 1,200, RWEA 660) and r0060 (8 obligors, EV 800, RWEA 540). OF 34.07: the 20 swap counterparties in one PD band and the Total. The rule computes 30 - 20 = 10 against 20.

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Total reported as 20 + 20 = 40 (b1_alt_total_as_sum): every rule passes in Arelle, but r0010 then counts ten legal entities twice, contrary to 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted' (p.114). It is rejected on the wording of p.114, not on test results: the convention 'row 0010 = the OF 08.03 count plus the CCR rows' always satisfies boe_b0737. With the total reported otherwise, when the 20 borrowers have a drawn loan and an undrawn commitment as well, the rule fails with the total reported as the distinct count (30) and as the sum of the category rows (60) alike - b4_onoff_overlap_distinct_total and b4_onoff_overlap_summed_total both give boe_b0737 [0,1]. (b) r0050 c0300 counting only the 10 swap-only obligors (b1_alt_ccr_only_obligors): boe_b0737 passes, boe_b0846 fails [0,1] because OF 34.07 has 20 CCR counterparties. (c) r0050 c0300 left empty (b1_alt_blank_ccr_count): boe_b0737 [0,1] and boe_b0846 [0,1]. No Annex-II-compliant way of counting satisfies the rule.
issues.proposed_fix: Deactivate boe_b0737, as the EBA did with v09775_m on 2021-03-10. If a check is wanted, replace it with a one-sided warning that is true for distinct counts: {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0300} i>= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, c: 0060}), severity WARNING, same sheet scope. The amount siblings boe_b0736 / b0738 / b0739 / b0740 are not affected by this point (amounts are additive).
issues.eba_precedent: boe_b0737 restates EBA v09775_m (the Bank's own v4.0.0 workbook names it as the equivalent). In docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx v09775_m is severity Warning, deactivated on 2021-03-10 and never reactivated in any release sheet from v3.0 to 3.5 (the formula was re-expressed in 3.2.0 and stayed deactivated). Its siblings v09773_m - v09778_m carry the same deactivation date - including v09774_m (exposure value) and v09776_m (RWEA), which are additive - so the EBA's deactivation does not single out the non-additive count; from 3.2.0 the EBA formula also sums over sheets s0001-s0017 rather than applying per sheet.
issues.reach: Any IRB firm with obligors that have both a CCR netting set and a loan or commitment in the same exposure class (corporate borrowers that hedge with the lender), or both an SFT and a derivatives netting set (bank counterparties), from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions (effective 1 January 2027). Blocking.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: Seventeen rules equate the OF 34.07 number of CCR obligors with the sum of three overlapping OF 08.01 obligor counts
issues.requirement: Per sheet: the number of obligors on the OF 34.07 Total row (r0180 c0030) must equal the sum of the numbers of obligors on OF 08.01 rows 0040 (SFT netting sets), 0050 (derivative netting sets) and 0060 (cross-product netting sets), column 0300. Blocking (ERROR), 17 rules.

authority.quote: The number of legal entities or obligors allocated to each bucket of the fixed PD scale, which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.
CCR exposures (determined at counterparty level) shall be allocated to the appropriate bucket of the fixed PD scale based on the PD estimated for each obligor assigned to this exposure class
the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.

authority.locator: OF 07.00 rows 0090 and 0110 (to which OF 08.01 rows 0040 and 0050 refer, p.116)
authority.quote: Netting sets containing only SFTs, as defined in Article 4(1)(139) CRR. SFTs that are included in a contractual cross product netting set and therefore reported in row 0130 shall not be reported in this row. [...] Netting sets containing only derivatives listed in Annex II CRR and long settlement transactions as defined in Article 272(2) CRR.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: OF 34.07 counts each CCR counterparty once ('determined at counterparty level', 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted'). OF 08.01 row 0040 counts the obligors with an SFT netting set and row 0050 the obligors with a derivatives netting set. A counterparty with a repo agreement and a derivatives agreement - and no cross-product netting agreement, so nothing in row 0060 - is one obligor in OF 34.07 and is counted in both OF 08.01 rows. With K such counterparties the right side exceeds the left by K. The allowance is at most 0.5 per integer fact stated with decimals 0 (0.5 x 4 = 2 with all four facts reported, 1.5 with rows 0040 and 0050 only), so two such counterparties can break the rule and three always do; a count stated with decimals INF (allowed by the Filing Manual's rule 2.18) has no allowance, and one is enough.

example.description: Institutions (FIRB), sheet 0006: 12 bank counterparties, all with a derivatives netting set, 10 of them also with a repo netting set, no cross-product netting. OF 08.01: r0010 c0300 = 12, r0040 = 10, r0050 = 12; exposure value 300 (SFT) + 600 (derivatives) = 900, RWEA 60 + 180 = 240. OF 34.07: one PD band and the Total with EV 900, 12 obligors, RWEA 240, density 0.2667. The rule computes 12 against 10 + 12 = 22.

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) OF 34.07 c0030 counting a counterparty once per netting-set type (22; b2_alt_ccr7_per_row): boe_b1035 passes [1,0], but the cell is then not the number of legal entities 'regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted' (p.206) and not 'determined at counterparty level' (p.207). (b) De-duplicating across OF 08.01 rows 0040 / 0050 has no basis in the instructions (each row is its own netting-set population) and would need an arbitrary allocation rule. No compliant alternative found.
issues.proposed_fix: In each of boe_b0836, b0837, b0840-b0853 and b1035 replace 'i=' by 'i<=' ({t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0180, c: 0030, z: S} i<= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: 0300, z: S})) and set severity WARNING; or deactivate the 17 rules, as the EBA has done (deleted from release 3.2 onward). The inequality also survives the two population differences in PI-08 (slotting, CCP-cleared).
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA family is v10521_h - v10537_h ({C 34.07, r0180, c0030, sNNNN} = C 08.01 r0040 + r0050 + r0060 c0300, one per sheet), added in release 3.0.0 with severity Warning, never Error. In the v3.0 and v3.1 sheets of docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx, v10522_h (s0002 Total F-IRB) and v10526_h (s0006 Institutions F-IRB) are deactivated on 2021-09-10 and v10523_h / v10524_h (the two central-government sheets) on 2022-12-12; in the sheets for releases 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 all 17 are flagged Deleted = y. Matched by sheet code (the Bank kept the EBA codes 0001, 0002, 0006, 0009-0012, 0015-0017), boe_b0837 and boe_b1035 restate rules the EBA deactivated; the example sheet (0006) is one of them. Caution: the eba_equivalent column of the Bank's v4.0.0 workbook pairs these rules by position, not by sheet (boe_b0841, sheet 0010, is paired with v10526_h, the EBA's sheet 0006 rule), so it should not be quoted as a sheet-for-sheet mapping.
issues.reach: Any IRB firm with at least three counterparties on one sheet that have both an SFT netting set and a derivatives netting set without a cross-product netting agreement - the normal position for bank and large financial counterparties. All 17 sheets in principle; realistic on the institution, corporate and Total sheets. Blocking from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions.

If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0768, boe_b0769, boe_b0770 (ERROR) add OF 08.03 sub-band rows on c0030 (exposure-weighted average conversion factor); boe_b0767 dropped c0030 in v4.1.1 and the EBA dropped it from all four
issues.requirement: For each column in scope and each sheet, the parent PD band (0.75 to <2.5; 2.5 to <10; 10 to <100) must equal the sum of its sub-bands. Column 0030 is in scope of the three rules. Its data point is eba_met:mi796, declared in the Bank's package as <xs:element name="mi796" type="xbrli:monetaryItemType" ...> (label 'Exposure weighted conversion factors'), so its rounding allowance is whatever decimals the filer states for a monetary fact. The other averaged columns of the template (0050 PD, 0070 LGD, 0080 maturity) are correctly outside the scope; the XBRL formula of boe_b0767 no longer lists mi796, those of boe_b0768-b0770 still do.

authority.quote: EXPOSURE WEIGHTED AVERAGE CONVERSION FACTORS For all exposures included in each bucket of the fixed PD range, the average conversion factor used by institutions in their calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts, weighted by the off-balance sheet exposure pre-CCF as reported in column 0020.
Exposures shall be allocated to an appropriate bucket of the fixed PD range based on the PD estimated for each obligor assigned to this exposure class

The Bank will interpret the decimals setting on reported data as specifying that the absolute difference between the true value of the number as known to the reporter and its reported lexical representation (known as the “absolute error” of the representation - eabs) is less than or equal to 0.5 x 10-n.

The reported accuracy of a numeric fact SHOULD be a realistic indication of the accuracy to which the lexical representation represents the true value. In particular, it SHOULD NOT be excessively high.

E.g. decimals setting of greater than 2 would generally be inappropriate for calculated “monetary” values resulting from e.g. multiplications or divisions, “INF” is often unlikely to be appropriate for calculated values.

authority.locator: Accuracy Requirements for 2.18 (table: Monetary '>= -3'; Percentage '>= 4', 'Must be expressed as a ratio in reports'; Integer '0')
authority.quote: INF (meaning exact as written) is acceptable for the decimal attribute of all numeric types.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: A parent band's average conversion factor is the nominal-weighted mean of its sub-bands' factors, so it lies between them and cannot equal their sum unless only one sub-band has off-balance-sheet exposure. Band 0.75 to <2.5: sub-bands 0.40 (60m nominal) and 0.20 (20m) give a parent of (24m + 4m) / 80m = 0.35 against a required 0.40 + 0.20 = 0.60. The comparison is |parent - sum| <= sum of allowances, each 0.5 x 10^-decimals. Measured in Arelle on the same figures: decimals 4, 2 and INF, all three rules unsatisfied on c0030; decimals 0, boe_b0768 and boe_b0769 satisfied (tolerance 1.5 swallows a factor that cannot exceed 1) and boe_b0770 unsatisfied (0.40 against 1.10: its plain sum leaves only the parent's 0.5); decimals -3, all three satisfied (tolerance in the hundreds, vacuous). So the outcome depends on an accuracy attribute and not on the figures: as measured here, all three rules pass at decimals -1 or below, boe_b0770 alone fails at 0, and all three fail at 1 or above (the thresholds depend on the figures; with two sub-bands boe_b0768 / boe_b0769 cannot fail at decimals 0). The Bank's own sample instance states every mi796 fact at decimals -3.

example.description: OF 08.03 sheet 0012 (Corporates - Other general corporates - non-SME, FIRB; conversion factors from Article 111 Table A1). For each PD sub-band: off-balance-sheet nominal (c0020), its exposure-weighted average conversion factor (c0030) and exposure value (c0040); each parent row carries the totals and the nominal-weighted average factor. 0.75 to <2.5: 60m at 0.40 and 20m at 0.20, parent 80m at 0.35. 2.5 to <10: 15m at 0.50 and 5m at 0.10, parent 20m at 0.40. 10 to <100: 4m at 0.50, 2m at 0.20, 2m at 0.40, parent 8m at 0.40. 0.00 to <0.15 (control band, boe_b0767): 20m at 0.30, 20m at 0.40, 10m at 0.50, parent 50m at 0.38. c0030 stated to two places (decimals 2, pence, the Filing Manual's ceiling for a calculated monetary value); amounts exact to units.

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) State c0030 at decimals -3 (or -1, -2): passes, and the Filing Manual's minimum for a monetary fact (>= -3) allows it, though it declares a ratio of 0.35 to be known only to the nearest 1,000; rule 2.18(c) says accuracy 'SHOULD NOT be excessively high' and does not prohibit understating it, and -3 is what the Bank's own sample instance states. (2) Report c0030 on the sub-bands and leave it empty on the parent rows (spec c6): fails, 0 against the sum. (3) Leave c0030 empty everywhere: passes, but Annex II asks for it 'for all exposures included in each bucket'. (4) Report the parent as the sum of the sub-band factors: passes, misstates the figure and can exceed 100%. (5) Only one sub-band with off-balance-sheet exposure: passes trivially. Which accuracy would a real filing carry? The Manual sets only a floor (monetary >= -3, INF allowed) and asks for values 'as known' with a realistic decimals; for a factor known to two or four places that is 2 (footnote 11's ceiling for calculated monetary values) or INF, and at either the rules fail. Software that stamps one decimals value on every monetary fact carries whatever that value is: -3 passes vacuously, 0 fails boe_b0770 only, 2 fails all three. Real filings were not observed.
issues.proposed_fix: Remove c0030 from the scope of boe_b0768, boe_b0769 and boe_b0770, giving each the scope boe_b0767 has in v4.1.1 and the EBA has used since framework 3.2.0: scope({t: OF08.03.01.01, c:0010;0020;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110, z:0001;0002;0006;0009;0010;0011;0012;0015;0016;0017;0018;0019;0020;0021;0022;0023;0024}). Separately, eba_met:mi796 holds a ratio and should not be a monetary item; while it is, the published accuracy floor of -3 makes any check on it depend on the filer's decimals.
issues.eba_precedent: The equivalents are v09753_m to v09756_m (C 08.03, WARNING at the EBA, ERROR at the Bank). In EBA releases 3.0 and 3.1 all four had columns (0010;0020;0030;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110); in framework release 3.2.0 ('Last Change: Change') all four became (0010;0020;0040;0060;0090;0100;0110) and remain so in 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 (docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx, sheets 'v3.1(3.1.1)' and '3.2(3.2.1, 3.2.2)' to '3.5'). The Bank's v4.0.0 rules had the pre-3.2 scope on all four; v4.1.1 changed boe_b0767 alone.
issues.reach: IRB firms filing OF 08.03 with off-balance-sheet exposure in two or more sub-bands of a parent PD band, whose software states c0030 at decimals >= 1 (boe_b0768, boe_b0769) or >= 0 (boe_b0770): for example any filer stating monetary facts to pence or as exact. Firms stating all monetary facts to thousands are not affected.

If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0770 is written 'i= sum(...)' where its siblings use isum, so the summed sub-band rows get no rounding allowance
issues.requirement: The 10 to <100 PD band must equal the sum of its three sub-bands on eight columns. In the Bank's interval-arithmetic functions a reported fact carries a threshold of 0.5 x 10^-decimals and anything that is not a fact carries 0 (interval-arithmetics.xml, iaf:splitValueThreshold: 'if (not($item instance of element()) ...) then ($item, 0)'), and iaf:numeric-equal is 'abs($itemA[1] - $itemB[1]) le ($itemA[2] + $itemB[2])'. XPath sum($v1) returns a plain number, so boe_b0770 allows only the parent row's own threshold, where boe_b0767-b0769 (iaf:sum) allow the parent's plus every sub-band's.

authority.quote: In particular, if numbers are truncated or rounded for reporting, they should not be “adjusted” so that they appear to be visually consistent (i.e. so that they “foot” or “cast”) but should instead be simply reported with the appropriate @decimals value – the validation checks will take into account the declared accuracy to determine if reported values are valid.

Note: This, combined with the definition of the decimals setting, means that in general monetary values must not be truncated to thousands (since the reported value might then be up to 1000 from the true value, which is more than the 500 implied by decimals=-3, requiring instead decimals= –4 to be consistent), but may be rounded (i.e. to nearest value) to thousands
The Bank’s XBRL validation rules use interval arithmetic for validation.
test="iaf:numeric-equal($v0,sum($v1))"

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Take three sub-band exposures of 12,345,400, 8,765,400 and 3,210,400 (total 24,321,200) and a filer that rounds each fact to the nearest thousand and states decimals -3, as the Filing Manual permits and the Bank's own sample instance does. Reported: 12,345,000 + 8,765,000 + 3,210,000 = 24,320,000 against a parent of 24,321,000. Every fact is within 500 of its true value. With isum the tolerance would be 4 x 500 = 2,000 and the rule holds; boe_b0770 allows 500 and the difference is 1,000, so it is unsatisfied. The same arithmetic on the two-row bands (21,111,000 against 21,110,000, tolerance 1,500) passes boe_b0768 and boe_b0769. A filer who reports exact units is unaffected.

example.description: OF 08.03 sheet 0012, column 0010 (on-balance-sheet exposures) only, every fact rounded to the nearest thousand and stated at decimals -3. Bands 0.75 to <2.5 and 2.5 to <10 (controls): sub-bands 12,345,000 and 8,765,000, parent 21,111,000 (true 21,110,800). Band 10 to <100: sub-bands 12,345,000, 8,765,000 and 3,210,000, parent 24,321,000 (true 24,321,200).

issues.alternatives_considered: Report every figure unrounded in units, as the Filing Manual prefers ('reported as known'): passes. Or adjust the rounded parent so that it foots (24,320,000): passes, but the Manual tells firms not to do this. A firm that rounds each fact correctly and declares decimals -3, which the Manual expressly allows, fails boe_b0770 and nothing in the instructions lets it pass.
issues.proposed_fix: Change sum to isum in boe_b0770 so that it matches boe_b0767-b0769: {t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0130, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0140; 0150; 0160, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}) (XBRL test iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:sum($v1))). Review the five other interval rules that divide a plain sum, boe_b0820, boe_b0821, boe_b0822, boe_b0823 and boe_b0829, for the same substitution.
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA original v09756_m is '{r0130} = {r0140} + {r0150} + {r0160}' with 'Arithmetic approach: Interval', the same as v09753_m to v09755_m. The plain sum is in the Bank's v4.0.0 and v4.1.1 workbook text and in the v4.1.1 formula alone among the four.
issues.reach: Any firm that rounds monetary facts (to thousands, say) and states the matching decimals, on OF 08.03 band 10 to <100 on any of the eight columns: it fails whenever the rounding errors of the three sub-bands and the parent add to more than the parent's own allowance. Firms that file exact units are not affected.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0830 - boe_b0834 sum an exposure-weighted average maturity (c0050) and a ratio (c0070) down the OF 34.07 PD bands; on c0070 they cannot hold together with boe_b0759
issues.requirement: boe_b0830 - b0834: on every OF 34.07 sheet, each PD-band subtotal row equals the sum of its sub-bands and the Total row (0180) equals the sum of the eight top-level bands, for each of columns 0010 (exposure value), 0030 (number of obligors), 0050 (exposure-weighted average maturity), 0060 (RWEA) and 0070 (density of RWEA). boe_b0759: on every row including the subtotals and the Total, c0070 x c0010 = c0060. All blocking (ERROR).

authority.quote: Density of risk-weighted exposure amounts Ratio of the total risk-weighted exposure amounts (reported in column 0060) to the exposure value (reported in column 0010).
Exposure weighted average maturity (years) Average of obligor maturities in years weighted by their corresponding exposure value as defined for column 0010.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Two bands with exposure values E1, E2 and densities d1, d2 (RWEA = d x E). boe_b0834 on c0010 and c0060 makes the Total row E1 + E2 and d1E1 + d2E2; boe_b0759 on the Total row then forces its density to (d1E1 + d2E2) / (E1 + E2), which is also what Annex II defines. boe_b0834 on c0070 forces the same cell to d1 + d2. Both hold only if d1E2 + d2E1 = 0, that is only if one band alone carries exposure. The same algebra applies to every subtotal row (boe_b0830 - b0833). For c0050 no second rule pins the cell, but Annex II defines it as an exposure-weighted average, and the sum of two averages is not the average: reporting the Annex II figure fails the rule, reporting the sum satisfies the rule and misstates the cell. c0050 is an integer-typed metric (eba_met:ii791), so the allowance is 0.5 per fact; two bands with maturities of two years or more already exceed it.

example.description: Institutions (FIRB), sheet 0006, three populated PD bands. r0040: EV 500, 7 obligors, maturity 2, RWEA 120, density 0.24. r0080: EV 300, 3 obligors, maturity 4, RWEA 180, density 0.60. r0090: EV 100, 2 obligors, maturity 5, RWEA 80, density 0.80. As Annex II defines them: subtotal r0070 = EV 400, 5 obligors, maturity (300x4 + 100x5)/400 = 4.25 reported 4, RWEA 260, density 260/400 = 0.65; Total r0180 = EV 900, 12 obligors, maturity 2,700/900 = 3, RWEA 380, density 380/900 = 0.4222. The rules want r0070 maturity 9 and density 1.40, and - with r0070 at those values - Total maturity 11 and density 1.64 (with r0070 at the Annex II values, 4 and 0.65, boe_b0834 asks the Total for 6 and 0.89).

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Subtotal and Total c0050 / c0070 reported as the sums the rules ask for (d_way_b_sums): boe_b0831 [5,0] and b0834 [5,0], but boe_b0759 [3,2] - it fails on r0070 and r0180 - and both cells contradict their Annex II definitions. (b) c0050 and c0070 left empty on the subtotal and Total rows (d_omit_totals): boe_b0831 [3,2], b0834 [3,2], b0759 [3,2] (an empty cell is read as 0). (c) c0050 and c0070 not reported on any row (d_omit_columns): boe_b0759 [0,5]. No way of reporting two populated bands passes all six rules.
issues.proposed_fix: Change the scope of boe_b0830, b0831, b0832, b0833 and b0834 from c:0010;0030;0050;0060;0070 to c:0010;0030;0060 (sheets unchanged), matching EBA v09836_m - v09840_m as reactivated on 2022-03-10. Keep boe_b0759 as it is.
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA originals are v09836_m - v09840_m on C 34.07 (band sums) and v09843_m ({c0070} * {c0010} = {c0060}, all rows), all severity Warning. In the v3.0 and v3.1 sheets of docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx the five band-sum rules have columns (All) and are deactivated on 2021-06-30. From release 3.2.0 they are marked 'Change+Reactivate' (reactivated 2022-03-10) with columns restricted to (0010;0030;0060) - the EBA's fix was exactly to drop the averaged and ratio columns. The Bank's scope (0010;0030;0050;0060;0070) drops c0020 and c0040 but keeps c0050 and c0070. Correction to the earlier investigation: these EBA rules are not simply 'deactivated'; the packaged extract crr-eba-v3.0-credit-risk.json reads the v3.0 sheet and so does not show the 3.2.0 change and reactivation. v09843_m is live in every release sheet.
issues.reach: Every firm that reports OF 34.07 with exposure in more than one PD band on any sheet - in practice every IRB firm with CCR exposures - from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions. Blocking, and unavoidable: the choice is between failing boe_b0830 - b0834 or failing boe_b0759.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: Slotting CCR exposures: six OF 34.07 = OF 08.01 rules on the two 'FIRB or slotting' sheets cannot hold together with boe_b0834, and Annex II paragraphs 75 and 130 disagree on whether OF 34.07 covers slotting
issues.requirement: On sheets 0002 (Total, FIRB or slotting) and 0010 (Specialised lending, FIRB or slotting), the OF 34.07 Total row must equal the sum of OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 for exposure value (boe_b0873, b0877), RWEA (b0855, b0859) and number of obligors (b0837, b0841); and boe_b0834 requires the same OF 34.07 Total row to equal the sum of its PD bands. All blocking.

authority.quote: In OF CR IRB 1, "FIRB/slotting" in cases where the FIRB approach or the slotting approach is applied, and "AIRB" in cases where the AIRB approach is applied. This includes all retail portfolios. In OF CR IRB 2, OF CR IRB 3, OF CR IRB 5 and OF 34.7, “FIRB” in cases where the FIRB approach is applied; and “AIRB” in cases where the AIRB approach is applied.

128. This template shall be reported by institutions using either the FIRB or AIRB Approach to compute risk-weighted exposure amounts for all or part of their CCR exposures [...] 130. In order to clarify whether the institution uses the FIRB or AIRB approach, the following information shall be provided for each reported exposure class: "FIRB or slotting" = in case the FIRB approach or the slotting approach are used.
CCR exposures (determined at counterparty level) shall be allocated to the appropriate bucket of the fixed PD scale based on the PD estimated for each obligor assigned to this exposure class
SPECIALISED LENDING SLOTTING APPROACH: TOTAL Exposures subject to the slotting approach. This shall only apply to the exposure sub-class ‘corporate – specialised lending’.

BREAKDOWN OF TOTAL EXPOSURES BY EXPOSURE CATEGORIES: [...] Exposures that are subject to counterparty credit risk shall be reported in rows 0040-0060 and, therefore, shall not be reported in this row.
OF WHICH: ARISING FROM COUNTERPARTY CREDIT RISK See OFCR SA instructions for column 0210.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: A swap with a specialised-lending borrower whose exposures are on the slotting approach is a CCR exposure: Annex II sends it to OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 on sheets 0010 and 0002 (it is part of the Total and of row 0080; OF 08.06 has an 'of which: arising from counterparty credit risk' column for it, and the Bank's boe_b0821 ties that column to OF 08.01 row 0080). OF 34.07 allocates exposures to PD buckets 'based on the PD estimated for each obligor'; under slotting no PD is estimated, so the exposure has no bucket. If it is left out of OF 34.07 (the reading of paragraph 75, which lists OF 34.7 as FIRB / AIRB only), the Total is short of OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 by the slotting CCR amount and the six cross-template rules fail. If it is included in the Total only (the reading of paragraph 130 and of the sheet labels 'FIRB approach or slotting approach'), the Total exceeds the sum of the PD bands and boe_b0834 fails. One blocking rule fails either way.

example.description: A bank with FIRB institutions and slotting specialised lending. Institutions (sheet 0006): 12 derivative counterparties, EV 600, RWEA 180. Specialised lending, all slotting (sheet 0010): 15 income-producing real-estate borrowers, loans EV 3,000 / RWEA 2,100 and an interest-rate swap each, EV 150 / RWEA 105 in total. OF 08.01 sheet 0010: r0010 3,150 / 2,205, r0020 3,000 / 2,100, r0050 150 / 105, r0080 3,150 / 2,205, 15 obligors on each row, c0130 = 150; sheet 0002 = 0006 + 0010 (r0050 EV 750, RWEA 285, 27 obligors). OF 08.06 r0095: EV 3,150, of which CCR 150, RWEA 2,205. OF 34.07 as filed in the failing return: institutions only on sheets 0006 and 0002 (EV 600, 12 obligors, RWEA 180), nothing on sheet 0010 because the slotting swaps have no PD bucket.

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Slotting swaps included in the OF 34.07 Total rows only, since they have no PD bucket (s_total_only): the six cross-template rules pass [1,0] each and boe_b0834 fails [6,8] - on sheets 0010 and 0002 the Total no longer equals the sum of the bands for exposure value, obligors, RWEA and density. (b) Slotting swaps allocated to a PD bucket (s_alt_invented_bucket): every rule passes (boe_b0834 [15,0], the six rules [1,0]), but no PD is estimated for a slotting exposure, so the bucket is invented and contradicts the row instruction on p.207. (c) Reporting the swaps outside OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 is excluded by the row 0020 instruction (p.115). There is no compliant way through.
issues.proposed_fix: First settle the instruction: state in Annex II whether OF 34.07 includes slotting CCR exposures (paragraph 75 says FIRB / AIRB only, paragraph 130 and the sheet labels say 'FIRB or slotting'). If they are excluded (the only reading the PD-scale rows can hold): for exposure value, subtract the slotting CCR amount - boe_b0877: {t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0180, c: 0010, z: 0010} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: 0110, z: 0010}) i- {t: OF08.01.01.02, r: 0080, c: 0130, z: 0010, dv: 0}, and the same on z: 0002 for boe_b0873; for RWEA and obligors (boe_b0855, b0859, b0837, b0841) OF 08.01 has no cell that isolates slotting CCR, so change 'i=' to 'i<=' or deactivate. If they are to be included, OF 34.07 needs a row for exposures without a PD and boe_b0834 must add it. A single change of 'i<=' with severity WARNING would cover the family, but should not lean on PI-08b, which remains an open question of interpretation.
issues.eba_precedent: Matched by sheet code, the EBA rules on s0002 (Total F-IRB) - v10522_h (c0030), v10539_h (c0060), v10701_h (c0010) - and on s0010 (Specialised lending F-IRB) - v10547_h (c0060), v10709_h (c0010) - were deactivated on 2021-09-10; v10530_h (c0030, s0010) was not deactivated. All are severity Warning and all are flagged Deleted from release 3.2 onward (docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx). The EBA does not publish its reason, and the same date also deactivated the three rules of sheet s0006 (institutions, F-IRB, which has no slotting): the pattern is the F-IRB sheets s0002 / s0006 / s0010, not specific evidence for this gap. The CRR Annex II text (docs/assets/crr-annex-ii-reporting-instructins.pdf p.185, para 130) labels the C 34.07 sheets 'NO' = Foundation IRB / 'YES' = Advanced IRB with no mention of slotting; PS1/26 paragraph 130 added 'or slotting'.
issues.reach: The claim as raised named all 51 rules; this population difference reaches six of them - boe_b0837, b0841, b0855, b0859, b0873, b0877 (sheets 0002 and 0010) - together with boe_b0834. It affects any firm with CCR exposures (typically hedging swaps) to specialised-lending borrowers on the slotting approach, from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions. Blocking and unavoidable for such a firm.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: CCP-cleared exposures: OF 34.07 excludes them, OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 do not, so the OF 34.07 = OF 08.01 rules fail for IRB-weighted client-clearing legs
issues.requirement: Per sheet, the OF 34.07 Total row must equal the sum of OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060: exposure value (17 rules, boe_b0872-b0889 and b1068), RWEA (17 rules, boe_b0854-b0871 and b1067) and number of obligors (the 17 rules listed under PI-07b-b). 51 blocking rules in all.

authority.quote: The template shall be reported separately for the total of all exposure classes as well as separately for each of the categories of exposures reported for template OF 08.01. This template excludes exposures cleared through a CCP.

authority.locator: OF 07.00 column 0211 (the instructions' own definition of the phrase)
authority.quote: Of which: Arising from Counterparty Credit Risk excluding exposures cleared through a CCP Exposures reported in column 0210 excluding those arising from contracts and transactions listed in Article 301(1) of the Counterparty Credit Risk (CRR) Part as long as they are outstanding with a central counterparty (CCP), including CCP-related transactions as defined in Rule 1.3 of that Part.

Institutions shall report the information on exposures to CCPs, i.e. to contracts and transactions listed in Article 301(1) CRR for as long as they are outstanding with a CCP and exposures from CCP-related transactions, in accordance with Article 300(2) CRR, for which the own funds requirements are calculated in accordance with Section 9 of Chapter 6 of Title II of Part Three CRR.

authority.locator: Credit Risk: General Provisions (CRR) Part, Article 107(2)
authority.quote: For trade exposures and for default fund contributions to a central counterparty, institutions shall apply the treatment set out in Section 9 of Chapter 3 of Counterparty Credit Risk (CRR) Part to calculate their risk-weighted exposure amounts
Exposures / Transactions subject to counterparty credit risk See the corresponding OFCR SA instructions in rows 0090-0130.
Transactions subject to counterparty credit risk, i.e. derivative instruments, securities financing transactions and long settlement transactions.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: A clearing member's exposure to its client on a cleared derivative is a CCP-related transaction. It is capitalised as a bilateral exposure to the client, so an IRB firm risk-weights it under the IRB approach and reports it in OF 08.01 on the client's sheet, in row 0050 (rows 0020 / 0030 exclude CCR, and rows 0040-0060 carry no CCP exclusion). OF 34.07 'excludes exposures cleared through a CCP', a phrase Annex II itself defines, in OF 07.00 column 0211, as including CCP-related transactions. So OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 = bilateral + cleared, OF 34.07 Total = bilateral only, and every one of the three equalities on that sheet fails by the cleared amount. OF 07.00 has column 0211 to carve these exposures out; OF 08.01 has no counterpart column, so the difference cannot be reconciled from reported data.

example.description: Financial corporates and large corporates (FIRB), sheet 0022. A clearing member has bilateral derivatives with 8 clients (EV 400, RWEA 200) and client-cleared derivatives with 6 other clients (EV 250, RWEA 125), all risk-weighted under FIRB. OF 08.01 r0010 = r0050 = r0070: EV 650, RWEA 325, 14 obligors. OF 34.07 (cleared exposures excluded): one PD band and the Total with EV 400, 8 obligors, RWEA 200, density 0.50. The rules compute 400 against 650, 200 against 325 and 8 against 14.

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Including the cleared client legs in OF 34.07 (c_alt_include_cleared): all three rules pass [1,0], but that contradicts paragraph 129. (b) Leaving them out of OF 08.01 rows 0040-0060 is not open: they are IRB-weighted exposures that belong to the sheet Total, and row 0020 / 0030 instructions send CCR exposures to rows 0040-0060. (c) A narrow reading of paragraph 129 - only trades outstanding with the CCP itself, which are not IRB-weighted - would remove the gap; only OF 07.00 column 0211 (p.86) supports the broad reading. C 34.02 paragraph 124 (p.190) and C 34.10 paragraph 132 (p.210) include CCP-related transactions only where the own funds requirements are calculated under Section 9, which excludes clearing-member-to-client exposures (Article 304(1): Sections 1 to 8); OF 07.00 row 0100 (p.94) is drafted the same way; and Article 107(2) supports the narrow reading, since Section 9 exposures are not IRB-weighted. Under the narrow reading the example with the client legs included passes all three rules: this is an open question of interpretation for the Bank. This is why confidence is medium, not high.
issues.proposed_fix: OF 08.01 has no cell that isolates cleared exposures (OF 07.00 has column 0211; OF 08.01 has no counterpart), so the equality cannot be restored from reported data. In all 51 rules replace 'i=' by 'i<=' ({t: OF34.07.01.01, r: 0180, c: C, z: S} i<= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: C', z: S})) and set severity WARNING; or deactivate them, as the EBA has (Warning from the start, deleted from release 3.2). Alternatively, and only with a taxonomy change, add to OF 08.01 an 'of which: excluding exposures cleared through a CCP' column on the pattern of OF 07.00 c0211 and point the rules at it.
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA equivalents are v10521_h - v10537_h (obligors), v10538_h - v10554_h (RWEA) and v10700_h - v10716_h (exposure value): 51 rules, added in release 3.0.0, all severity Warning. In the v3.0 / v3.1 sheets of docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx eight are deactivated on 2021-09-10 (v10522_h, v10526_h, v10539_h, v10543_h, v10547_h, v10701_h, v10705_h, v10709_h - sheets 0002 Total F-IRB, 0006 Institutions F-IRB and 0010 Specialised lending F-IRB) and five on 2022-12-12 (v10523_h, v10524_h, v10540_h, v10703_h, v10711_h); in the sheets for releases 3.2 to 3.5 all 51 are flagged Deleted = y. Matched by sheet, the Bank's live ERROR rules boe_b0837, b0855, b0873 (0002), b1035, b1067, b1068 (0006), b0859, b0877 (0010) and b0882 (0012, 2022-12-12) restate rules the EBA had deactivated. The Bank's v4.0.0 workbook lists an EBA equivalent for 45 of the 51 (none for boe_b0853, b0871, b0889, b1035, b1067, b1068), but pairs them by position rather than by sheet - the earlier investigation's list (b0837, b0841, b0855, b0859, b0863, b0873, b0877, b0881, b0883) used that pairing and should be replaced by the sheet-matched list above. The same exclusion sentence is in the current CRR instructions (crr-annex-ii-reporting-instructins.pdf p.185, para 129), so the gap is inherited, not new in PS1/26.
issues.reach: Any IRB firm that risk-weights CCP-related transactions under the IRB approach: clearing members' exposures to clients, and clients' exposures to clearing members where the 2% / 4% treatment is not available. All 51 rules in principle, on whichever sheet the counterparty sits (institutions 0006, financial and large corporates 0022, other corporates, and the Totals 0001 / 0002). Blocking from the first PRA001 return under the PS1/26 instructions.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: Average maturity is integer-typed: OF 08.01 / OF 08.02 c0250 (days) and OF 08.03 c0080 / OF 34.07 c0050 (years) must be filed as whole numbers
issues.requirement: No validation rule is at fault. The taxonomy dictionary types the two maturity metrics as integers: eba_met:ii163 'Maturity value (days)' is the only metric of OF 08.01 c0250 (306 cells) and OF 08.02 c0250 (17), and eba_met:ii791 'Maturity value (years)' of OF 08.03 c0080 (306) and OF 34.07 c0050 (323). An integer item cannot carry a fraction, and the Bank's filing manual gives decimals 0 for an integer (it also accepts INF, 'exact as written', for every numeric type).

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 column 0250
authority.quote: The value reported shall be determined in accordance with Article 162 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted averages. The average maturity shall be reported in days.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.02 columns
authority.quote: Instructions for each of these columns are the same as for the corresponding numbered columns in OF CR IRB 1 template.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.03 column 0080
authority.quote: The maturity value reported shall be determined in accordance with Article 162 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. The average maturity shall be reported in years.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 34.07 column 0050
authority.quote: Average of obligor maturities in years weighted by their corresponding exposure value as defined for column 0010.

authority.locator: 30 May 2024 (bankofengland.co.uk, xbrl-filing-manual-april-2024) - rule 2.18, Accuracy Requirements table (one row: Data Type / Decimals setting / Note / Example)
authority.quote: Integer 0 Must be reported without any decimal part 126
Integers must be reported as whole numbers and without any decimals (rule 2.18).

Note however that if numbers are for any reason rounded, they MUST be rounded as per the XBRL 2.1 specification (i.e. [IEEE-754] 4.3.1 Rounding-direction attributes to nearest, roundTiesToEven), and as above the decimals setting must accurately represent the relationship between the reported and unrounded values.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: It does not, provided the figure is rounded. Tested in Arelle: a fractional literal in either metric (912.5 days, 2.5 years) is an XML Schema validity error (xmlSchema:valueError, level ERROR) - the instance is not valid XBRL - and every formula that reads the fact aborts with err:FORG0001; stating decimals="2" on it adds filing-rule error EBA.2.18 ('Integer fact eba_met:ii163 of context c3 has a decimals attribute ≠ 0'). The same return with whole numbers (912 days and 2 years under the rounding the Filing Manual's rule 2.18 prescribes, roundTiesToEven; Arelle accepts any integer) with decimals="0" loads with no message and every rule evaluates. So the claim 'contradicts Annex II and blocks filing' is too strong: Annex II fixes the unit (days / years) and no precision, the taxonomy fixes whole units, and the two are reconciled by rounding half-to-even as rule 2.18 prescribes. What is left for the Bank: (1) Annex II never says the average is rounded, so a firm discovers it from an XBRL validity error; (2) for the two YEARS cells a whole number is close to uninformative - an average of 2.5 years is filed as 2, of 3.4 as 3; in DAYS the loss is at most half a day and is immaterial.
issues.alternatives_considered: (1) The fraction with decimals=0: XBRL-invalid (xmlSchema:valueError). (2) The fraction with decimals=2: invalid, plus EBA.2.18. (3) The value rounded to a whole unit with decimals=0: accepted - this is the compliant way and the only one. (4) Leaving the cell empty: no rule requires c0250 / c0080 / c0050 to be present, so it would pass, but Annex II asks for the figure. There is no decimal-typed alternative data point for any of the four cells.
issues.proposed_fix: No rule change. (1) Add to Annex II, at OF 08.01 c0250 (p.111), OF 08.03 c0080 (p.121) and OF 34.07 c0050 (p.207): 'The average shall be reported as a whole number of days / years, rounded to the nearest whole unit (ties to even).' (2) For the two cells in YEARS, preferably replace eba_met:ii791 with a decimal metric (xbrli:decimalItemType - the dictionary already has decimal metrics such as eba_met:ri769 and the Bank's own boe_met:ri10063) so that an average of 2.5 years can be reported as such; the Bank already mints its own metrics for these templates (boe_met:pi10057 on OF 08.03 c0050 and OF 34.07 c0020).
issues.eba_precedent: The metrics are the EBA's own (ii163 in force since 2013-12-01, ii791 since 2021-06-30), so EU COREP has the same constraint. In EBA Q&A 2026_7840 (submitted 23/04/2026, rejected 15/10/2026) a bank wrote: 'as the Maturity is required to be rounded to full days and cannot be delivered with decimals, the rule cannot be met as the rounding will cause a difference between the templates'; Q&A 2026_7881 asked 'should the column 250 of the C.08.01 and C.08.02 be reported as integers or decimals?'. Both were rejected because the matter 'has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version of the Reporting framework / release of the respective validation rules'. No EBA answer says how to round.
issues.reach: Every IRB firm filing PRA001 from the first 2027 reference date, on OF 08.01, OF 08.02, OF 08.03 and OF 34.07. No return is rejected if the average is rounded.
issues.meanwhile: No validation result shows this issue. Report as the instructions require; the issue is recorded for the Bank's attention.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.03 column 0030
authority.quote: For all exposures included in each bucket of the fixed PD range, the average conversion factor used by institutions in their calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts, weighted by the off-balance sheet exposure pre-CCF as reported in column 0020.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - C 34.02 column 0140
authority.quote: The value of α is fixed as 1.4 in the rows for OEM in accordance with Articles 282(2) of the CCR Part of the PRA Rulebook.

Facts that represent amounts in any currency will be of an item that is derived from xbrli:monetaryItemType, which must follow the restriction in XBRL 2.1, section 4.8.2, regarding monetaryItemType (i.e., unit measure is an ISO 4217 currency designation).

E.g. decimals setting of greater than 2 would generally be inappropriate for calculated “monetary” values resulting from e.g. multiplications or divisions, “INF” is often unlikely to be appropriate for calculated values.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: It does not. Arelle (filing rules on) accepts <eba_met:mi796 unitRef=GBP decimals="4">0.4</> and <eba_met:mi784 unitRef=GBP decimals="2">1.4</> with no message; the same facts with the pure unit are XBRL-invalid (xbrl.4.8.2:monetaryFactUnit-notMonetaryMeasure, ERROR, plus the WARNING EBA.2.23). So a firm must file a conversion factor of 0.38 as 'GBP 0.38' and alpha as 'GBP 1.4'. Two sub-claims of the original finding do not hold as stated: (a) 'a +/-500 rounding allowance makes every CCF rule vacuous' is true only when the fact is stated at decimals=-3 (the filing manual's minimum for monetary, and a house default applied to every monetary fact): r0070 = 0.38 against r0080 + r0090 = 0.30 + 0.50 satisfies boe_b0768 at decimals=-3 [2,0] and breaks it at decimals=2 [1,1]; (b) v10633_m is a plain '>=' and is unaffected by the type - alpha 1.0 is unsatisfied at decimals=-3 and at 2 alike. The real cost of the typing is that the stated accuracy of a ratio is governed by money conventions: footnote 11 calls more than 2 decimals 'generally inappropriate' for a calculated monetary value, which discourages stating an average conversion factor more precisely than +/-0.005 (the SHOULD is in rule 2.18(c); the footnote is an example, and Arelle accepts decimals=4 on the fact with no message).
issues.alternatives_considered: Pure unit: invalid XBRL (tested). Percent scale (38 instead of 0.38): no instruction supports it and every PRA001 rule compares ratios as fractions. A different data point: none exists for either cell. Stating decimals=4: accepted by Arelle, but discouraged by the SHOULD of rule 2.18(c), which footnote 11 illustrates.
issues.proposed_fix: Retype the two data points: OF 08.03 c0030 to a percentage metric (num:percentItemType, pure unit, decimals >= 4 - e.g. a new boe_met:pi... as the Bank did with boe_met:pi10057) and C 34.02 c0140 to a decimal metric (xbrli:decimalItemType, as boe_met:ri10063 'Internal loss multiplier value'). Until then, state in Annex II or the filing manual the accuracy at which these two monetary-typed ratios are to be filed (decimals >= 2, or >= 4), since the general monetary minimum of -3 is meaningless for them. The same pattern elsewhere in the taxonomy: eba_met:mi663 'Exposure-weighted average maturity of assets' (C 14.00 c0204) and boe_met:mi10009 'mCVA multiplier' (OF 25.03 c0030) are also monetary.
issues.eba_precedent: Both metrics are the EBA's (created 2020-11-15, in force 2021-06-30), so EU COREP C 08.03 c0030 and C 34.02 c0140 carry the same typing. The same dictionary types a conversion factor correctly elsewhere: eba_met:pi370 'Credit conversion factor' is num:percentItemType. No EBA Q&A on the point was found.
issues.reach: Every IRB firm with off-balance-sheet exposure (OF 08.03 c0030) and every IMM firm (C 34.02 r0040 c0140 is the only alpha cell the taxonomy publishes). Nothing is rejected. On our returns: cosmetic today, and it hides three ERROR rules on c0030.
issues.meanwhile: No validation result shows this issue. Report as the instructions require; the issue is recorded for the Bank's attention.

issues.title: OF 09.02 row 0105 (retail purchased receivables) cannot carry original exposure, exposure value or RWEA on the all-countries sheet: the retail roll-up and the OF 08.01 sheet ties force those columns to zero
issues.requirement: boe_b0783 requires OF 09.02 row 0060 (Retail) to equal the sum of rows 0071, 0072, 0073, 0074, 0100, 0105, 0120 and 0130 in each of the twelve monetary columns, on every country sheet. boe_b0291 / b0292 / b0293 require row 0060 on the all-countries sheet to equal the sum of row 0010 across the seven OF 08.01 retail sheets (0015-0021) for original exposure, exposure value and RWEA. A further 22 rules (boe_b0294-b0302, b0304, b1056-b1066, b1071; 21 distinct, because boe_b0304 and boe_b1057 are the same expression) require each of the seven other retail rows to equal row 0010 of exactly one OF 08.01 sheet in those three columns. No rule ties row 0105 to anything in OF 08.01.

authority.locator: Bank of England Banking taxonomy v4.1.1 package (.taxonomy/boe-banking-v411.zip): dict/dom/eba_ec/mem-lab-en.xml and tab/of09.02.01.01 (row hierarchy and data points)
authority.quote: Retail exposures - purchased receivables

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Take the all-countries sheet and one of the three tied column pairs (OF 09.02 c0010 / c0105 / c0110 against OF 08.01 c0020 / c0110 / c0260). Write S15 ... S21 for row 0010 of the seven OF 08.01 retail sheets. (1) boe_b0783: r0060 = r0071 + r0072 + r0073 + r0074 + r0100 + r0105 + r0120 + r0130. (2) boe_b0291 / b0292 / b0293: r0060 = S15 + S16 + S17 + S18 + S19 + S20 + S21. (3) Seven one-row-one-sheet equalities: r0100 = S15, r0120 = S16, r0130 = S17, r0073 = S18, r0074 = S19, r0071 = S20, r0072 = S21. Putting (3) into (1) and comparing with (2) leaves r0105 = 0: nine evaluations per column (ten for RWEA, where boe_b0304 and boe_b1057 both evaluate), and no step depends on how the firm reads Annex II. A purchased retail receivable has to sit in one of S15 ... S21: Article 147(2)(d) gives retail exactly three subclasses and purchased receivables are not one of them (they are a roll-out class, Art. 147B(1)(g)); Annex II para 76 lists no purchased-receivables sheet; and OF 08.01 row 0175 shows them inside each class sheet. In the taxonomy, row 0105 carries its own exposure-class member (boe_eba_EC:x10011, 'Retail exposures - purchased receivables') and sits beside rows 0100 / 0120 / 0130 under 'Retail' with no 'Of which' label, while no OF 08.01 sheet carries that member. So with r0105 above zero one of three things gives way: the class row is reported net of the receivables and no longer equals its sheet (boe_b0300-b0302 in the example); or it is reported gross and r0060 no longer equals the sum of its rows (boe_b0783); or r0060 is inflated to make the sum work and no longer equals the OF 08.01 sheets (boe_b0291-b0293). The effect is confined to original exposure, exposure value and RWEA on the all-countries sheet; the other nine monetary columns of row 0105 and the individual country sheets are subject to boe_b0783 only. The equalities use interval arithmetic, so 'zero' means zero within the rounding allowance of the reported decimals.

example.description: AIRB firm, all obligors in one country, so only the all-countries sheet of OF 09.02 is due (Annex II para 85). Retail book: qualifying revolving 500 original exposure / 400 exposure value / 120 RWEA (OF 08.01 sheet 0015); other retail non-SME 1,000 / 1,000 / 400 (sheet 0017), of which 100 / 100 / 60 are purchased retail receivables risk-weighted under Art. 154(5) and so 'other retail' under Art. 147(5C). OF 08.01: sheet 0017 r0010 = 1,000 / 1,000 / 400 and r0175 = 100 / 100 / 60; AIRB total sheet 0001 r0010 = 1,500 / 1,400 / 520 and r0175 = 100 / 100 / 60. OF 09.02 all countries, columns 0010 / 0105 / 0110: r0060 = 1,500 / 1,400 / 520; r0100 = 500 / 400 / 120; r0105 = 100 / 100 / 60; r0130 = 900 / 900 / 340 (other retail net of the receivables shown in row 0105); r0150 = r0060. Arelle: boe_b0300, b0301, b0302 each [0 satisfied, 1 unsatisfied]; every other evaluated rule satisfied. A second set with all seven retail sheets populated (retfull_*.json) makes every rule of the certificate evaluate, with the same result.

issues.alternatives_considered: Four other ways to report the same position, each run through Arelle. (B) Row 0105 as an 'of which' of other retail - r0130 = 1,000 gross, r0105 = 100, r0060 = 1,500: boe_b0783 [0,3], everything else satisfied. (C) As B with r0060 raised to 1,600 / 1,500 / 580 so the rows add up: boe_b0291, b0292, b0293 [0,1] each. (D) Receivables kept out of every OF 08.01 retail class sheet (sheet 0017 = 900, only the AIRB total sheet carries them): boe_b0291-b0293 [0,1] each, and it is not what para 76 or row 0175 describe. (Z) Row 0105 left empty: passes, but omits the figure Annex II asks for in row 0105. Reporting row 0105 only on country sheets, or only in the nine columns without a sheet tie, would leave original exposure, exposure value and RWEA at zero on the all-countries sheet for a row that has exposure. The same algebra applies if the receivables qualify as qualifying revolving or property-secured retail (sheets 0015, 0018-0021): the tie that breaks is then boe_b0294-b0296 or the b1056-b1066 / b1071 family. None of the alternatives is both Annex-II-compliant and rule-satisfying.
issues.proposed_fix: State in Annex II whether OF 09.02 row 0105 is a separate breakdown row (rows 0071-0074, 0100, 0120 and 0130 reported net of purchased receivables) or an 'of which' row, then align the rules. Fix A - row 0105 stays a separate row, as the template hierarchy, its own exposure-class member (boe_eba_EC:x10011) and boe_b0783 already treat it: subtract the same sheet's row 0175 in each one-row-one-sheet rule. boe_b0300 becomes {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0130, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0020, z: 0017, dv: 0, id: v1} i- {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0017, dv: 0, id: v2}; make the same change in boe_b0294-b0299, b0301, b0302, b0304, b1056-b1066 and b1071 (column pairs c0010/c0020, c0105/c0110, c0110/c0260), and add the missing tie for the row itself: {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0105, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0015; 0016; 0017; 0018; 0019; 0020; 0021, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}), with its c0105/c0110 and c0110/c0260 twins. boe_b0783 and boe_b0291-b0293 stay as they are. Fix B - row 0105 is an 'of which' row: remove 0105 from boe_b0783, i.e. {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0060, dv: 0, id: v0} i= isum({t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0071; 0072; 0073; 0074; 0100; 0120; 0130, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}); keep boe_b0336 (r0060 >= r0105); label the row 'Of which: purchased receivables'. Under either fix, say whether dilution-risk amounts (OF 08.01 row 0180) belong in row 0105, since its definition cites Article 157. Separately, boe_b0304 and boe_b1057 are the same expression; one can be withdrawn.
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA's C 09.02 has no purchased-receivables row (EBA v3.0 rule list held in the repo, retrieved 2026-08-01). In the BoE v4.0.0 extract, boe_b0783 is mapped to EBA v2245_h ({r0060} = +{r0110} + {r0100} + {r0070}), which the EBA list marks deactivated (2014-05-19); boe_b0291 and boe_b0300 are mapped to v0440_m and v0475_m, both with status 'deactivated' in that list; boe_b0336 is mapped to v4778_m ({r0060} >= {r0110}, the EBA 'other retail' row); boe_b1056-b1066 and b1071 have no EBA equivalent. The picture is of row 0105 added to an inherited roll-up without the inherited sheet ties being adjusted - an inference, not something the Bank has stated. Not on the Bank's known-issues logs of 27 August and 16 November 2026.
issues.reach: Every firm with IRB permission that holds purchased retail receivables under the IRB approach (roll-out class Art. 147B(1)(g)), from the first PRA001 return under PS1/26 (reference dates from 1 January 2027). Every firm that files OF 09.02: Annex II para 85 makes the all-countries sheet due from every institution, though Reporting (CRR) Part Chapter 5 Article 5(5) (PS1/26 Appendix 1 p.481) can be read as gating the whole template on the 10% non-domestic threshold. ERROR severity.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

authority.locator: Bank of England Banking taxonomy v4.1.1 package (.taxonomy/boe-banking-v411.zip): dict/dom/eba_ec/mem-lab-en.xml and tab/of09.02.01.01 (row hierarchy and data points)
authority.quote: Exposures to corporates - purchased receivables

issues.why_correct_return_fails: On the all-countries sheet, for each of original exposure, exposure value and RWEA, write S9 ... S24 for row 0010 of the OF 08.01 corporate sheets. (1) boe_b0785: r0030 = r0042 + r0045 + r0048 + r0049 + r0050 + r0055. (2) boe_b0282 / b0283 / b0284: r0030 = S9 + S10 + S11 + S12 + S22 + S23 + S24. (3) r0048 = S22, r0050 = S23 + S24, r0055 = S11 / S12. Substituting leaves r0049 = (S9 + S10) - r0042 - r0045. That is the 'cap' the earlier review reported, but it is not a real allowance: rows 0042 and 0045 together are all IRB specialised lending, and sheets 0009 and 0010 together are the same population, so on a truthful return r0042 + r0045 = S9 + S10 and r0049 = 0 - with or without specialised lending on the book. A purchased corporate receivable is in one of the corporate class sheets (Art. 147(2)(c) has three subclasses and purchased receivables are not one of them; para 76 lists no sheet for them; OF 08.01 row 0175 shows them inside each sheet). For row 0055 Annex II is explicit - it is what is 'not reported in 0042-0050' - while rows 0048 and 0050 (pp.143-144) have no such carve-out, so for receivables of SME or financial / large corporate obligors the text has the same gap as for retail; so the receivables go in row 0049 and row 0055 is reported net of them - and then boe_b1053-b1055 fail because row 0055 no longer equals the whole sheet. Reported the other way round (row 0055 gross), boe_b0785 fails. The only shape that satisfies every rule with r0049 above zero understates row 0042 or row 0045 by exactly the receivables amount (run corp_E2). Confined to the three tied columns on the all-countries sheet; interval arithmetic, so zero within the rounding allowance.

example.description: FIRB firm, all obligors in one country. Corporate book: financial corporates and large corporates 500 original exposure / 450 exposure value / 300 RWEA (OF 08.01 sheet 0022); other general corporates non-SME 1,000 / 1,000 / 700 (sheet 0012), of which 100 / 100 / 80 are purchased corporate receivables (Art. 153(6)). OF 08.01: sheet 0012 r0010 = 1,000 / 1,000 / 700 and r0175 = 100 / 100 / 80; FIRB total sheet 0002 r0010 = 1,500 / 1,450 / 1,000 and r0175 = 100 / 100 / 80. OF 09.02 all countries, columns 0010 / 0105 / 0110, as Annex II rows 0049 and 0055 are written: r0030 = 1,500 / 1,450 / 1,000; r0048 = 500 / 450 / 300; r0049 = 100 / 100 / 80; r0055 = 900 / 900 / 620 (what is 'not reported in 0042-0050'); r0150 = r0030. Arelle: boe_b1053, b1054, b1055 each [0 satisfied, 1 unsatisfied]; every other evaluated rule satisfied. Only sheet 0012 (not 0011) is populated so that the missing isum in boe_b1053-b1055 plays no part.

issues.alternatives_considered: Five other ways to report the same position, each run through Arelle. (B) Row 0049 as an 'of which' of row 0055 - r0055 = 1,000 gross, r0049 = 100, r0030 = 1,500: boe_b0785 [0,3], everything else satisfied. (C) As B with r0030 raised to 1,600 / 1,550 / 1,080: boe_b0282, b0283, b0284 [0,1] each. (D) Receivables kept out of every OF 08.01 corporate class sheet (sheet 0012 = 900, only the FIRB total sheet carries them): boe_b0282-b0284 [0,1] each, and not what para 76 or row 0175 describe. (E1) The firm also has 300 / 300 / 240 of slotting specialised lending on sheet 0010, reported truthfully as r0045, with r0049 = 100 beside r0055 = 1,000: boe_b0785 [0,3] - having specialised lending does not create room. (E2) As E1 but r0045 understated to 200 / 200 / 160: every rule satisfied. This is the 'cap' - it passes only by misstating specialised lending by the receivables amount, and still counts the receivables in both row 0049 and row 0055. (Z) Row 0049 left empty: passes, but omits the figure Annex II asks for. None of the alternatives is both Annex-II-compliant and rule-satisfying.
issues.proposed_fix: Fix A - matches Annex II as written for row 0055 (what is 'not reported in 0042-0050'; rows 0048 and 0050 would need the same carve-out) and the template, where row 0049 is a sibling row with its own exposure-class member (boe_eba_EC:x10013): subtract row 0175 of the same sheets in each class-row tie. boe_b1053 becomes {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0055, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0020, z: 0011; 0012, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}) i- isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0011; 0012, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v2}) - which also supplies the isum the rule lacks today; the same for boe_b1054 and b1055 (c0105/c0110, c0110/c0260); boe_b0288-b0290 with z: 0023; 0024; boe_b1034, b1051, b1052 with z: 0022. Add the missing tie for the row itself: {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0049, c: 0010, dv: 0, filter: dim(this(), [eba_dim:CEG]) = [eba_GA:x1], id: v0} i= isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0175, c: 0020, z: 0009; 0010; 0011; 0012; 0022; 0023; 0024, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}), with its exposure-value and RWEA twins. boe_b0785 and boe_b0282-b0284 stay as they are. Fix B - if 'of which' is what the Bank intends: remove 0049 from boe_b0785, i.e. {t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0030, id: v0} i= isum({t: OF09.02.01.01, r: 0042; 0045; 0048; 0050; 0055, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True, id: v1}); keep boe_b1050 (r0030 >= r0049); and amend Annex II row 0055 so it no longer excludes row 0049. Either way, tie row 0045 to OF 08.01 (today it has no cross-template rule, which is what leaves the E2 loophole open), and say whether dilution-risk amounts (OF 08.01 row 0180) belong in row 0049.

issues.title: boe_b1043 ties the slotting FCCM change (OF 08.06 c0031) to off-balance-sheet exposure, and boe_b1042 equates exposure value with a pre-conversion-factor amount

issues.why_correct_return_fails: boe_b1043. Write F for the summed OF 08.06 r0095 c0031 and X for the slotting off-balance-sheet exposure before conversion factors (OF 08.01.01.02 r0080 c0100, shown on both sheets 0002 and 0010, so the rule's right-hand side is 2X x 0.5 = X). The rule demands F = X. boe_b1044 makes every c0031 cell <= 0, so F <= 0; boe_b0315_2 makes c0100 >= 0, so X >= 0. The three hold together only when F = 0 and X = 0, and boe_b0818 then forces column 0030 to zero as well. So a return passes only if the firm has no off-balance-sheet slotting exposure at all AND reports no FCCM effect at all. Any undrawn slotting commitment (X > 0, F = 0) fails it; any slotting loan with financial collateral under the FCCM (F < 0, X = 0) fails it. The two quantities are unrelated: c0031 is a reduction for collateral, c0100 is an 'of which' of exposure. The right-hand side is boe_b0818's, apparently carried over when the rule was written. The matching OF 08.01 quantity is c0101 + c0102 on row 0080 (boe_b1040: c0104 = c0090 + c0101 + c0102). boe_b1042. Column 0040 is the exposure value under Articles 166A-166D, i.e. after conversion factors (Art. 166C(1)); column 0020 is before conversion factors; column 0031 is, by its instruction, only the FCCM reduction. For an undrawn commitment of nominal N with conversion factor CF and no collateral: c0020 = N, c0031 = 0, c0040 = CF x N. The rule needs CF x N = N, true only at CF = 100%. Table A1 gives 40%, 50%, 20% and 10% for the commitments and trade items a specialised-lending book normally holds. The Bank's own OF 07.00 rule boe_b0471 (c0200 = c0150 - 0.9 c0160 - 0.8 c0170 - 0.6 c0171 - 0.5 c0180) applies conversion factors between the pre-CF and post-CF columns; boe_b1042 has no such term.

(2) Report c0031 = +1,000 so boe_b1043 holds (A3): b1043 [1,0] but boe_b1044 [0,2], boe_b0311 [0,2] and boe_b1042 [0,2]; and a positive figure contradicts the '(-)' label and the column's definition. issues.why_correct_return_fails: Signs first. The '(-)' label and paragraph 9 make both columns non-positive; boe_b0699 (c0150 = c0110 + c0120 + c0130) and boe_b1040 (c0104 = c0090 + c0101 + c0102) make the Cvam column a deduction, so c0130 = c0102 = -Cvam; Annex II gives the other column as (Cvam - C), which is <= 0 because haircuts and the maturity factor only reduce collateral. Collateral C = 100: with Cvam = 80, c0130 = -80 and c0140 = -20, and -80 <= -20 is TRUE. With Cvam = 19.6, c0130 = -19.6 and c0140 = -80.4, and -19.6 <= -80.4 is FALSE. In general -Cvam <= Cvam - C exactly when Cvam >= C/2 (Arelle: satisfied at Cvam = 80 and at the boundary 50, unsatisfied at 46.26 and 19.6). The rule reads 'of which' as 'part of', but the adjustment is not a part of Cvam: it is the difference between the collateral's value and Cvam, and the two are complements that sum to -C. Nothing in the definitions bounds one by the other. Realistic ways to fall below C/2: (a) a maturity mismatch - Art. 239(2) scales by (t - 0.25)/(T - 0.25), which is 0.2 for 1.2 years of protection against an exposure of five years or more, and below one half whenever t is under about 2.6 years against five; (b) haircuts alone - a secured loan (20-day liquidation period) against listed non-main-index equity in another currency takes 42.426% + 11.314% = 53.74%, leaving Cvam = 46.26% of C. A second route exists at smaller haircuts: where collateral exceeds the exposure, c0130 has to be capped at the exposure for boe_b0699 to hold with E* floored at zero, and the calculated adjustment can then exceed the capped figure (run C8: exposure 100, main-index equity 400 at 28.284%: c0130 -100, c0140 -113.14, unsatisfied although Cvam is 72% of C).

example.description: Two positions in one return, each with collateral C = 100 and Cvam = 19.6 (a 2% volatility adjustment and a maturity factor (1.2 - 0.25)/(5 - 0.25) = 0.2: 100 x 0.98 x 0.2). (1) Standardised corporate loan of 1,000, FCCM: OF 07.00 sheet 0008 row 0010: c0010 1,000; c0040 1,000; c0110 1,000; c0120 0; c0130 -19.6; c0140 -80.4; c0150 980.4; c0200 980.4; c0220 980.4. (2) Slotting project-finance loan of 1,000 (Good, 2.5 years or more), FCCM: OF 08.01 sheet 0010 row 0080: c0020 1,000; c0090 1,000; c0101 0; c0102 -19.6; c0103 -80.4; c0104 980.4; c0110 980.4; c0260 882.36. Arelle: boe_b0555 [0,1] and boe_b1036 [0,1]; the arithmetic and sign rules on the same cells all pass. The same two positions with Cvam = 80 (c0130 / c0102 = -80, c0140 / c0103 = -20) pass both rules. Fuller returns with total sheet 0001, row 0070, OF 08.01 rows 0010 / 0020 on both sheets and OF 08.06 give boe_b0555 [0,4] and boe_b1036 [0,6] against [4,0] and [6,0]. A version built only from Article 224 table figures - listed non-index equity in another currency, 20-day period, Cvam = 46.26, no maturity mismatch - is also unsatisfied on both (runs C3: b0555 [0,4]; B4: b1036 [0,6]).

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) Report the adjustment as a positive number (+80.4): boe_b0555 becomes [4,0] but boe_b0733 fails [4,4] (run C6); on OF 08.01 boe_b1036 becomes [6,0] but boe_b1038, an ERROR, fails [0,6] (run B6); and paragraph 9 expects no positive figure under a '(-)' label. (2) Leave the 'of which' column blank: both rules pass because the missing cell defaults to 0 (C4: b0555 [4,0]; B5: b1036 [6,0]) - but that omits a figure Annex II asks for whenever a haircut or maturity mismatch applies; the rule rewards not reporting it. (3) Report Cvam before the cap, or scale the adjustment down with the cap: no instruction supports either, and an uncapped c0130 breaks boe_b0699 on an over-collateralised exposure. (4) Positive c0130: breaks boe_b0699 / b1040 and the sign rules. No compliant reporting of a position with Cvam below C/2 satisfies the rules.
issues.proposed_fix: Deactivate boe_b0555 and boe_b1036, as the EBA did with v0008_h on 9 September 2015. No inequality between the two columns follows from their Annex II definitions: c0130 + c0140 = -C says only that both are non-positive, which boe_b0733 (OF 07.00 c0130, c0140 <= 0) and boe_b1037 / boe_b1038 / boe_b0306 (OF 08.01 c0102, c0103 <= 0) already check, and the arithmetic is checked by boe_b0699 and boe_b1040. If the Bank keeps boe_b1036 while it reviews, lower it from ERROR to WARNING so that it matches boe_b0555 and cannot reject a correct return.

issues.reach: Every firm that uses IMM exposure values in BA-CVA and is in scope of the output floor, on every PRA001 return from the first Basel 3.1 reference date (1 January 2027 onwards), whenever the IMM-based and SA-CCR-based BA-CVA figures differ. issues.title: boe_b1076 (and boe_b1075) have no guard for a return that does not complete column 0020, so SA-CVA / AA-CVA / BA-CVA firms outside the output floor's scope get a warning
issues.requirement: This is a NEW facet found while rechecking PI-13, not part of the original claim. b1076 compares the standardised-only CVA total (r0640 c0020, default 0) with two operands that exist only in column 0010 (r0641 SA-CVA and r0643 AA-CVA). A firm that reports SA-CVA or AA-CVA in column 0010 and nothing in column 0020 is therefore told 0 = its CVA figure.

authority.quote: The columns Standardised approaches only (Output floor) (0020) and Standardised approaches including multiplier (Output Floor) (0030) are a requirement for Internal Multiplier (IM) firms in scope of the Basel 3.1 standards:

authority.locator: Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part, Article 92(2A)(c)
authority.quote: for the purposes of complying with the obligations of this Part on an individual basis, the total risk exposure amount of a ring-fenced body that is a member of a sub-consolidation group and an institution which is not a stand-alone institution in the UK shall be the un-floored total risk exposure amount calculated in accordance with paragraph 3;
1.6.3. Alternative Approach (AA) Own funds requirements for credit valuation adjustment risk in accordance with Chapter 6 of the Credit Valuation Adjustment Risk Part of the PRA Rulebook.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Annex II makes column 0020 a requirement only for IM firms in scope of the floor. A firm outside that scope (a non-IM firm, or a solo return of a UK subsidiary under Art. 92(2A)(c)) that leaves column 0020 empty and has AA-CVA 50: r0643 c0010 = 50, r0640 c0010 = 50. b1076 evaluates with r0640 c0020 defaulted to 0: 0 = 0 + 0 + 50, unsatisfied. Same for SA-CVA (r0641). For BA-CVA only, b1076 does not evaluate (all four of its cells are absent) but b1075 fails (see PI-13). It is rescoped rather than confirmed because a compliant alternative exists: the firm can complete column 0020 voluntarily (r0640 c0020 = 50), which satisfies the rule, and the Bank's ERROR rule boe_b0716 already forces r0040 c0020 on every firm with SA credit risk, so in practice column 0020 is not optional.

example.description: Small firm on the alternative approach to CVA (Chapter 6), outside the output floor's scope, CVA risk exposure amount 50; column 0020 not completed. r0643 c0010 = 50, r0640 c0010 = 50, r0010 c0010 = 50.

issues.alternatives_considered: Completing column 0020 voluntarily (S-TREA figures equal to the column 0010 figures for a firm with no models) satisfies b1076 and is not forbidden by Annex II, which only says the column is 'a requirement for' IM firms in scope. That alternative exists, so this is a scope-guard gap, not a contradiction a compliant return cannot escape.
issues.proposed_fix: Either state in Annex II that column 0020 is completed by every firm (which is what boe_b0716 already enforces), or guard the rule on the total being reported, in the form the Bank already uses in boe_b0793: if not(isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence()})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence()} i= {r: 0641, c: 0010, dv: 0} i+ {r: 0642, c: 0020, dv: 0} i+ {r: 0643, c: 0010, dv: 0} else true(). Verified in Arelle on a patched copy.
issues.eba_precedent: Known-issues log issue 6 (LVR001) is the same pattern, accepted and fixed by the Bank: "Non- LREQ firms are not expected to report every data item within the LV47.00.00.01 template. These firms will report some data points in scope of validation rules boe_b0017, boe_b0019 and boe_b0021 but not others causing the validations to fail."
issues.reach: Firms that hold SA-CVA or AA-CVA and leave OF 02.00 column 0020 empty: non-IM firms and solo returns outside the floor's scope, from 1 January 2027. WARNING only.
