issues.title: boe_b0718: the branch its label describes (r5860 blank: r0520 c0020 = r0530 + r0571) never runs, because r5860 has no default value
issues.requirement: What a firm reading the workbook believes: an ERROR rule that checks the standardised market-risk figure for the output floor in both cases. Label, verbatim: "If the ASA requirement for all desks (applicable only to IMA firms) is populated, the firm is an IMA firm. The Market Risk SA requirement for output floor purposes would then be equal to that amount. If the ASA requirement for all desks (applicable only to IMA firms) is blank, the firm must be either an SSA firm or an ASA firm. The SA requirement for output floor purposes would be equal to the sum of the firm's SSA requirement and the ASA requirement for ASA desks only, with one of the two expected to be blank depending on the firm's approach". What the gateway does: the formula (vr-boe_b0718.xml) declares <variable:factVariable xlink:label="boe_boe_b0718.v1" bindAsSequence="false" id="boe_boe_b0718.v1" /> with NO fallbackValue (v0, v2, v3 have fallbackValue="0"), and test="if (not(empty($v1))) then (iaf:numeric-equal($v0,$v1)) else ((iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:numeric-add($v2,$v3))))". A fact variable with no fallback and no matching fact produces no evaluation, so when r5860 c0020 is absent the assertion is not evaluated at all. Only the then-branch can ever run. No other PRA001 rule checks r0520 c0020 against r0530 + r0571 (every rule touching rows 0520/0530/0571/5860 was listed: b0706, b0718, b0720, b0793, b1091, b1092).

authority.quote: dv prefix is a prefix to define a default value for a variable, that will be used, if no data will be found, in the example, the default value is set to defaultValue (optional). If the default value will not be specified, an evaluation may return no results - in most cases, all facts must have value (from the report itself or the default value); the only function, that is able to handle null values for facts is isNull.
IsNull | Returns TRUE if fact specified by a variable node is null, otherwise FALSE.

1.3.4 Risk exposure amount for Position, foreign exchange and commodities risks under advanced standardised approaches (ASA) - for all desks [This is only applicable for IMA firms] The ASA own funds requirements for all positions, calculated for purpose of output floor.
The ASA own funds requirements for relevant desks (i.e., all desks for ASA firms). This is not applicable to SSA firms.
The fallback value for $v1 is incorrectly set as zero and it should be emptysequence. The validation will not function as expected when  $v1 isn't reported.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: A correct return does not fail; the defect runs the other way. For every firm that is not an IMA firm (r5860 blank, as Annex II requires), the rule is silent whether or not r0520 c0020 equals r0530 c0010 + r0571 c0010: Arelle gives [0,0] on a return where they agree (300 = 0 + 300) and [0,0] on one where they do not (500 against 0 + 300). The workbook's own Note says a missing default 'may return no results' but also that IsNull is the function that handles null facts, so a reader expects the else-branch to run. Two side effects were measured: (1) a non-IMA firm that writes an explicit 0 in r5860 c0020 instead of leaving it blank is taken down the then-branch and FAILS an ERROR rule (r0520 c0020 = 300 against r5860 = 0; Arelle [0,1]); (2) the obvious repair on its own (dv: emptySequence() on v1) would make the else-branch fail any firm that reports market risk in column 0010 and does not complete column 0020 (r0520 c0020 defaults to 0 against r0571 = 300; Arelle [0,1] on a patched copy), so the repair needs a guard.

example.description: ASA firm with no internal model for market risk: ASA requirement 300 in r0571 c0010 and r0520 c0010; r5860 blank as Annex II requires; r0520 c0020 misreported as 500. The label says this is an error; the gateway says nothing.

issues.alternatives_considered: Tried to find a path that makes the else-branch run: an IMA firm populates r5860 and takes the then-branch; a non-IMA firm that leaves it blank gets no evaluation; a non-IMA firm that writes 0 gets the then-branch (and an ERROR). The pivot variable (always execute = yes) does not help, because a fact variable without a fallback still blocks the evaluation. Nil facts are not admitted (no nils attribute). There is no input that reaches the else-branch.
issues.proposed_fix: Give both nullable cells an empty default and skip a return that reports neither: if isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), id: v0}) and isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), id: v1}) then true() else (if not(isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), id: v1})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, id: v0} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020, id: v1} else {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, id: v0} i= {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0530, c: 0010, dv: 0, id: v2} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0571, c: 0010, dv: 0, id: v3}). In formula terms: fallbackValue="()" on v0 and v1 and test "if (empty($v0) and empty($v1)) then true() else (if (not(empty($v1))) then (iaf:numeric-equal((if (empty($v0)) then 0 else $v0),$v1)) else (iaf:numeric-equal($v0,iaf:numeric-add($v2,$v3))))"; this exact text was run in Arelle (see control). If the Bank does not want the else-branch, the label should be cut back to the IMA case. Optionally test r5860 for a non-zero value instead of presence, so a zero-filled cell is not read as 'IMA firm'.
issues.eba_precedent: No EBA equivalent (v4.0.0 extract: none). In v4.0.0 the rule was a plain sum, "{t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020} = {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0530, c: 0010} + {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0571, c: 0010} + {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5860, c: 0020}"; the if/else was introduced in v4.1.1 and lost the default. The Bank has already logged the same kind of defect as a known issue (issue 12, boe_v0775_m_1, quoted above). boe_b0718 is not in the August 2026 log.
issues.reach: Every PRA001 filer that is not an IMA firm: the check its label promises is never applied. In addition, any such firm (or its software) that zero-fills r5860 c0020 gets an ERROR.
issues.meanwhile: The rule checks nothing on a return like this, at the gateway or here: check what it was meant to check yourself.

issues.title: Seven OF 91.01 ERROR rules can never bind: they name no sheet, and their formulas pin the sheet dimension (eba_dim:PRP) to its default member, which no OF 91.01 cell carries
issues.requirement: What a firm reading the workbook believes: seven ERROR checks on OF 91.01 (ASA general interest rate risk) - positive sensitivities >= 0, negative <= 0, net = positive + negative, scenario total = delta + vega + curvature for the low / medium / high scenarios, and total risk exposure = 12.5 x own funds requirement - applying to the template as reported, i.e. on both of its sheets. What the gateway does: each formula carries a variable-set filter <df:dimension><df:qname>eba_dim:PRP</df:qname></df:dimension><df:member><df:qname>eba_PL:x0</df:qname></df:member> (e.g. filter boe_boe_b0527.f68). eba_PL:x0 is PRP's default member (EBA dim-def.xml: dimension-default arc from eba_PRP to pl/mem.xsd#eba_x0). Every one of OF 91.01's 1,144 cells is on sheet 0001 (PRP = boe_eba_PL:x753, 'Dedicated general interest rate internal hedge portfolio', 572 cells) or sheet 0002 (PRP = eba_PL:x51, 'Other trading book positions', 572 cells). No fact can match, so the seven rules never produce an evaluation. Precision on the claim: the workbook does not say 'both sheets', it names no sheet at all. Of the 729 enforced PRA001 rules that reference a fixed-sheet table, these seven are the only ones whose reference names no z code (neither in the reference nor in the scope); the other 722 list the sheets explicitly, as the two neighbouring OF 91.01 rules boe_b0931 (z: 0001) and boe_b0931_1 (z: 0002) do. The formula generator reads 'no z' as 'no sheet'.

authority.quote: Where applicable, this template shall be reported separately for the following portfolios: • Dedicated general interest rate internal hedge portfolio, as referred to in paragraph 9 of Trading Book (CRR) Part Article 106; • Other trading book positions
This is net unweighted delta sensitivities to risk factors, i.e. the total sensitivities of positive sensitivities and negative sensitivities from columns 0010-0020
z prefix is used to define the sheet or group of sheets from which data should be extracted, in the example, the sheet will be identified by a code sheet1,

authority.locator: fws/banking/banking_reporting/2026-08-17/val/vr-boe_b0527.xml (identical filter in the other six files)
authority.quote: <df:dimension> <df:qname>eba_dim:PRP</df:qname> </df:dimension> <df:member> <df:qname>eba_PL:x0</df:qname> </df:member>

issues.why_correct_return_fails: No correct return fails. The rules are published as ERROR, 'Include in XBRL: yes', 'Deactivated: no', and are never evaluated on any return, right or wrong. A return that breaks all seven on sheet 0002 (and boe_b0281 and boe_b0541 on sheet 0001 as well) is accepted: Arelle reports [0,0] for each of the seven while the two rules that name their sheet evaluate on the same facts (boe_b0931 [0,1], boe_b0931_1 [1,0]).

example.description: OF 91.01 row 0010 with every one of the seven identities deliberately broken on sheet 0002 (positive sensitivity -5, negative +7, net 999, each scenario total 10 against components 1 + 1 + 1, total risk exposure 1 against own funds requirement 10), and on sheet 0001 a negative 'positive' sensitivity and r0010 c0160 = 10 against a largest scenario total of 4 (so that the control boe_b0931 is seen to fail).

issues.alternatives_considered: Looked for any way a fact could bind: OF 91.01 has no cell without a sheet (cells.arrow: 572 cells on each of sheets 0001 and 0002, none unsheeted), and PRP = eba_PL:x0 is not a member any OF 91.01 data point carries, so no reporting choice changes the outcome. The other OF 91 tables (91.02-91.10) are single-sheet and their 57 rules leave PRP open, so the defect is confined to these seven.
issues.proposed_fix: Name the sheets, as every other rule on a sheeted table does. Either add z: 0001; 0002 to each reference or scope (e.g. boe_b0527 scope({t: OF91.01.01.01, r:0010;...;0380, z:0001;0002, f: banking, fv: banking_reporting}); boe_b0281 {t: OF91.01.01.01, r: 0010; ...; 0380, c: 0010, z: 0001; 0002} >= 0; boe_b0541 {t: OF91.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0170, z: 0001; 0002, dv: 0} i= {t: OF91.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0160, z: 0001; 0002, dv: 0} i* 12.5), or split each rule per sheet as was done for boe_b0931 / boe_b0931_1. In the formulas that means dropping the eba_dim:PRP = eba_PL:x0 set-filter so the sheet is matched fact by fact (shown to work in Arelle on a patched copy). Because these checks have never run, they should be tested on real data before being switched on as ERROR.
issues.eba_precedent: None found; these are Bank-authored (boe_b) rules for the UK ASA templates. Not in the August or November 2026 known-issues logs.
issues.reach: Every ASA market-risk filer of OF 91.01, every period: seven published ERROR checks give no protection, and vendor software built from the workbook will apply checks the gateway does not.
issues.meanwhile: The rule checks nothing on a return like this, at the gateway or here: check what it was meant to check yourself.

issues.title: v4011_a (C 14.00 c0190) and v4023_a (C 06.02 c0050): the workbook expression is cut at 32,700 characters and there is no formula, but the gateway still enforces the country list through the cell's data type, with a longer list than the workbook shows
issues.requirement: Each rule is an allowed-values list for a country cell (C 14.00 c0190 'Country of origin of the ultimate underlying of the transaction'; C 06.02 c0050 'Jurisdiction of incorporation'). The workbook gives three different versions of the list for the same rule: the 'Expression' cell is exactly 32,700 characters long and stops mid-reference ('... seq: False, id: v'; 287 opening braces against 286 closing; 286 complete alternatives, the last being eba_GA:_4O); the 'Simplified Expression' cell is complete and has 336 alternatives; the 'Label' cell names 359 entries (it includes [KOSOVO]). Correction to the claim: the cut is at 32,700 characters, which is the exporter's cap, not Excel's 32,767-character cell limit. What the gateway does: there is no formula for either rule (no vr-v4011_a*.xml or vr-v4023_a*.xml anywhere in the package; 'Include in XBRL' = no). But both cells are enumerated items in the taxonomy: eba_met:ei86 and eba_met:ei152 are declared type="enum:enumerationItemType" with enum:linkrole=".../dict/dom/GA/GA4_1", a hierarchy of 359 members. An XBRL processor validates the value against that list. So the rule is not 'never run' in effect: its intent is enforced by the data type, against 359 members, 23 of which are missing from the Simplified Expression (eba_GA:XK Kosovo, eba_GA:_6P to _6U, _6Z, _7Y, _7Z, _8A, _9B and eleven eba_GA:IMF.CL_AREA.* codes) and 73 of which are missing from the truncated Expression.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: It does not fail at the gateway. The harm is on the firm's side: a firm or vendor that builds the allowed list from the workbook's Expression (286 codes, unparseable) or Simplified Expression (336 codes) will reject values the gateway accepts. Measured: C 06.02 c0050 = eba_GA:XK (Kosovo, named in the rule's own Label, absent from both expression cells) and = eba_GA:_6P are accepted by Arelle with no message; eba_GA:x29, a GA member outside hierarchy GA4_1, is rejected with enumie:InvalidFactValue.

issues.proposed_fix: Publish the complete rule text: split the expression so it is not cut at 32,700 characters, or replace the disjunction with a reference to the hierarchy the taxonomy already uses (GA4_1). Bring the three cells into line with each other and with the taxonomy: Expression (286 complete alternatives), Simplified Expression (336) and Label (359) should all carry the 359 members of GA4_1. State in the workbook's Note sheet what 'Include in XBRL: no' means and that allowed-value (_a) rules are enforced by the enumerated data type.

issues.title: 45 PRA001 rules are marked 'Include in XBRL: no' and have no formula; 15 of the 38 active ones are checked by nothing in the package (5 ERROR), the other 23 are allowed-value lists the taxonomy enforces through the data type
issues.requirement: Counts, measured on the workbook and the package: 1,486 rules; 1,441 'Include in XBRL: yes' and exactly 1,441 assertion files in fws/banking/banking_reporting/2026-08-17/val (same ids, no extras, none missing); 45 'no', none with a formula anywhere in the package. Of the 45, 7 are also deactivated (all WARNING: v7363_m, v7364_m, v7667_a, v7380_m, v7381_m, v7386_m, v7387_m) and 38 are active (17 ERROR, 21 WARNING). The 38 active rules are two different things. (A) 15 checks that nothing in the package performs: ERROR boe_b0755, boe_b0756, boe_b0757, boe_b0758 (OF 08.01 r0070 against exposure-weighted sums over OF 08.02), boe_b0903 (reference-date format); WARNING v8731_m (C 09.04), v7371_m (C 14.00/C 14.01), v7338_m (C 14.01), v09805_m (C 34.01), v10494_s (C 34.02), v10288_h and v10328_s (C 34.03), v10487_s (C 34.04), v10491_s (C 34.05), v10481_s (C 34.09). (B) 23 allowed-value lists on enumerated cells, which the taxonomy enforces through the data type (Arelle: enumie:InvalidFactValue): ERROR v4010_a, v4011_a, v4014_a, v4015_a, v4018_a, v4020_a, v4021_a, v4022_a, v4023_a, v6305_a, v6577_a, v7299_a; WARNING v6520_a, v7668_a, v7675_a, v7676_a, v7677_a, v7678_a, v7679_a, v10270_a, v10475_a, v10476_a, v10564_a. For 16 of them the workbook list equals the taxonomy's hierarchy member for member (v4010_a, v4014_a, v4015_a, v4018_a, v4020_a, v4022_a, v6305_a, v6577_a, v7299_a, v7675_a, v7677_a, v7678_a, v7679_a, v10270_a, v10475_a, v10476_a); v7676_a matches on the pack's list (not re-read from met.xsd); 6 are narrower than what the taxonomy accepts (v4011_a and v4023_a: 336 of 359; v4021_a: 4 of 5, eba_PL:x71; v6520_a: 8 of 14; v7668_a: 13 of 18; v10564_a: 2 of 3, eba_ZZ:x427). The '16 in the credit-risk tables' of the claim is right: boe_b0755-b0758, v8731_m, v09805_m, v10475_a, v10494_s, v10288_h, v10328_s, v10476_a, v10487_s, v10491_s, v10270_a, v10564_a, v10481_s. Of those, 12 are checked by nothing (4 ERROR, 8 WARNING) and 4 are allowed-value lists (v10475_a, v10476_a, v10270_a equal to the taxonomy; v10564_a narrower). What a firm reading the workbook believes: the row says ERROR, Deactivated = no, and the Note sheet does not define the 'Include in XBRL' column, so the rule looks binding. What the gateway does, as far as the published package shows: no assertion exists, so an XBRL processor running the Bank's package never evaluates them.

authority.locator: issue 18, v11871_m: the Bank's own description of a rule that is not serialised
authority.quote: preventing this validation from being serialized into xbrl. Consequently, it's being omitted from the taxonomy output.
No temporary solution. The validation hasn't been serialized and is therefore excluded from the taxonomy package

authority.locator: OF 08.01 column 0230 (basis for the boe_b0756 algebra)
authority.quote: Exposures and the respective LGDs for large regulated financial sector entities and unregulated financial sector entities as defined in Rules 1.3 and 1.4 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part shall not be included in the calculation of column 0230, but only be included in the calculation of column 0240.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: At the gateway nothing fails, because nothing runs. Two consequences. (1) Firms and vendors that implement the workbook as published will run checks the gateway does not, and one of them is wrong as written. boe_b0756's right-hand side subtracts raw exposure, isum(c0140), from an LGD-weighted sum; the identity that matches Annex II p.111 is c0230(r0070) x (sum c0110 - sum c0140) = sum(c0230 x (c0110 - c0140)). Two grades (exposure 600 and 400, of which large financial sector entities 100 each, LGD 40% and 30%): Annex II gives r0070 c0230 = 36.25%; left side 0.3625 x 800 = 290; right side as published 0.40 x 600 + 0.30 x 400 - 200 = 160; with the corrected right side 290. So boe_b0756 applied literally fails every sheet that holds a large or unregulated financial sector entity. boe_b0755, b0757 and b0758 hold on the same example (26 = 26, 90 = 90, 820,000 = 820,000). This algebra is hand-worked; it cannot be run in Arelle because no formula exists. (2) For six allowed-value rules the gateway accepts values the workbook says are not allowed, e.g. C 34.06 c0050 = eba_ZZ:x427 'No CCP' passes Arelle although v10564_a lists only QCCP and NON-QCCP.
issues.alternatives_considered: Not applicable: no correct return fails at the gateway. Considered whether the rules might be applied outside XBRL: the workbook's Note sheet does not define 'Include in XBRL', the v4.1.1 release note does not mention it, and the Bank's own known-issues log describes a rule that is not serialised as 'excluded from the taxonomy package'. Whether the gateway runs any non-XBRL check is not determinable from published material, so 'never run' is proven for the XBRL layer only.
issues.proposed_fix: (1) Define the 'Include in XBRL' column in the Note sheet and say whether a rule marked 'no' is applied by any other means. (2) For the 15 checks with no formula: either serialise them or mark them Deactivated / informational so they are not read as binding ERROR rules. issues.title: boe_b0710 (and boe_b0710_1/_2/_3) requires E* (c0150) to equal the off-balance-sheet conversion-factor breakdown (c0160-c0190) on rows that also hold on-balance-sheet and counterparty-credit-risk exposure

publisher_log.statement: The formula requires column 0150 (Fully Adjusted Exposure Value) to equal the sum of columns 0160, 0170, 0171, 0180, 0190. These columns represent the breakdown of fully adjusted exposure values by credit conversion factor and therefore relate solely to off-balance sheet exposures. The scope of the formula has been erroneously extended beyond row 0080 (off-balance sheet exposures). Solution: The validations have been deactivated. They will be reviewed with the next taxonomy update to ensure they apply only to row 0080

issues.requirement: On each of 26 rows of OF 07.00.01.01 (r0010 Total; the of-which rows 0015, 0020-0026, 0050, 0060; r0080 off-balance-sheet; the real-estate rows 0330-0360) and on all 16 sheets, column 0150 (fully adjusted exposure value, E*) must equal the sum of columns 0160, 0170, 0171, 0180 and 0190 (E* of off-balance-sheet items in the 10%, 20%, 40%, 50% and 100% conversion-factor buckets). The _1/_2/_3 variants assert the same on the memorandum rows 0300/0320 (OF 07.00.01.03, exposures in default), 0371-0374 (OF 07.00.01.04, equity under the transitional approaches) and 0380 (OF 07.00.01.05, currency-mismatch exposures). A missing cell is read as 0; a row with none of the six cells reported is not evaluated.

(-) Breakdown of the fully adjusted exposure value of off-balance sheet items by conversion factors Table A1 of Article 111 of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part and the Glossary Part. The figures reported shall be the fully adjusted exposure values before application of the conversion factor.

(b) subject to point (c), an off-balance sheet item listed in Column A of Table A1 shall be the product of:

authority.quote: Conversion factors for off-balance sheet items

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Annex II defines c0150 as E* of every exposure in the row and c0160-c0190 as the breakdown of E* of off-balance-sheet items only; under Article 111(1) only an off-balance-sheet item has a conversion factor. So on any row holding an on-balance-sheet asset (or, on the total row, a counterparty-credit-risk exposure): c0150 - (c0160 + c0170 + c0171 + c0180 + c0190) = on-balance-sheet E* (+ CCR E*) > 0, and the equality is false. It is an identity only on r0080. The amount cannot be put in a bucket instead: the taxonomy has no bucket cells on the on-balance-sheet row r0070, and the Bank's own ERROR rule boe_b0765 fixes the total row's buckets to the off-balance-sheet row's (r0010 = r0080 on c0160-c0190). Algebra: boe_b0710 at r0010 gives E*(0010) = sum of buckets(0010); boe_b0710 at r0080 gives E*(0080) = sum of buckets(0080); boe_b0765 gives buckets(0010) = buckets(0080); hence E*(0010) = E*(0080), i.e. total E* must equal off-balance-sheet E*. Meanwhile boe_b0699 (ERROR) builds r0010 c0150 from c0110 + c0120 + c0130, the net exposure of all items. A firm with no off-balance-sheet business at all fails on every populated row in scope (return G below).

example.description: A firm with no off-balance-sheet business at all, so no cell of columns 0160-0190 is reported anywhere: on OF 07.00.01.01, a real-estate exposure of 1,200 on sheet 0010 (rows 0010, 0070, 0330, 0331 and its risk-weight row 0180) and an SME corporate loan of 500 on sheet 0008 (rows 0010, 0020, 0070 and risk-weight row 0230); one defaulted loan on OF 07.00.01.03 row 0300 (sheet 0008), one equity holding on OF 07.00.01.04 row 0372 (sheet 0016) and one currency-mismatch mortgage on OF 07.00.01.05 row 0380 (sheet 0010). boe_b0710 is unsatisfied on every one of the five populated rows in its scope, and boe_b0710_1, _2 and _3 once each, while the sibling rules hold (boe_b0471, its _2 and _3, boe_b0556_1 and _2, boe_b0655, boe_b0656, boe_b0657_1 and _2, boe_b0717). With an off-balance-sheet item as well (a loan of 1,000 and an undrawn commitment of 400 at 40%, Total sheet only), boe_b0710 fails on row 0010 (1,400 against 400) and holds on row 0080 (400 = 400).

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Put the loan in the 100% bucket (c0190) of the total row: boe_b0710 is then satisfied [4,0] but boe_b0765 fails [2,2] because r0080 c0190 does not hold it; it also contradicts the column definition and Article 111(1)(a). (b) Put it in the off-balance-sheet row's 100% bucket and E* as well: boe_b0710 and boe_b0765 pass, but the off-balance-sheet row is overstated, boe_b0717 fails [2,2] and boe_b0699 fails [4,2]. (c) Leave the loan out of E* and exposure value altogether: every rule passes but the return no longer describes the firm. (d) Leave c0150 blank on the total row: it defaults to 0 against buckets of 400 and boe_b0699/boe_b0471 fail. (e) No precondition, filing indicator or greyed cell removes r0010 from the rule: Arelle evaluates it. None is Annex-II-compliant and passing.
issues.proposed_fix: boe_b0710: keep the expression and reduce the row scope to the off-balance-sheet row, as the EBA's v6364_m does: scope({t: OF07.00.01.01, r:0080, z:0001;0002;0003;0004;0005;0006;0007;0008;0009;0010;0011;0012;0013;0015;0016;0017}). If a check is wanted on the other 25 rows, make it an inequality (the form of the EBA's former v4748_m): {c: 0150} i>= {c: 0160} i+ {c: 0170} i+ {c: 0171} i+ {c: 0180} i+ {c: 0190}. boe_b0710_1, boe_b0710_2 and boe_b0710_3: replace 'i=' with 'i>=' (rows 0300/0320, 0371-0374 and 0380 are not limited to off-balance-sheet items), or withdraw them. boe_b0765, boe_b0471, boe_b0717 and boe_b0655 need no change: the correct return satisfies all of them.
issues.eba_precedent: EBA v6364_m (live, ERROR; EBA validation rules list of 2026-06-10, framework 3.0): '{c0150} = {c0160} + {c0170} + {c0180} + {c0190}' on C 07.00.a row 0080 ONLY; the Bank's v4.0.0 workbook extract names v6364_m as the EBA equivalent of boe_b0710. v6364_m replaced v4748_m ('{c0150} >= {c0160} + {c0170} + {c0180} + {c0190}' on 22 rows including 0010, an inequality, deactivated 2018-03-09). EBA v0311_m (live, ERROR) '{r0010} = {r0080}' on columns 0160-0190 is boe_b0765. So the EBA holds the equality on the off-balance-sheet row and ties the total row's buckets to it; the Bank kept both and widened the equality to 26 rows.
issues.reach: Every PRA001 filer with standardised-approach exposure that holds any on-balance-sheet asset or CCR exposure, i.e. in practice every firm, on every return under taxonomy v4.1.1 (instructions effective 1 January 2027). It fails on r0010 of the Total sheet and of every class sheet with on-balance-sheet exposure, on each populated of-which row (mortgage lenders: rows 0330-0360), and on the memorandum tables for defaulted loans, transitional equity and currency-mismatch lending. The Bank recorded it as known issue #22 on 2 October 2026 and deactivated the four rules at its gateway on 19 October 2026 (validations deny list).
issues.meanwhile: Nothing to change. The Bank deactivated boe_b0710, boe_b0710_1, boe_b0710_2 and boe_b0710_3 at its gateway on 19 October 2026 (validations deny list; known issues log #22), and rwa-filer does not run them on a submission date from then on. Before that date a break is reported, labelled with this issue.

issues.title: Extended chain: boe_b0710 + boe_b0765 + boe_b0471 force total exposure value (r0010 c0200) to equal off-balance-sheet exposure value on every sheet; rows 0070/0090/0110/0130 are forced to zero only if the WARNING boe_b0717 is honoured too

publisher_log.statement: The scope of the formula has been erroneously extended beyond row 0080 (off-balance sheet exposures)

issues.requirement: Re-derived from the rule book, not taken from the earlier report. Write E(r) for c0150, V(r) for c0200 and B160..B190(r) for the five buckets at row r. (1) boe_b0710 at r0010: E(0010) = B160+B170+B171+B180+B190 at r0010. (2) boe_b0710 at r0080: the same at r0080. (3) boe_b0765: each bucket at r0010 equals the bucket at r0080. Hence E(0010) = E(0080). (4) boe_b0471 at r0010: V(0010) = E(0010) - 0.9 B160 - 0.8 B170 - 0.6 B171 - 0.5 B180; substituting (1): V(0010) = 0.1 B160 + 0.2 B170 + 0.4 B171 + 0.5 B180 + 1.0 B190 at r0010. (5) The same at r0080; with (3): V(0010) = V(0080). Steps (1)-(5) are all ERROR rules. (6) boe_b0717, a WARNING: V(0010) = V(0070) + V(0080) + V(0090) + V(0110) + V(0130), so V(0070) + V(0090) + V(0110) + V(0130) = 0. (7) boe_b0655 (ERROR): each of them is >= 0, so each is 0 (and rows 0100/0120, of-which rows of 0090/0110, with them). All five rules have the same 16-sheet scope, which is every sheet of OF 07.00.01.01.

authority.quote: Exposure value after taking into account value adjustments, all credit risk mitigants and conversion factors that is to be assigned to risk weights in accordance with Article 113 of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.
Exposure values for CCR business shall be the same as reported in column 0210.

1. For Derivative instruments, securities financing transactions and long settlement transactions subject to counterparty credit risk the original exposure shall correspond to the Exposure Value for Counterparty Credit Risk (see instructions to column 0210).

Breakdown of total exposures by exposure types Reporting institution´s “banking book” positions shall be broken-down, following the criteria provided below, into on-balance sheet exposures subject to credit risk, off-balance sheet exposures subject to credit risk and exposures subject to counterparty credit risk.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: The chain is real, but narrower than claimed in two respects. First, what the ERROR rules alone force is a wrong TOTAL row, not zero rows: r0010 c0150 = r0080 c0150 and r0010 c0200 = r0080 c0200 on every sheet. No rule sets r0070 c0150 to zero (boe_b0699 only ties it to c0110 + c0120 + c0130), so 'forces on-balance-sheet E* to zero' should read 'forces total E* to equal off-balance-sheet E*'. Second, exposure value on rows 0070 (on-balance-sheet), 0090 (SFT), 0110 (derivatives) and 0130 (cross-product netting) is forced to zero only through boe_b0717, which is a WARNING and does not block a submission. Arelle shows both ends: a return with honest rows 0070, 0080 and risk-weight rows and a total row set to the off-balance-sheet row's figures satisfies every ERROR rule and trips only the WARNINGs boe_b0717 and boe_b0719 (the spec below); the only return that satisfies every rule, warnings included, is the one that leaves the on-balance-sheet loan out altogether. Either way a correct return cannot pass: it fails boe_b0710 on r0010 (PI-15a).

example.description: Same position as PI-15a (loan 1,000 on-balance-sheet, commitment 400 at 40%), Total sheet 0001. Rows 0070, 0080 and 0230 are reported correctly; the total row r0010 is bent to what the ERROR rules require: c0010 = c0040 = c0110 = c0150 = 400 (instead of 1,400), c0171 = 400, c0200 = 160 (instead of 1,160), c0220 left at the true 1,160. Result: every ERROR rule satisfied; boe_b0717 fails on c0200 (160 against 1,000 + 160) and boe_b0719 fails on c0150 and c0200 (400 and 160 against the risk-weight row's 1,400 and 1,160).

issues.alternatives_considered: With the rules as published there are exactly three ways to file the position, all tested: correct figures (fails the ERROR boe_b0710 on r0010); a total row equal to the off-balance-sheet row (passes every ERROR, fails the WARNINGs boe_b0717 and boe_b0719, and misstates total E* by 1,000 and total exposure value by 1,000); or omitting the on-balance-sheet and CCR exposure value from the sheet (passes everything, is not the firm's position). None is both correct and passing.
issues.proposed_fix: No change beyond PI-15a. Once boe_b0710 is confined to row 0080 the chain disappears: boe_b0765, boe_b0471, boe_b0717 and boe_b0655 are each consistent with Annex II, and the correct return satisfies all of them (Arelle, pi15_A1).
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA set has boe_b0765's and boe_b0717's equivalents (v0311_m ERROR; v0310_m WARNING, r0010 = r0070 + r0080 + r0090 + r0110 + r0130 on c0200, 0215-0217, 0220) but the chain does not arise there, because v6364_m holds the bucket equality on row 0080 only.
issues.reach: Same population as PI-15a (every firm with on-balance-sheet or CCR standardised-approach exposure, every sheet).
issues.meanwhile: Nothing to change: the chain rests on boe_b0710, which the Bank deactivated at its gateway on 19 October 2026 (PI-15a).

issues.title: boe_b0779 sums OF 08.07 column 0050, a percentage per roll-out class, down rows 0180-0250 into the Total row 0260
issues.requirement: For each of thirteen columns of OF 08.07 (0010, 0020, 0050 and 0060-0150), the Total row 0260 must equal the sum of the eight roll-out-class rows 0180-0250. Twelve of those columns are amounts (exposure value, risk-weighted exposure amount). Column 0050 is the percentage of a class's total exposure value that is under the IRB approach (data type percentage, metric eba_met:pi824); the other two percentage columns 0030 and 0040 are not in the scope.

authority.quote: TOTAL Institutions shall report the sum of the values reported in rows 0180-0250 for each of columns 0060-0150.

PERCENTAGE OF TOTAL EXPOSURE VALUE SUBJECT TO THE INTERNAL RATINGS BASED APPROACH (%) Institutions shall report the percentage of the total exposure value for each roll-out class for exposures that are subject to the IRB approach. Institutions shall calculate this percentage by dividing point (1) by point (2) below:
(2) Total exposure value for all exposures in that roll-out class as reported in column 0020.

84. Columns 0070 to 0150 shall cover the risk-weighted exposure amounts for the full spectrum of exposures, so the sum of each row for those columns shall be 100% of the risk-weighted exposure amounts for each roll-out class.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: A share does not add down rows. With class shares s_i and class weights w_i = class exposure value / total exposure value (w_i > 0, sum of w_i = 1), the total row's IRB share is sum(w_i x s_i); the rule demands sum(s_i). They are equal only if sum((1 - w_i) x s_i) = 0, i.e. when a single class holds all the exposure or no class has any IRB exposure. For any IRB firm with exposure in two or more roll-out classes the equality is false. The instruction's own row-0260 sum stops at columns 0060-0150 and does not reach column 0050. Example: s = (0.8, 1.0), w = (0.25, 0.75): the total is 0.95, the rule demands 1.8.

example.description: OF 08.07 for an IRB firm with two roll-out classes. r0210 (financial, large and other general corporates): exposure value 1,000 (c0020), of which 800 IRB (c0010) and 200 under a permanent-partial-use permission; shares c0030 = 0.2, c0040 = 0, c0050 = 0.8; RWEA c0060 = 680 = 200 (c0090) + 480 (c0150). r0230 (retail secured by residential property): 3,000, all IRB; shares 0 / 0 / 1.0; RWEA 450. r0260 Total: c0010 = 3,800, c0020 = 4,000, shares 200/4,000 = 0.05, 0, 3,800/4,000 = 0.95; RWEA 1,130 = 200 + 930. boe_b0779 fails on column 0050 only (0.95 against 0.8 + 1.0 = 1.8) and holds on columns 0010, 0020, 0060, 0090 and 0150.

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Report the row sum (1.8, i.e. 180%) as the total IRB share: boe_b0779 [6,0] but boe_b0778 fails on r0260 [2,1] (0.05 + 0 + 1.8). (b) As (a) and a total PPU share of -0.8: both rules pass (pi16_D, see PI-16b), with a 180% and a -80% share that mean nothing. (c) Leave the three share cells of r0260 blank, reading the row-0260 instruction literally: boe_b0779 still fails on column 0050 [5,1] because the blank total defaults to 0 against a row sum of 1.8. (d) Leave c0050 blank on the class rows: boe_b0778 then fails on every class with an IRB share. No compliant alternative.
issues.proposed_fix: Remove 0050 from the column scope of boe_b0779: scope({t: OF08.07.01.01, c:0010;0020;0060;0070;0080;0090;0100;0110;0120;0130;0140;0150}). boe_b0778 already checks the three shares on row 0260.
issues.eba_precedent: The Bank's v4.0.0 extract names EBA v09797_m as the equivalent: '{r0170} = {r0010} + {r0040} + {r0050} + {r0090} + {r0150} + {r0160}' on all columns of C 08.07, a WARNING the EBA deactivated on 2021-06-30. The Bank itself withdrew the same pattern elsewhere in v4.1.1: boe_b0752_1 (PD), _22/_23 (LGD) and _24 (maturity), which summed averaged OF 08.02 columns into OF 08.01 row 0070, are in the v4.0.0 workbook and absent from the v4.1.1 workbook and rule book.
issues.reach: Every IRB firm reporting OF 08.07 with exposure in two or more roll-out classes, at least one of them with IRB exposure, on every return. Not in the Bank's known-issues logs of 27 August and 16 November 2026.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0779 against boe_b0778 on OF 08.07 row 0260: not a formal contradiction; both can be satisfied, but only with a total IRB share above 100% offset by a negative PPU or roll-out share
issues.requirement: On row 0260: boe_b0779 requires c0050 = sum of the class rows' c0050; boe_b0778 requires c0030 + c0040 + c0050 = 1. Together: c0030(0260) + c0040(0260) = 1 - sum of class IRB shares. Only seven PRA001 rules touch OF 08.07 (boe_b0320, b0778, b0779, b1045-b1048) and none bounds columns 0030, 0040 or 0050 between 0 and 1: boe_b0320's non-negativity covers the amount columns only.

authority.quote: Institutions shall report the percentage of the total exposure value for each roll-out class that is subject to the Standardised Approach in accordance with a permission granted under Article 150(1) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. Institutions shall calculate this percentage by dividing (1) by (2) below:
TOTAL Institutions shall report the sum of the values reported in rows 0180-0250 for each of columns 0060-0150.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Arelle accepts a return that satisfies both: total IRB share 1.8 (the row sum) and total PPU share -0.8. So the pair is satisfiable, but only by figures that are not shares. For a return whose percentages are true shares (each between 0 and 1, the total row computed on the totals) the two rules hold together only when sum(s_i) = sum(w_i x s_i), the single-class case of PI-16a. The defect is boe_b0779's column 0050 on its own (PI-16a); boe_b0778 is what stops a firm from simply filing the row sum, and the absence of any bound on the percentage cells is what leaves the nonsense solution open.

example.description: The PI-16a position with the total row altered to satisfy both rules: r0260 c0050 = 1.8 (0.8 + 1.0) and r0260 c0030 = -0.8, c0040 = 0, so that -0.8 + 0 + 1.8 = 1. Everything else as PI-16a. Arelle: boe_b0779 [6,0], boe_b0778 [3,0], boe_b0320 [14,0].

issues.alternatives_considered: This record is itself the alternative: the only way to pass both rules with two or more classes is a total IRB share equal to the sum of class shares with the excess over 100% offset by a negative share in c0030 or c0040. It is not Annex-II-compliant (c0030, c0040 and c0050 on row 0260 would not be percentages of the total exposure value).
issues.proposed_fix: As PI-16a (remove 0050 from boe_b0779's column scope). Optionally add the EBA's bounds for OF 08.07 columns 0030, 0040 and 0050 (each >= 0 and <= 1 on rows 0180-0260) so that an out-of-range share cannot satisfy boe_b0778.
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA bounds every C 08.07 share: v09769_m '{c0030} <= 1', v09770_m '{c0040} <= 1', v09771_m '{c0050} <= 1' and v10300_s '{C 08.07} >= 0' on columns 0010-0050 (all live WARNINGs). None of the four has a PRA001 counterpart for OF 08.07, which is why the out-of-range solution passes the Bank's rules.
issues.reach: Wording, not a separate break: same population as PI-16a.
issues.meanwhile: No validation result shows this issue. Report as the instructions require; the issue is recorded for the Bank's attention.

issues.requirement: c0030 (share under a permanent-partial-use permission) + c0040 (share under a roll-out plan) + c0050 (share under the IRB approach) = 1 on every roll-out-class row and on the Total row. The published label states an upper bound; the formula is an equality.

In exceptional circumstances, such as where an institution has acquired exposures to which it applies the Standardised Approach, but it has not yet received permission under Article 148(1) or Article 150(1) of the Credit Risk: Internal

authority.locator: OF 08.07 column 0140 (continuation on the next page)
authority.quote: Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, these exposures shall be reported in this column.

Institutions shall report the percentage of the total exposure value for each roll-out class that is subject to the Standardised Approach in accordance with a permission granted under Article 150(1) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. Institutions shall calculate this percentage by dividing (1) by (2) below:

Institutions shall report the percentage of the total exposure value for exposures that are subject to a roll-out plan under Article 148(1) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part for each roll-out

84. Columns 0070 to 0150 shall cover the risk-weighted exposure amounts for the full spectrum of exposures, so the sum of each row for those columns shall be 100% of the risk-weighted exposure amounts for each roll-out class.

authority.locator: C 08.07 general remarks, the text PS1/26 replaced
authority.quote: 84. Columns 0020 to 0040 should cover the full spectrum of exposures, so the sum of each row for those three columns should be 100% of all exposure classes except of securitisation positions and deducted positions.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: The three shares are defined by the basis on which an exposure is treated: under an Article 150(1) permission (c0030), under an Article 148(1) roll-out plan (c0040), under the IRB approach (c0050). Annex II itself describes a fourth population in the class: exposures on the standardised approach with neither permission yet, whose RWEA goes in column 0140. Those exposures are in the denominator (column 0020, all exposures of the class) and in none of the three numerators, so the shares total less than 100% and the equality fails. The PS1/26 instructions no longer say the three percentage columns total 100%: paragraph 84 now makes that statement about the RWEA columns 0070-0150 (which boe_b1045 checks and which include column 0140). The rule's own label asks only that the percentages not exceed 100%.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: On sheets 0002 and 0010, OF 08.01 row 0010 is the sum of row 0070 (exposures assigned to obligor grades) and row 0080 (slotting). Paragraph 77 keeps slotting out of OF 08.03, so the OF 08.03 PD rows add up to the non-CCR part of row 0070 only. Left side minus right side is therefore row 0080 in the rule's column. In the example, sheet 0010: exposure value 36,000 against 12,000 (gap 24,000 = r0080 c0110); RWEA 31,200 against 9,600 (gap 21,600); expected loss 222 against 30 (gap 192); provisions -80 against -30 (gap -50); off-balance-sheet pre-conversion-factor amount 15,000 against 5,000 (gap 10,000 = OF 08.01.01.02 r0080 c0100). Each rule breaks whenever the slotting figure in its own column is non-zero beyond the rounding allowance. So boe_b0735 needs the slotting book to have undrawn or other off-balance-sheet items (with fully drawn slotting loans it holds, variant E), and boe_b0740 needs provisions on slotting exposures. A book whose specialised lending is all on slotting breaks too (variant D): row 0010 on sheets 0010 and 0002 carries the slotting amounts, OF 08.03 has nothing to report for them, and the empty sum is read as zero.

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Put the slotting exposure into an OF 08.03 PD row: all six rules then hold [3,0] (pi17_C_slotting_forced_into_0803), but paragraph 77 forbids it and a slotting exposure has no PD estimate to bucket on. This is the change that is never wrong. Or (B), expression, to keep the check on those sheets. boe_b0735: read row 0070 instead of row 0010, i.e. {t: OF08.01.01.02, r: 0070, c: 0100, dv: 0, seq: False} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, c: 0020, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}). boe_b0736, b0738, b0739, b0740: also subtract the slotting row, i.e. {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0010, c: C, dv: 0, seq: False} i- isum({t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0040; 0050; 0060, c: C, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) i- {t: OF08.01.01.01, r: 0080, c: C, dv: 0, seq: False} i= isum({t: OF08.03.01.01, r: 0010; 0040; 0050; 0060; 0070; 0100; 0130; 0170, c: D, dv: emptySequence(), seq: True}) with (C, D) = (0110, 0040), (0260, 0090), (0282, 0100), (0290, 0110). On the example this gives 36,000 - 24,000 = 12,000, 31,200 - 21,600 = 9,600, 222 - 192 = 30, -80 + 50 = -30, and 5,000 = 5,000 for boe_b0735. issues.title: boe_b0737 (number of obligors): the same slotting gap, but one F-IRB plus one slotting obligor passes; whether it breaks depends on the rounding allowance on counts
issues.requirement: On the same 17 sheets as boe_b0736: OF 08.01 row 0010 c0300 (number of obligors) less the sum of c0300 on the CCR rows 0040, 0050 and 0060 must equal the sum of OF 08.03 c0060 (number of obligors) over PD rows 0010, 0040, 0050, 0060, 0070, 0100, 0130 and 0170. Row 0080 (slotting obligors) is not subtracted.

authority.quote: Information reported in this template shall not include data on specialised lending exposures on the slotting approach, which is included in template OF08.06.
the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: The gap is the number of slotting obligors (row 0080 c0300), as for the monetary rules. But a count is filed with decimals 0, so every reported count carries an allowance of 0.5 and the interval arithmetic adds them up: the rule tolerates a gap of 0.5 times the number of count facts it reads on the sheet (row 0010, each reported CCR row, each reported OF 08.03 PD row). It breaks only when the slotting obligors exceed that. Measured in Arelle: one populated PD row and 1 slotting obligor, 2 against 1, satisfied (N1, and the PI-17 example); the same with 2 slotting obligors, 3 against 1, unsatisfied (N2); three populated PD rows and 2 slotting obligors, 5 against 3, allowance 2.0, satisfied (N4); a sheet holding only slotting with 1 obligor and no OF 08.03 fact, 1 against an exact 0, allowance 0.5, unsatisfied (N3). So the claim as put, that the rule fails on one F-IRB plus one slotting exposure, is not right; the rule is still wrong on sheets 0002 and 0010 and breaks for any firm whose slotting obligors outnumber half the count facts involved.

example.description: Sheet 0010 (Corporates - Specialised Lending, FIRB approach or slotting approach): one F-IRB obligor in OF 08.03 row 0060 and two slotting obligors. Annex II asks for OF 08.01 c0300: row 0010 = 3, row 0070 = 1, row 0080 = 2; OF 08.03 row 0060 c0060 = 1 (no slotting, paragraph 77); OF 08.02 one grade with c0300 = 1. Sheet 0012 (F-IRB general corporate, one obligor) is the control sheet. issues.title: boe_b0793: the output floor is checked as x * (S-TREA + OF-ADJ); Article 92(2A) and Annex II give x * S-TREA + OF-ADJ
issues.requirement: Whenever OF 02.00 row 0010 column 0030 (the output floor) is reported, it must equal (r0036 c0030 [OF-ADJ] + r0040 c0020 + r0490 c0010 + r0520 c0020 + r5898 c0010 + r0590 c0010 + r0630 c0010 + r0640 c0020 + r0680 c0020 + r0690 c0020) multiplied by r0035 c0030 (the output floor multiplier x). The nine risk rows are S-TREA; the adjustment sits inside the bracket, so the rule states x * (S-TREA + OF-ADJ). The workbook text and the XBRL formula say the same thing.

authority.locator: Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part, Article 92(2A)
authority.quote: TREA = max {U-TREA; x ∙ S-TREA + OF-ADJ}
S-TREA= the standardised total risk exposure amount of the entity calculated in accordance with paragraph 3A; x= 72.5%; Output Floor Adjustments OF-ADJ= 12.5 * (IRB T2 – IRB CET1 – GCRA + SA T2);

The standardised total risk exposure amount shall be calculated as the sum of points (a) to (f) of paragraph 3: (a) after having taken into account paragraph 4; and (b) calculated without using any of the following approaches or as if permission to use the following approaches has not been granted:

an institution or CRR consolidation entity may apply the following factor x during the periods specified below: (a) 60% during the period from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2027; (b) 65% during the period from 1 January 2028 to 31 December 2028; (c) 70% during the period from 1 January 2029 to 31 December 2029.

The output floor (reported in row 0010 column 0030) should reflect the formula provided in Article 92 (2a) of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook: “x ∙ S-TREA + OF-ADJ” where x = the output floor multiplier, reported in row 0035 S-TREA = the total of all SA exposures provided in columns 0010 and 0020; and OF-ADJ = the output floor adjustment, reported in row 0036
1.03 Output floor adjustment (OF-ADJ) Indicate the total adjustment to the output floor described in Article 92 (2a) of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook as “OF-ADJ”.
This should be reported after applying the output floor multiplier and output floor adjustment as per Article 92 of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Article 92(2A) and Annex II give floor = x * S-TREA + OF-ADJ. The rule checks floor = x * (S-TREA + OF-ADJ). The two differ by (1 - x) * OF-ADJ, and x is never above 0.725 (boe_b0359), so the gap is at least 27.5% of OF-ADJ and 40% of it in 2027. Row 0036 is OF-ADJ itself: the taxonomy labels the row and its metric boe_met:mi10099 'Output floor adjustment (OF-ADJ)', Annex II says to report 'the total adjustment ... described in Article 92 (2a) ... as OF-ADJ', and neither Annex II nor the rules define a pre-multiplier adjustment (OF-ADJ appears only on Annex II p.29 and App 1 p.13; it is 12.5 times own-funds items, not an RWEA). In the example the floor is 0.60 x 1,170,000 + 50,000 = 752,000 and the rule expects (50,000 + 1,170,000) x 0.60 = 732,000: 20,000 apart. The rule holds only when (1 - x) * |OF-ADJ| is inside the propagated rounding allowance, roughly 0.00005 x (S-TREA + OF-ADJ) when x is filed to 4 decimals: on S-TREA 1,170,000 a gap of 40 is satisfied (OF-ADJ 100) and a gap of 80 is not (OF-ADJ 200).

example.description: An IM firm at 31 March 2027, GBP units, x = 60% (Article 92(5)(a)). Credit risk RWEA 700,000 on all approaches and 1,000,000 on standardised approaches only (r0040 c0010 / c0020); market risk 50,000 on both (r0520); operational risk 100,000 (r0590 c0010); CVA 20,000 on both (r0640). U-TREA = 870,000 (r0010 c0010); S-TREA = 1,170,000. OF-ADJ = 12.5 x (IRB T2 4,000 - IRB CET1 0 - GCRA 0 + SA T2 0) = 50,000 (r0036 c0030). Annex II and Article 92(2A): r0010 c0030 = 0.60 x 1,170,000 + 50,000 = 752,000; r0034 = false because 752,000 is below 870,000. boe_b0793 expects 732,000.

issues.alternatives_considered: (1) Report the floor the rule's way, 732,000: boe_b0793 is satisfied (pi18_C_rule_way), but the figure is not the Article 92(2A) floor, and boe_b0787 to b0792, b0560, b0561 and b0565 take row 0010 c0030 as TREA whenever it exceeds c0010. (2) Gross row 0036 up to OF-ADJ / x = 83,333 and keep the floor at 752,000: satisfied (pi18_D_r0036_grossed_up), but row 0036 is then not the OF-ADJ of Article 92(2A). (3) Leave row 0036 blank: boe_b0957 (ERROR) requires rows 0034, 0035 and 0036 whenever row 0010 c0030 is reported. (4) Leave row 0010 c0030 blank: the rule is then true(), but Annex II p.28 makes column 0030 a requirement for IM firms in scope. None is a compliant way to report the position.
issues.proposed_fix: Move row 0036 out of the bracket: if not(isNull({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0030, dv: emptySequence(), seq: False, id: v0})) then {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0010, c: 0030, dv: emptySequence(), seq: False, id: v0} i= ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0040, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v1} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0490, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v2} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0520, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v3} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 5898, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v12} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0590, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v6} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0630, c: 0010, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v7} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0640, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v8} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0680, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v9} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0690, c: 0020, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v10}) i* {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v11} i+ {t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0036, c: 0030, dv: 0, seq: False, id: v5} else true(). In the formula: iaf:numeric-equal($v0, iaf:numeric-add(iaf:numeric-multiply(<the nine-term sum without $v5>, $v11), $v5)). On the example: 1,170,000 x 0.60 + 50,000 = 752,000. The label could also be changed to say what the rule checks, for example 'Output floor (r0010 c0030) = output floor multiplier x S-TREA + OF-ADJ, Article 92(2A)'; today it reads 'Total credit risk RWAs under standardised approaches should reflect the sum of SA on the SA, and IRB exposures on the SA'.

issues.title: boe_b0346: an 'of which' ceiling applied to an average - LGD over all exposures must be at least LGD over defaulted exposures
issues.requirement: On 17 class rows of every OF 09.02 country sheet, the exposure-weighted average LGD of all exposures (col 0090) must be greater than or equal to the exposure-weighted average LGD of the defaulted exposures (col 0100). Label: 'OF WHICH: DEFAULTED (%) exposures shall not exceed EXPOSURE WEIGHTED AVERAGE LGD (%)'.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 09.02 col 0090
authority.quote: Same definition as for columns 0230 and 0240 of OF CR IRB template: the exposure weighted average LGD (%) shall refer to all exposures, including exposures to large financial sector entities and unregulated financial sector entities as defined in Rules 1.3 and 1.4 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part. Article 181(1)(h) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part shall be taken into account.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 09.02 col 0100 'Of which: defaulted'
authority.quote: Exposure weighted LGD for those exposures which have been classified as defaulted exposures in accordance with Article 178 of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part.

authority.locator: PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 181(1)(h)(i)
authority.quote: the institution shall, subject to point (h)(ii), for the specific case of exposures already in default, ensure that the LGD in default reflects downturn conditions where the estimates of LGD in default that are appropriate for an economic downturn are more conservative than the long-run average LGD for defaulted exposures;

authority.locator: PRA2026/1  - Article 154(1)(a) (retail; Art. 153(1)(b) is the AIRB corporate equivalent, p.101)
authority.quote: if PD = 1, i.e., for defaulted exposures: RW = max{0 , 12.5 ∙(LGD −BEEL)};

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Cols 0090 and 0100 are the same metric (eba_met:pi128 'Exposure weighted average LGD'); col 0100 only adds the dimension member 'defaulted'. An average over a population and the average over one of its subsets have no ordering: with weights w for defaulted and (1-w) for the rest, col 0090 = (1-w) x LGD_performing + w x LGD_defaulted, which is below col 0100 exactly when LGD_defaulted > LGD_performing. Under the AIRB approach that is the normal state: LGD in default must reflect downturn conditions and sit above BEEL by an unexpected-loss margin (Art. 181(1)(h)), while performing LGDs average over cured and low-loss outcomes. The rule copies the additive 'of which <= total' pattern (as in boe_b0349, cols 0107/0105) onto an averaged column. The Bank's own boe_b0668 / boe_b0682 treat these same columns as averages (the total row must lie between the minimum and maximum of the class rows).

example.description: An AIRB residential-mortgage book (the firm's only IRB class), total sheet eba_GA:x1: exposure value 100,000,000 of which 5,000,000 defaulted; LGD 12% on the non-defaulted exposures and LGD in default 30%. Col 0090 = (95,000,000 x 12% + 5,000,000 x 30%) / 100,000,000 = 12.9%; col 0100 = 30%. Rows 0072 (retail secured by residential immovable property, non-SME), 0060 (retail) and 0150 (total) all report 0.129 / 0.3 with exposure value 100,000,000 / 5,000,000. Arelle: boe_b0346 unsatisfied on all three rows. In a mixed book the FIRB corporate rows, where defaulted and performing exposures both carry the 40% supervisory LGD, pass and the retail and total rows fail: boe_b0346 [2, 3].

issues.alternatives_considered: (a) Leave col 0100 empty: the rule passes on the default of 0 but the firm has not reported a required figure. (b) Read col 0100 as the defaulted exposures' contribution to the overall average (sum over defaulted of EV x LGD, divided by total EV), which would always be <= col 0090: not a credible reading - the instruction says 'Exposure weighted LGD for those exposures which have been classified as defaulted', and the data point is the average-LGD metric restricted to defaulted exposures, exactly as cols 0230/0240 of OF 08.01 are defined. No compliant alternative.
issues.proposed_fix: Deactivate boe_b0346. The two columns are already bounded as averages by boe_b1049 (each between 0 and 1) and boe_b0668 / boe_b0682 (total row between the class rows' minimum and maximum). No inequality between col 0090 and col 0100 holds in either direction.
issues.eba_precedent: None. The EBA rule list has no C 09.02 rule comparing col 0090 with col 0100 (its live of-which rules on C 09.02 are v4783_m, col 0110 >= col 0120, and v4784_m, col 0010 >= col 0030); the v4.0.0 Bank workbook gives boe_b0346 no EBA equivalent. It is a Bank-origin rule.
issues.reach: Any IRB firm whose defaulted exposures in a class (or in total) carry an average LGD above the class average - common in AIRB retail books with defaults (wherever a row's defaulted exposure-weighted LGD exceeds the row's overall average), and in mixed books on aggregate rows, where defaulted AIRB retail LGD is averaged with performing FIRB corporates, where the defaulted exposures are concentrated in a higher-LGD class. FIRB-only corporate books pass unless the mix differs. WARNING severity, every OF 09.02 country sheet, from the first PS1/26 return.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0908: exposure value must be at least the risk-weighted exposure amount - false whenever a row's average IRB risk weight is above 100%
issues.requirement: On 18 class rows of every OF 09.02 country sheet, exposure value (col 0105) must be greater than or equal to the risk-weighted exposure amount (col 0110), i.e. the row's average risk weight must not exceed 100%. Label: 'Exposure value should exceed Risk-weighted exposure amount'.

authority.locator: PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 153(5) Table A (slotting; row 0045 of OF 09.02 is in the rule's scope): risk weights for IPRE, in the order Strong A, Strong B, Good C, Good D, Satisfactory, Weak, Default

authority.quote: where an institution uses the Advanced IRB Approach, RW shall be: RW = max (0, 12.5 ∙(LGD −BEEL))

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 09.02 col 0105
authority.quote: Same definition as for column 0110 of OF CR IRB template.

authority.locator: paragraph 87 (the only Annex II text on OF 09.02's RWEA columns: the column table on p.142-143 goes from 0107 to 0130 with no entry for 0110 or 0120)
authority.quote: Data regarding ‘exposure value’ and ‘Risk-weighted exposure amounts’ shall be reported as of the country of residence of the ultimate obligor.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: RWEA = RW x exposure value, and nothing in the IRB approach caps RW at 100%. The slotting table assigns 115% to 'Satisfactory' and 250% to 'Weak' specialised lending (140% / 250% for HVCRE); the Art. 153(1)(c) formula gives a senior unsecured FIRB corporate exposure (LGD 40%, M 2.5) a risk weight of 102.1% at PD 2% and 114.2% at PD 3%; an AIRB defaulted exposure is weighted 12.5 x (LGD - BEEL), above 100% as soon as the gap exceeds 8 percentage points. Any row whose exposure-weighted risk weight is above 100% has col 0110 > col 0105.

example.description: A slotting book reported on the total sheet eba_GA:x1: income-producing real estate, exposure value 10,000,000, every exposure graded 'Satisfactory' (115%), so RWEA = 11,500,000. Rows 0045 (specialised lending under the slotting approach), 0030 (corporates) and 0150 (total) each report col 0105 = 10,000,000 and col 0110 = 11,500,000. No model figure is involved - the 115% is the rule's own table. Arelle: boe_b0908 unsatisfied on all three rows. In the mixed book boe_b0908 is [3, 3]: rows 0045, 0055 and 0030 fail; the retail and total rows pass.

issues.alternatives_considered: None exists: both columns are single, unambiguous amounts (exposure value and RWEA of the row) and no instruction, grey cell, default or precondition changes either. The rule can only be met by a book whose average risk weight is at or below 100%.
issues.proposed_fix: Deactivate boe_b0908, as the EBA did with its original v4786_m on 10 December 2020. If a ceiling is wanted, use the 1,250% maximum risk weight rather than 100%, at WARNING severity: {t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0110, dv: 0} <= 12.5 * {t: OF09.02.01.01, c: 0105, dv: 0}. Separately, Annex II has no entry for OF 09.02 cols 0110 and 0120 (p.142-143); ask the Bank to restore them.
issues.eba_precedent: boe_b0908 restates EBA v4786_m ({c0105} >= {c0110} on C 09.02, WARNING). docs/assets/eba-validation-rules.xlsx: 'Deactivated on 2020-12-10' in every sheet from v2.8 to 3.5, (the v2.6 sheet shows an earlier deactivation on 2017-12-08; it is listed live again in the v2.7.0.1 sheet). The EBA's v4786_m row scope had no slotting row; the Bank's adds row 0045, where the slotting weights of 115%, 140% and 250% make the failure certain. Correction to the earlier report: the v4.0.0 Bank workbook also puts the label 'v4786_m' on boe_b0349 and boe_b0350, but neither restates it - v4786_m is the exposure-value-versus-RWEA check only.

issues.title: boe_b0350: OF 09.01 original exposure must be at least 'defaulted exposures' - but on 21 of its 29 rows the defaulted column is not a part of column 0010
issues.requirement: On 29 rows of every OF 09.01 country sheet (the SA geographical breakdown), original exposure pre-conversion factors (col 0010) must be at least 'defaulted exposures' (col 0020). Label: 'Original Exposures pre-CFs for the relevant IRB exposure class shall exceed Defaulted Exposures' (the template is the SA one).

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 09.01 col 0020 'Defaulted exposures' (heading on p.136)
authority.quote: Original exposure pre-conversion factors for those exposures which have been classified as “exposures in default” and for defaulted exposures assigned to the exposure classes “exposures associated with particularly high risk” or “subordinated debt, equity and other own funds instruments”.

This column shall provide additional information about the obligor structure of defaulted exposures. Exposures classified as “exposures in default” as referred to in Article 112(1)(j) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part shall be reported where the obligors would have been reported if those exposures were not assigned to the exposure classes 'exposures in default'.

authority.locator: PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 112(2); Table A2 puts 'Exposures in default' at position (5), above covered bonds (6), real estate (7), institutions (10), retail (14) and corporates (15), and below CIUs (2), subordinated debt/equity (3) and high risk (4) (p.33-34)
authority.quote: Where an exposure meets the criteria for more than one exposure class it shall be assigned to the exposure class that has the highest position in Table A2.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Under Art. 112(2) a defaulted corporate, retail, real estate, institution or sovereign exposure belongs to the class 'exposures in default': its original exposure is in row 0100 col 0010, not in the row of the class it came from. Col 0020 then shows it, as a memorandum item, against the class 'where the obligors would have been reported'. So on those class rows col 0010 is the non-defaulted book and col 0020 the defaulted book that used to be in the class - two disjoint populations, not a total and its part. The rule demands non-defaulted >= defaulted for every class, sub-class ('of which') row and country, which fails for any row whose exposures are mostly or wholly in default: one defaulted obligor in a country, a run-off sub-portfolio, a single project-finance loan in default. The identity is genuine only where defaulted exposures stay in their own class - rows 0110 (high risk), 0140-0143 (CIUs), 0150 (subordinated debt and equity) - and on the total row 0170; on row 0100 col 0020 is a greyed cell. That is 21 rows where the rule is not an identity, 7 where it is, 1 where it is trivial. The Bank's own rules encode the Annex II layout: boe_b0730 adds row 0100 into the col 0010 total, boe_b0729 leaves row 0100 out of the col 0020 total, and boe_b0263 ties the col 0020 total (less high risk, equity and CIUs) to the OF 07.00 'exposures in default' sheet.

example.description: An SA firm above the Article 5(5) threshold reports the total sheet (x1), GB and FR. GB: corporates, non-defaulted 40,000,000; one project-finance loan in default, 2,000,000. FR: institutions, non-defaulted 8,000,000; one corporate obligor in default, 500,000. Reported: total sheet r0070 (corporates) c0010 40,000,000 / c0020 2,500,000; r0073 (of which project finance) c0020 2,000,000 and no c0010; r0100 (exposures in default) c0010 2,500,000; r0170 c0010 50,500,000 / c0020 2,500,000; the country sheets likewise (FR r0070: c0020 500,000, no c0010); and the OF 07.00 original exposures the Bank's cross-template rules tie to (sheet 0001 50,500,000; 0007 8,000,000; 0008 40,000,000; 0011 2,500,000). Arelle: boe_b0350 [10, 3] - unsatisfied on x1 r0073, GB r0073 and FR r0070 - with boe_b0729, boe_b0730, boe_b0263, boe_b0237, boe_b0222, boe_b0258, boe_b0262 and boe_b0904 all satisfied.

issues.alternatives_considered: The only reporting that satisfies boe_b0350 for such a position counts the defaulted exposure twice in col 0010 (in row 0100 and in its original class row). Arelle shows that breaks the Bank's ERROR rule boe_b0730 and the ties to OF 07.00, and it contradicts Art. 112(2). Leaving col 0020 empty on class rows contradicts Annex II p.137 and, by their expressions, breaks boe_b0729 or boe_b0262 / boe_b0263 (not run). No compliant alternative.
issues.proposed_fix: Restrict boe_b0350 to the rows where col 0020 is a part of col 0010: scope({t: OF09.01.01.01, r:0110;0140;0141;0142;0143;0150;0170}), and correct the label ('IRB exposure class' -> SA exposure class). If a check on the other class rows is wanted, the true identity there is that a class's defaulted exposures cannot exceed the country's 'exposures in default' class: {t: OF09.01.01.01, c: 0020, dv: 0} i<= {t: OF09.01.01.01, r: 0100, c: 0010, dv: 0} over r:0010;0020;0030;0040;0050;0060;0070;0071;0072;0073;0075;0080;0085;0090;0091;0092;0093;0094;0095;0120;0160.
issues.eba_precedent: None for the rule: the EBA list has no C 09.01 rule comparing col 0010 with col 0020. The v4.0.0 Bank workbook labels boe_b0350 'v4786_m', which is a different check on a different template (C 09.02 col 0105 >= col 0110); the earlier report repeated that label. The rule looks like the IRB of-which pattern (EBA v4784_m, C 09.02 col 0010 >= col 0030, live and valid - under IRB a defaulted exposure stays in its class) carried over to the SA template, where it does not hold.
issues.reach: Any SA firm with a class, 'of which' sub-row or country whose defaulted original exposure exceeds its non-defaulted original exposure - typical of country sheets with one or two obligors, sub-rows such as specialised lending or land acquisition and development, and run-off books. WARNING severity, from the first PS1/26 OF 09.01 return.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

issues.title: Annex II has no instruction for OF 08.01 column 0010 (PD), and boe_b0356 demands a PD on rows that hold only slotted exposures
issues.requirement: On 18 rows of 16 sheets of OF 08.01, wherever exposure value (c0110) is positive, the PD in c0010 must be at least 0.05%; a PD that is not reported is read as 0 (dv: 0) and fails. The sheets include 0002 (Total FIRB and slotting) and 0010 (Specialised lending, FIRB or slotting); the rows include 0010 Total, 0020 on-balance-sheet and 0030 off-balance-sheet, but not 0080 (slotting total).

authority.locator: first entry of the OF 08.01 column table
authority.quote: Columns Instructions 0020 ORIGINAL EXPOSURE PRE-CONVERSION FACTORS Institutions shall report the exposure value before taking into account any value adjustments, provisions, effects due to credit risk mitigation techniques or credit conversion factors.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.02 columns
authority.quote: 0010-0300 Instructions for each of these columns are the same as for the corresponding numbered columns in OF CR IRB 1 template.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 09.02 column 0080
authority.quote: INTERNAL RATING SCALE/ PD ASSIGNED TO THE OBLIGOR GRADE OR POOL (%) Same definition as for column 0010 of OF CR IRB 1 template.
INTERNAL RATING SCALE | PD ASSIGNED TO THE OBLIGOR GRADE OR POOL (%) | 0010

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 row 0080
authority.quote: SPECIALISED LENDING SLOTTING APPROACH: TOTAL Exposures subject to the slotting approach. This shall only apply to the exposure sub-class ‘corporate – specialised lending’.

authority.locator: CRR COREP Annex II  - C 08.01 column 0010 (the instruction PS1/26 did not carry over)
authority.quote: For figures corresponding to an aggregation of obligor grades or pools (e.g. total exposures), the exposure weighted average of the PDs assigned to the obligor grades or pools included in the aggregation shall be provided. The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted average PD.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Two separate things. (1) Documentation: the Annex II column table for OF 08.01 begins at 0020 (p.102). Column 0010 exists - in the Annex I template (code 0010, 'PD assigned to the obligor grade or pool (%)', greyed only on rows 0080 and 0170) and in the taxonomy (eba_met:pi187, 306 cells on all 17 sheets, rows 0080 and 0170 not reportable) - and two other instructions (pp.118, 142) define their own PD column by reference to it. Nothing says what it holds on an aggregate row, how it is weighted, or whether it is before or after the PD input floor. (2) Rule: a firm that slots all of its specialised lending reports sheet 0010 with exposure value on rows 0010, 0020 and 0030, which are open for c0010 in template and taxonomy; a slotted exposure has a category, not a PD, so there is nothing to average and c0010 stays empty. boe_b0356 reads the empty PD as 0 and fires on each such row. The taxonomy itself greys the PD on the slotting row 0080, but the rule's scope takes the sheet's total rows.

example.description: A firm with 1,000 of specialised lending, all on the slotting approach (sheet 0010: rows 0010, 0020 and 0080 each 1,000 exposure value, RWEA 700, no PD), and 500 of FIRB general corporates at PD 1.2% (sheet 0012). Total FIRB-and-slotting sheet 0002: exposure value 1,500, PD 1.2% (the average over the PD-rated part).

issues.alternatives_considered: Report a PD on the slotting-only rows: there is none - Annex II gives no instruction, the CRR text it replaced averages 'the PDs assigned to the obligor grades or pools included', and none is included. Report the exposure only on row 0080: row 0010 is the sheet total and must include it. Row 0080 itself is outside the rule and greyed for c0010. A sheet that mixes FIRB and slotted specialised lending passes (the PD is the average of the rated part), as does sheet 0002 whenever any FIRB exposure exists.
issues.proposed_fix: (1) Annex II: restore an instruction for OF 08.01 column 0010 - what is reported on aggregate rows (exposure-weighted average, weight c0110), whether it is the PD before or after the input floor, and that it is left blank where no exposure on the row has a PD (slotting). (2) boe_b0356: do not evaluate the total rows of the two sheets that contain slotting - for z:0002;0010 restrict the scope to r:0070 (exposures assigned to obligor grades or pools), keep the present rows on the other 14 sheets; or drop 'dv: 0' from the c0010 reference so that an unreported PD is not read as 0, as in the EBA original.
issues.eba_precedent: The v4.0.0 workbook names the EBA original: v10670_m, 'if {c0110} > 0 then {c0010} >= 0.0003' on C 08.02 (the obligor-grade template, which holds no slotting), severity Warning, 'If value missing: do not run rule'. The Bank moved the check to OF 08.01, added total rows and the FIRB-or-slotting sheets, and treats a missing PD as zero.
issues.reach: Instruction gap: every IRB firm. Rule: any firm whose sheet 0010 carries only slotted exposure on a row in scope, every period, at WARNING (does not block).
