issues.title: OF 07.00 memorandum rows 0300 / 0320: Annex II names sheets the taxonomy does not publish

publisher_log.statement: The Credit Risk SA templates OF 07.00 Part 3 – Memo Items (Rows 0300 and 0320) and SC 07.00 Part 3 – Memo Items (Rows 0300 and 0320) do not contain a separate sheet for exposures assigned to the real estate exposure class (as referred to in Article 112(1)(i) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook).

issues.requirement: Not a rule. Table OF07.00.01.03 ('Memorandum items - Exposures in default') has a z-axis of seven sheets: 0001 Total, 0002 Central governments or central banks, 0003 Regional governments or local authorities, 0004 Public sector entities, 0007 Institutions, 0008 Corporates, 0009 Retail (read from of07.00.01.03-rend.xml and its code labels in the package). All 11 rules on the table are scoped to exactly those seven sheets and none compares one sheet with another.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - para 52
authority.quote: Those memorandum items in rows 0300 and 0320 shall only be reported for the following exposure classes: (a) central governments or central banks (Article 112(1)(a) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (b) regional governments or local authorities (Article 112(1)(b) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (c) public sector entities (Article 112(1)(c) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (d) institutions (Article 112(1)(f) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (e) corporates (Article 112(1)(g) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part); (f) retail (Article 112(1)(h) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part). (g) real estate (Article 112(1)(i) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part).

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - para 54
authority.quote: Exposures shall be reported in these rows where the obligors would have been reported in the exposure classes ‘Central governments or central banks’, ‘Regional governments or local authorities’, ‘Public sector entities’, ‘Institutions’, ‘Corporates’, ‘Retail’ and ‘Real estate’ within OF CR SA, if those exposures were not assigned to the exposure classes 'in default'.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - para 55
authority.quote: then that information shall be reported in OF CR SA, row 0320 in the total and in the exposure class ‘in default’. If this exposure, before it defaulted, was an exposure to an institution, then that information shall also be reported in row 0320 of exposure class 'institutions'.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - rows 0300 and 0320
authority.quote: Firms shall report values in this row for exposure classes defined in Article 112 (1)(a) to (i) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - row 0300
authority.quote: Exposures included in the exposure class “exposures in default”, subject to Article 127(1)(b) and (3) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, which would otherwise have been assigned to the exposure class being reported on if they were not in default.

authority.locator: PRA Rulebook instrument PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part, Article 127(3)
authority.quote: A residential real estate exposure which is a defaulted exposure and is not materially dependent on the cash-flows of the property shall be assigned a risk weight of 100%.

authority.locator: CRR COREP Annex II  - para 52 (the list the taxonomy still follows)
authority.quote: (d) Institutions (point (f) of Article 112 CRR); (e) Corporates (point (g) of Article 112 CRR); (f) Retail (point (h) of Article 112 CRR).

issues.why_correct_return_fails: No rule fails; a figure Annex II asks for has no cell. The real-estate part is the Bank's known issue #27 (19 October 2026), with the PRA's interim instruction to report those exposures on the Total sheet s0001 only and a promised taxonomy fix; what follows adds the other missing sheets, and one point of wording: #27 speaks of 'exposures assigned to the real estate exposure class', where Annex II para 54 and p.97 mean the exposures that would otherwise have been assigned to it. Where text and taxonomy DISAGREE: (1) Real estate, Article 112(1)(i) - named in para 52(g), para 54 and the row instructions (p.97); the taxonomy has no sheet 0010 on OF07.00.01.03. (2) Multilateral development banks (d) and international organisations (e) - inside 'Article 112(1)(a) to (i)' on p.97 (though absent from para 52, so Annex II contradicts itself); no sheets 0005 / 0006. (3) The exposure class 'in default' - para 55 says 'in the total and in the exposure class in default'; the Total sheet 0001 is published, the 'in default' sheet 0011 is not. Where they AGREE: Total (0001) and classes (a) 0002, (b) 0003, (c) 0004, (f) 0007, (g) 0008, (h) 0009. The published sheet list is the CRR one (six classes plus total); PS1/26 added real estate to the text and the taxonomy did not follow. Consequence under Basel 3.1: a defaulted exposure whose class would otherwise be real estate (for example a defaulted owner-occupied mortgage, which Article 127(3) weights at 100% and which row 0300's own instruction therefore covers) can be shown on the Total sheet only, so the Total no longer equals the sum of the class sheets - harmless today because no rule sums them.
issues.alternatives_considered: Report a defaulted real-estate exposure on the Retail or Corporates memorandum sheet instead: contrary to para 54, which now names 'Real estate' as its own would-have-been class. Report it on the Total sheet only: the only thing the taxonomy allows, and what a firm will have to do. Report it in the main table's 'Exposures in default' sheet 0011: that is OF07.00.01.01, which has no rows 0300 / 0320.
issues.proposed_fix: Decide which is intended and align the other. Either add sheet 0010 (Real estate exposures) - and 0005 / 0006 if 'Article 112(1)(a) to (i)' on p.97 is meant - to table OF07.00.01.03 and to the seven-sheet scopes of its 11 rules (boe_b0471_2, b0556_2, b0656, b0660, b0665, b0670, b0672_1, b0673, b0708_1, b0710_1, b0733_1); or correct Annex II: delete para 52(g) and 'Real estate' from para 54, replace 'Article 112 (1)(a) to (i)' on p.97 with the para 52 list, and reword para 55 ('in the total and in the exposure class in default') to say the Total sheet and the sheet of the original class.
issues.eba_precedent: The six-class list is the EBA's (CRR Annex II para 52: central governments, regional governments, PSEs, institutions, corporates, retail). The sentence 'in the total and in the exposure class in default' is also inherited from CRR Annex II para 55 and was never a sheet in the EBA taxonomy either. The additions of real estate (paras 52(g), 54) and of '(a) to (i)' (p.97) are the PRA's own.
issues.reach: Every SA firm with defaulted real-estate exposure (and the rare defaulted MDB / international-organisation exposure), every period. Nothing is rejected; the breakdown is simply incomplete. Not a rule break on our returns; it is why 5 of our figures have no cell.
issues.meanwhile: Follow the PRA's interim instruction in the Bank's known issues log #27: "As a temporary solution, the PRA requests that firms report exposures assigned to the real estate exposure class in the total sheet s0001 for rows 0300 and 0320 but do not report such exposures separately to this, until the missing sheet 0010 is provided in the next taxonomy update." The log's entry covers the real-estate sheet only; the other sheets this issue finds missing are not in it.

issues.title: boe_b0748 sums the exposure-weighted average maturity (c0250) across the AIRB class sheets
issues.requirement: For each of 42 columns, row 0010 of the Total AIRB sheet (0001) must equal the sum of row 0010 over the ten AIRB class sheets (0009, 0011, 0015-0021, 0023). The column list includes 0250, the exposure-weighted average maturity in days. A sheet that does not report the column counts as 0.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 column 0250
authority.quote: The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted averages. The average maturity shall be reported in days. This data shall not be reported for the exposure values for which the maturity is not an element in the calculation of risk-weighted exposure amounts. This column shall therefore not be filled in for the exposure class ‘retail’ or for exposures subject to the slotting approach.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - para 76
authority.quote: The templates OF CR IRB 1, OF CR IRB 2, OF CR IRB 3 and OF CR IRB 5 shall be reported separately for the following exposure and sub-exposure classes: 1) Total (The Total template must be reported for the FIRB and the slotting approaches and, separately for the AIRB approach.)

v4769_m: The rule requires that the total of all exposure classes equals the sum of the exposure classes for template C08.01. However it is incorrectly applied to columns that contain exposure-weighted non-monetary values (c0230-0240: %s, c0250: days), which cannot be aggregated.

This question has been rejected because the matter it refers to has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version of the Reporting framework / release of the respective validation rules.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: The Total sheet is a sheet like any other, so its c0250 is the exposure-weighted average over the AIRB exposures for which maturity enters the risk weight. With class sheets A and B: M_total = (EAD_A x M_A + EAD_B x M_B) / (EAD_A + EAD_B), which lies between M_A and M_B; the rule demands M_total = M_A + M_B. The two agree only when at most one AIRB class sheet reports a maturity. Retail sheets report none (p.111), so the sheets that matter are 0009, 0011 and 0023: an AIRB firm with both SME and non-SME general corporates fails.

example.description: AIRB general corporates: non-SME book (sheet 0011) exposure value 1,000, average maturity 900 days; SME book (sheet 0023) exposure value 1,000, average maturity 1,100 days. Total AIRB sheet 0001: exposure value 2,000, average maturity (1,000 x 900 + 1,000 x 1,100) / 2,000 = 1,000 days, 30 obligors (10 + 20). The same figures are filed on the FIRB side (sheets 0012, 0024, total 0002) as the control. Rows 0017 / 0035 on the two AIRB sheets serve PI-20d.

issues.alternatives_considered: Report the sum (2,000 days) on the Total sheet: not an average, and not what p.111 defines. Leave the Total sheet's c0250 empty: read as 0, still unequal to 900 + 1,100. Leave the class sheets empty: contrary to p.111 for corporate exposures. There is no compliant way once two AIRB non-retail sheets carry a maturity.
issues.eba_precedent: The v4.0.0 workbook names v4769_m as the original. In the EBA rule lists for frameworks 3.0-3.5 its columns exclude 0230, 0240, 0250, 0300 and 0310; the Bank's list adds 0250 and 0300 (and the additive 0310). EBA Q&A 2026_7840 reports that the DPM 4.2 version of v4769_m does reach c0230-0250 and calls that incorrect; the EBA rejected the question only because the matter 'has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version'.
issues.reach: Any AIRB firm that reports an average maturity on two or more of sheets 0009, 0011 and 0023 - typically any AIRB lender with both SME and non-SME general corporates - every period, at ERROR (the return is rejected).
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. rwa-filer still reports the break, labelled with this issue, and an Error-severity break still blocks the return, as it would at the gateway. If the gateway rejects the return on this rule, raise it with the PRA, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0748 also sums the number of obligors (c0300) across the AIRB class sheets
issues.requirement: Row 0010 c0300 of the Total AIRB sheet must equal the sum of row 0010 c0300 over the ten AIRB class sheets.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 column 0300
authority.quote: For all exposure classes, with the exception of the exposure class ‘retail’ and, for other exposures classes, the cases mentioned in the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, the institution shall report the number of legal entities/obligors which were separately rated, regardless of the number of different loans or exposures granted.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 column 0300
authority.quote: Within the exposure class ‘retail’, or if separate exposures to the same obligor are assigned to different obligor grades in accordance with the second sentence of Article 172(1)(e) of the Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part in other exposure classes, the institution shall report the number of exposures which were separately assigned to a certain rating grade or pool.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Mostly it does not, so the original claim is narrowed. Retail sheets count EXPOSURES (p.114), which add up; non-retail sheets count legal entities, and SME / non-SME is a property of the obligor, so an entity is normally on one corporate sheet. The sum differs from the Total only when one legal entity is counted on two AIRB non-retail sheets (for example a corporate with a general facility and an exposure classed as specialised lending) - the Total counts it once. Even then the interval arithmetic absorbs small differences: each integer fact carries +/-0.5, so with two class sheets a difference of 1 is satisfied and a difference of 2 is not (tested). It is not shown that this is a common position; what is certain is that the Bank's FIRB twin boe_b0749 and the EBA's v4769_m (frameworks 3.0-3.5) both leave 0300 out.

example.description: AIRB sheets 0011 (10 legal entities) and 0009 (20 legal entities) with two entities present on both: the Total AIRB sheet has 28 distinct entities against a sum of 30. With one shared entity (29) the rule is satisfied through the rounding allowance.

issues.alternatives_considered: Report the Total as the plain sum of the class sheets (counting a shared entity twice): satisfies the rule, and p.114 does not say explicitly that the Total sheet de-duplicates across classes - so a firm has a defensible way to pass. That is why this part is 'rescoped' rather than 'confirmed'.
issues.proposed_fix: Remove 0300 from boe_b0748's scope together with 0250 (so that it matches boe_b0749), or state in Annex II that the Total sheet's number of obligors is the sum of the class sheets.
issues.eba_precedent: v4769_m (EBA frameworks 3.0-3.5) omits column 0300. Related counts problems (OF 34.07 / OF 08.03 obligor counts summed or subtracted) are reported under other findings.
issues.reach: Only an AIRB firm with at least two legal entities rated on two AIRB non-retail sheets, and only if it de-duplicates the Total. ERROR severity. Latent on our returns.
issues.meanwhile: No validation result shows this issue. Report as the instructions require; the issue is recorded for the Bank's attention.

issues.title: boe_b0355 applies 'revolving commitments >= own-estimate bucket' to the average maturity column (c0250)
issues.requirement: On every sheet of OF 08.01, for each of 42 columns, the absolute value on row 0017 (exposures to revolving loan commitments) must be at least the absolute value on row 0035 (off-balance-sheet items with an own-estimate conversion factor). The label is 'only conversion factors for exposures to revolving commitments should be modelled'. The column list is the same one boe_b0748 uses and includes 0250 (average maturity, days); it leaves out the other averages (0010 PD, 0230 / 0240 LGD).

authority.locator: PRA Rulebook instrument PRA2026/1  - Credit Risk: Internal Ratings Based Approach (CRR) Part, Article 166D(1)
authority.quote: (a) for revolving loan commitments which would not be subject to a 100% conversion factor under Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 111: an own estimate of conversion factor that the institution shall provide in accordance with Section 6; (b) for all other off-balance sheet items: the conversion factor that would be applicable to the off-balance sheet item under the Standardised Approach, as set out in Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part Article 111.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 rows 0031-0035
authority.quote: For exposures subject to the AIRB approach for which conversion factors are estimated, or where EADs are estimated directly, institutions shall report values in row 0035.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 08.01 column 0250
authority.quote: The exposure value (column 0110) shall be used for the calculation of the exposure-weighted averages. The average maturity shall be reported in days.

authority.locator: EBA Single Rulebook Q&A 2026_7880 (rejected 15/10/2026 as the same matter as 2026_7840)
authority.quote: it is not possible to establish a relation between the sum of the exposure-weighted average maturity value of the rows 15 and 16 and the row 10.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Row 0035 is a subset of row 0017 (Article 166D(1)(a): only revolving commitments are modelled), so for amounts and counts the inequality is an identity. An average is not monotone in the population: the modelled revolvers can have a longer average maturity than all revolvers together. Row 0017 also holds the revolving commitments that are NOT modelled - those that would take a 100% conversion factor, which 166D(1)(a) excludes - so the two rows are genuinely different populations. With modelled revolvers at 1,400 days and the rest at 400 days, row 0017 averages 900 and row 0035 is 1,400: 900 >= 1,400 is false.

example.description: AIRB non-SME corporates, sheet 0011. Revolving commitments, exposure value 200 (row 0017): half with an own-estimate conversion factor and an average maturity of 1,400 days (row 0035, exposure value 100), half taking the standardised factor with 400 days. Row 0017 c0250 = (100 x 1,400 + 100 x 400) / 200 = 900 days; row 0035 c0250 = 1,400 days. Sheet 0023 carries the opposite case (row 0017 1,100 days, row 0035 800 days) as the control.

issues.alternatives_considered: Leave c0250 empty on row 0035 or row 0017: both cells are open in the Annex I template and the taxonomy and p.111 asks for the average wherever maturity enters the risk weight; an empty row 0017 against a reported row 0035 fails anyway (0 >= 1,400). Retail sheets are unaffected (no maturity). No compliant alternative on a corporate AIRB sheet with a mixed revolving book.
issues.proposed_fix: Remove 0250 from the scope of boe_b0355, leaving the additive columns and the count 0300.
issues.eba_precedent: No EBA equivalent is recorded for boe_b0355 (it is the Bank's own). The same class of defect is before the EBA: Q&A 2026_7840 / 2026_7880 on v903250_h, a row-hierarchy inequality on C 08.01 that reaches c0250 - 'incorrectly applied to columns that contain exposure-weighted non-monetary values (c0230-0240: %s, c0250: days), which cannot be aggregated' - rejected because the matter 'has already been identified and will be considered for a forthcoming version'.
issues.reach: AIRB firms with corporate revolving commitments of which only part is modelled, whenever the modelled part has the longer average maturity. WARNING (does not block). Latent on our returns.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.

issues.title: boe_b0359 accepts 0.55 as an output-floor multiplier, a value Article 92 does not contain
issues.requirement: OF 02.00 row 0035 column 0030 (output floor multiplier, metric boe_met:pi10061, a percentage filed as a fraction) must be exactly one of 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.725. Label: 'Output Floor multiplier should be limited to 55, 60, 65, 70, 72.5'.

authority.locator: PRA Rulebook instrument PRA2026/1  - Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part, Article 92(2A)
authority.quote: TREA = max {U-TREA; x ∙ S-TREA + OF-ADJ}

authority.locator: PRA Rulebook instrument PRA2026/1  - Article 92(2A), definitions

authority.quote: When calculating TREA for the purposes of paragraph 2A(a), an institution or CRR consolidation entity may apply the following factor x during the periods specified below: (a) 60% during the period from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2027; (b) 65% during the period from 1 January 2028 to 31 December 2028; (c) 70% during the period from 1 January 2029 to 31 December 2029.

authority.locator: PS1/26 Annex II reporting instructions  - OF 02.00 row 0035
authority.quote: Indicate the output floor multiplier applicable during the reporting period, as per Article 92 (5) of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: It cannot. The four values the rules allow - 60%, 65%, 70% (Article 92(5), optional, by year) and 72.5% (Article 92(2A)) - are all accepted; an entity outside the floor reports nothing and the rule does not run (tested: not evaluated). The defect is only that 0.55 is also accepted: a search of the Required Level of Own Funds Part (pp.11-16) finds 72.5% on p.13 and 60%, 65%, 70% on p.15 and no 55% anywhere. The rule is also not date-aware (0.60 would be accepted in 2030), which is likewise permissive.

example.description: A firm reporting for 2027 files multiplier 0.60: satisfied. A firm that wrongly files 0.55: also satisfied (ERROR-severity rule lets it through). 0.50: unsatisfied.

issues.alternatives_considered: Not applicable - no correct return is rejected, so there is nothing to work around.
issues.proposed_fix: Delete the first disjunct: ({t: OF02.00.01.01, r: 0035, c: 0030} = 0.60) or (... = 0.65) or (... = 0.70) or (... = 0.725), and change the label to '60, 65, 70, 72.5'. Low priority.
issues.eba_precedent: None; the rule is the Bank's own (no EBA equivalent recorded in the v4.0.0 workbook).
issues.reach: No firm is affected adversely. A firm that files 0.55 by mistake is not stopped.
issues.meanwhile: A pass of this rule is no evidence that the figure is one the rules permit: check it against the rules yourself.

issues.title: Bank rules that restate EBA rules the EBA has deactivated: 34 enforced rules, not 46, and deactivation alone does not mark a defect
issues.requirement: The claim under test: 46 live PRA001 rules restate EBA rules that the EBA deactivated and never reactivated, taken from a join of the Bank's v4.0.0 EBA-equivalent labels to the EBA rule list. Rebuilt here from the v4.0.0 extract, the raw EBA workbook (every release sheet, v2.0 to 3.5) and the v4.1.1 gateway rule book.

authority.quote: The EBA from time to time publishes information about Validation rules which should be disregarded (primarily due to being identified as potentially incorrect).
Validation rules to be disregarded are identified by the presence of a date in the "Deactivated" column.

Starting from version 2.3, rules may be reactivated, indicated by a date in the "Reactivated On" column. Note that rules are reactivated at the individual version level (whereas they are, as policy, deactivated for all simultaneously).

Additionally, institutions fulfilling the threshold set in Article 5(5) of the Reporting (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook shall submit information broken down by country regarding the domestic country as well as any non-domestic country.
An institution shall assign a 150% risk weight to exposures that are associated with particularly high risk.

An equity exposure shall be assigned a risk weight of 250%, unless the exposure is a higher risk equity exposure, in which case the treatment in paragraph 4 applies, or is within scope of paragraph 6, in which case the treatment referred to in paragraph 6 applies.

Exposures subject to rules 4.1 to 4.10 of the Credit Risk: General Provisions Part should be reported in this row during the transitional period if they qualify as an equity exposure as set out in Article 133(1) and (2) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.

For exposures subject to the Risk Weight Substitution Method, and for collateral recognised under the Financial Collateral Simple Method or the Other Funded Credit Protection Method, firms shall separate each exposure, prior to the application of conversion factors, into a covered part and an uncovered part in accordance with Article 235 of the Credit Risk Mitigation (CRR) Part and report each part separately.
Institutions shall include the sum of rows 0020, 0030 and 0060.
In OF CR IRB 1, "FIRB/slotting" in cases where the FIRB approach or the slotting approach is applied, and "AIRB" in cases where the AIRB approach is applied.

Indicate (with ‘Yes’ or ‘No’) if the output floor has been activated (i.e., when, in row 0010, the value in column 0030 is equal to or greater than the value in column 0010) calculated per as per Article 92 of the Required Level of Own Funds (CRR) Part of the PRA Rulebook.
Where there is a negative sign (-) preceding the label of an item, no positive figure is expected to be reported for that item.

issues.requirement: On each of 29 rows of OF 09.01 (every exposure class, every of-which row and the total) and on every country sheet, original exposure pre conversion factors (column 0010) must be at least the defaulted exposures (column 0020). A cell that is not reported is read as 0.

authority.quote: This column shall provide additional information about the obligor structure of defaulted exposures. Exposures classified as “exposures in default” as referred to in Article 112(1)(j) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part shall be reported where the obligors would have been reported if those exposures were not assigned to the exposure classes 'exposures in default'.

Original exposure pre-conversion factors for those exposures which have been classified as “exposures in default” and for defaulted exposures assigned to the exposure classes “exposures associated with particularly high risk” or “subordinated debt, equity and other own funds instruments”.
Same definition as for column 0010 of OF CR SA template
Article 112(1)(j) of the Credit Risk: Standardised Approach (CRR) Part.

issues.why_correct_return_fails: Under the Standardised Approach a defaulted exposure leaves its class: it is an Article 112(1)(j) exposure, so its original exposure goes in column 0010 of row 0100, not of the row for its obligor's class. Column 0020 is a memorandum that shows the same defaulted exposure against the row where its obligor 'would have been reported'. So on the class rows (0010 to 0095, 0120, 0160) column 0010 holds the non-defaulted exposures of the class and column 0020 holds the defaulted exposures of that kind of obligor. These are two separate populations, not a total and an of-which. Column 0020 is a subset of column 0010 only on rows 0110, 0140 to 0143 and 0150 (classes that keep their defaulted exposures) and on the total row 0170. The taxonomy agrees: row 0100 has no column 0020 cell. The rule therefore holds only where a row's performing book is at least as large as its defaulted book. It fails on any row, on any country sheet, where it is not. Example: the firm's only ADC loan (2,000,000) is in default. Row 0094 column 0010 is empty (read as 0) and column 0020 is 2,000,000, so 0 >= 2,000,000 is false. The Bank's own rules read column 0020 as the memorandum. boe_b0263 requires OF 07.00 sheet 0011 (exposures in default) r0010 c0010 = OF 09.01 r0170 c0020 less the defaulted amounts of rows 0110, 0150 and 0140, 'in accordance with exposure class hierarchy in Article 112'. boe_b0237 ties row 0100 column 0010 to the same sheet. Both pass on the return that fails boe_b0350. The label of boe_b0350 says 'IRB exposure class' on an SA template; its IRB siblings boe_b0348 and boe_b0349 are correct, because in OF 09.02 the defaulted columns are true subsets.

example.description: An SA firm below the country threshold (total sheet only). Regulatory residential real estate 10,000,000, performing, 20% risk weight (RWEA 2,000,000). One ADC loan of 2,000,000 in default, specific provisions 500,000 (25%, so 100% under Art. 127(1)(b)); exposure value 1,500,000, RWEA 1,500,000. No performing ADC lending. Annex II figures on OF 09.01 (all countries): r0091 c0010 10,000,000; r0090 c0010 10,000,000 and c0020 2,000,000; r0094 c0020 2,000,000 with c0010 not reported; r0100 c0010 2,000,000, c0055 500,000, c0075 1,500,000, c0090 1,500,000; r0170 c0010 12,000,000 and c0020 2,000,000. OF 07.00 c0010: sheet 0010 r0010 and r0330 10,000,000; sheet 0011 r0010 2,000,000; sheet 0001 r0010 12,000,000. A second return shows the same on a country sheet: corporates 3,000,000 performing in GB and one defaulted corporate of 500,000 in CY; the total sheet passes and the CY sheet fails on row 0070 (0 >= 500,000).

issues.alternatives_considered: 1. Also report the defaulted loan in row 0094 column 0010. boe_b0350 then passes (5/0) but boe_b0987 fails (0/1), because row 0094 column 0010 must equal OF 07.00 sheet 0010 r0360 c0010; and it contradicts Article 112(1)(j) and the row 0100 instruction. 2. Leave column 0020 empty on the class rows and report it only on the total. This contradicts the instruction that the amount 'shall be reported where the obligors would have been reported'. 3. Report an explicit 0 in row 0094 column 0010. The comparison is the same (0 >= 2,000,000). None of the three is both compliant and passing.
issues.proposed_fix: Restrict the scope of boe_b0350 to the rows where column 0020 is a subset of column 0010: scope({t: OF09.01.01.01, r: 0110;0140;0141;0142;0143;0150;0170}). Or withdraw it; boe_b0262 to boe_b0265 and boe_b0967 already tie column 0020 to OF 07.00. Correct the label, which refers to an 'IRB exposure class' on the SA template.
issues.eba_precedent: The EBA has no rule that compares C 09.01 column 0010 with column 0020. Its rules on column 0020 treat it as the memorandum: v8727_m ({C 07.00.a, r0010, c0010, s0011} = {C 09.01.b, r0170, c0020, x1} - {r0110, c0020} - {r0150, c0020}) and v6404_m are live in the 3.5 sheet. The Bank's v4.0.0 workbook labelled boe_b0350 (and boe_b0349) with v4786_m, which is C 09.02 {c0105} >= {c0110}: a different relation, deactivated by the EBA on 10 December 2020.
issues.reach: Any SA firm with a row, on the total sheet or on a country sheet, where the original exposure of defaulted obligors exceeds the performing original exposure of that class. Narrow of-which rows (ADC, specialised-lending sub-types, SME) and country sheets make this likely for firms that report by country. WARNING severity, so it does not block a submission.
issues.meanwhile: Report the figures the instructions require; do not change correct figures to satisfy the rule. A Warning-severity break does not stop the submission: explain it when you submit, citing this issue.
